item.title: kb: close the audit gaps
item.description:
Everything the 2026-09-25 audit of `cli/kb-cli`, kb-js, kb-mcp and the Knowledge extension found against `specs/index-api.md` and `specs/index-ui.md`, minus what the single-store change (no `~/.kb`) already fixed.

Ground rules agreed since:
- **One store per workspace**, `.kb/` found by walking up; nothing under `~` except the read-only model directory `~/.kb/models`.
- **kb holds what was read, not what is being written**: reference code yes, the workspace's own tree no (see the spec ticket).
- The spec was rebuilt from transcripts after the repo loss, so it may have drifted from the original design; check with the user when a ticket leans on a spec detail that looks off.

item.title: kb_get include:["links"] returns no links
item.description:
`kb get D-n --include links --json` emits `links: {outgoing, incoming}` (`cli/kb-cli/src/cmd_get.c`), but kb-js's `readDocumentRead` (`packages/kb-js/src/shape.ts`) never reads it and `KbDocumentRead` has no field for it. So `kb_get` with `include:["links"]` silently returns nothing.

**Done when:** `KbDocumentRead` carries `links?: { outgoing: KbLink[]; incoming: KbLink[] }` exactly when asked for, `readDocumentRead` reads it through the existing `readLink`, and a kb-js contract test against the real binary plus a kb-mcp test cover it.

item.title: Search hits omit scores.fused, and minScore filters raw BM25
item.description:
`cmd_search.c` computes the reciprocal-rank-fusion score (`fused[i].score`) but emits only `scores.bm25`, and its comment wrongly says only computed scores are emitted. `--min-score` is applied to raw BM25 inside `fts_search`, not to the fused score index-api §4 describes.

**Done when:** every hit carries `scores.fused`; `scores.vector` stays absent until semantic search exists (T in M-3); `minScore` is defined (and documented) against the fused score, or the spec says otherwise; e2e covers both.

item.title: Knowledge: a document's Refresh button runs a store-wide report
item.description:
The stale badge's refresh action in the document header (`webview/Document.tsx`) sends `{document}`; `src/host.ts` drops it and runs `kb refresh` over the whole store, which only reports and fetches nothing, then silently reloads the tab.

index-ui §3.1 wants a per-document refresh. The honest options: (a) re-read the document's source when it is a file (the locator is its path) and re-file it with `kb add`, (b) for a URL source, re-fetch through the extension's existing `fetchPage`, (c) otherwise say plainly that there is nothing to refresh from. Needs the source route from M-2 only if we want the CLI to own it.

**Done when:** the button refreshes that document (or explains why it cannot), shows the outcome, and never runs a store-wide command.

item.title: Structured error details (§11), and unsupported_mime
item.description:
Errors are `{ok:false, error, message}`; the details §11 lists exist only as prose inside `message`: `collection_in_use` has no count, `store_locked` no pid, `index_stale` no structure name, `model_missing` no path. `unsupported_mime` is never raised (any `--mime` is accepted and unknown types fall back to text/plain).

**Done when:** errors carry a `details` object with §11's fields, `KbError` exposes it typed, Knowledge's collection-delete confirmation uses the count, and `kb add` refuses a mime the chunker cannot handle with `unsupported_mime`.

author: agent
body:
Fixed in lap session S3 (git `061a1bb`).

- `KbDocumentRead` gains `links?: { outgoing, incoming }`, present only when asked for; `readDocumentRead` reads it through the same `readLink` as `kb links` (kb-mcp needed no change: it already passed `links: true`).

item.title: Search hits omit scores.fused, and minScore filters raw BM25
item.description:
`cmd_search.c` computes the reciprocal-rank-fusion score (`fused[i].score`) but emits only `scores.bm25`, and its comment wrongly says only computed scores are emitted. `--min-score` is applied to raw BM25 inside `fts_search`, not to the fused score index-api §4 describes.

**Done when:** every hit carries `scores.fused`; `scores.vector` stays absent until semantic search exists (T-11); `minScore` is defined (and documented) against the fused score, or the spec says otherwise; e2e covers both.

author: agent
body:
Done in lap session S5 (git `6d4a5d0`).

- **`scores.fused`** is on every hit: the reciprocal-rank sum the list is ordered by (1/61 for the top hit of a single list). `vector` stays absent until the vector path runs.
- **`minScore`** stays a floor on the **bm25** score, applied **before** fusion — decided rather than changed. The fused score is 1/(k + rank): it says where a hit landed, not how well it matched (the best hit of a poor query scores the same as the best of a good one), so a floor on it would only be a second `k`. §4 and the code now say so.
- **e2e**: fused present on every hit, 1/61 at the top, hits in fused order; a floor between two hits' bm25 drops only the weaker, and fusion re-ranks the rest from the top. The old test asserted `fused` was absent — it encoded the bug.

Suites: C unit 2296, e2e 141, kb-js 102, kb-mcp 134 — all green; index-vscode 86/87 (only the known T-14 failure).

Left for T-11: kb-js reads an absent `scores.vector` as `0` (`readScores` in `shape.ts`), which blurs the absent-versus-zero distinction the CLI keeps. It only matters once vectors exist.

item.title: Knowledge: opening a search hit does not scroll to its heading in some documents

author: agent
body:
Done in lap session S7 (git `bac99b9`).

- **Headings:** the chunk's heading (kept *as written* by the chunker) is brought to the heading *as shown* before its id is made — markdown inline code, emphasis, strikethrough, links, escapes and entities; HTML entities through the HTML renderer's own decoder. Identifiers keep their underscores and stars (`io_uring_prep_recv`, `char *p`). The renderer side is untouched.
- **Code and plain text** are drawn with an anchor on every line; a hit lands on the line its span starts on, counted in **bytes** as spans are (multi-byte text tested). Copying plain text is still byte-identical.
- `revealId` in `src/view/headings.ts` is the one place that decides; the `window.__KB_CHUNKS__` global it replaced is gone.

**Checked end to end** beyond the unit tests: real `kb` chunks of a markdown, an HTML and a C document, rendered through the real `Body` component (server-side React), all 9 land on an element that exists — before, 4 of the 6 headings and all 3 code chunks would have stayed at the top.

index-vscode 96/97 (only T-14); combined build and check green. Not seen in a live VS Code window.

item.title: Forget a document or a source (DELETE /documents, /sources)

author: agent
body:
Done in lap session S8 (git `d395dc9`).

- **Log:** `documents.jsonl` gains a `forget` record. The fold drops the document; its id and chunk range stay spent (never reused), links to it read `resolved: false`, and its blob waits for `kb compact`.
- **`kb forget D-n`** forgets one document; **`kb forget S-n`** a source with every document under it. One path (`forget_records`): documents first, then sources, then the keyword index rebuilt, all under one lock.
- **`kb collections delete <name> --with-documents`** forgets what the topic holds. Without the flag it still refuses with `collection_in_use` (now naming the flag) — forgetting a topic's contents is asked for by name. `rename --with-documents` is refused.
- **kb-js:** `forget(id)` → `{documents, sources, note}`, `deleteCollection(name, { withDocuments })`. Not an MCP tool (§9).
- **Knowledge:** a collection's Forget now forgets its documents, as its confirmation already promised, instead of being refused.

**Found and fixed on the way (pre-existing):** kb-js appended `--json` after a `--` separator, where kb read it as a positional — so **renaming or deleting a collection** from Knowledge and **searching for a dash-led query** (from Knowledge or agents) got a text answer kb-js could not parse. `--json` now goes in front of `--`.

Tests: C unit 2312, e2e 148 (7 new forget tests), kb-js 105 (forget and the collection delete against the real binary, the `--json` placement, key coverage for `forget`), kb-mcp 134, index-vscode 96/97 (only T-14), combined check green. Spec §7 notes the default refusal.

item.title: Forget a document or a source (DELETE /documents, /sources)
Source routes: sources list/show/refresh, and file ingest

author: agent
body:
Done in lap session S9 (git `868092e`).

- **`kb sources [--collection C] [--kind K]`** lists sources; **`kb sources show S-n`** gives the source, its documents, and their **fetch history** (every `document` and `touch` record, oldest first — the fold only keeps the latest, so `doclog_fetches` reads them back).
- **`kb refresh S-n`** reads a **file** source again and re-indexes it only if the text changed (same document id, fresh chunk range). A **url** source is refused with `fetch_failed` (no HTTP client, §12.2 — re-file with `kb add --url`), an **inline** one with `usage` (nothing to read again). `kb refresh` without an id is still §5's report; mixing the two is refused.
- **`refile_document`** is now the one path by which an existing document is handed its text again — `kb add` and `kb refresh S-n` share it (a behaviour-preserving extraction; the whole suite passed before anything was added on top).
- **File ingest by locator** already existed as `kb add --file`; no directory walk, by design (T-12).
- **kb-js:** `sources()`, `source(id)`, `refreshSource(id)`; the key-coverage test checks `sources show` and each `sources` row against what the binary prints.
- **Knowledge:** the `kb:/S-n` page now reads `kb sources show`: kind, locator, last fetch, the documents, the fetch history newest first, and a Refresh action for file sources. Checked rendered in headless Chrome.

Tests: C unit 2312, e2e 153 (5 new), kb-js 107, kb-mcp 134, index-vscode 96/97 (only T-14), combined check green.

item.title: Source routes: sources list/show/refresh, and file ingest
Batch ingest in one transaction, without a full index rebuild per add
item.description:
index-api §2's `POST /documents/batch` ("many at once, one transaction") does not exist. kb-mcp's `kb_add` takes a `documents[]` array but files them one `kb add` at a time, stopping at the first failure, and every `kb add` rebuilds the whole keyword index.

**Done when:** `kb add --batch` reads JSONL on stdin and files every document under one lock with one index rebuild (all or nothing); kb-js `addBatch`; `kb_add` uses it; e2e shows a failing document leaves the store unchanged.

author: agent
body:
Done in lap session S10 (git `e80b134`).

- `kb add` is split into **prepare** (kind, locator, mime, hash — refusable before any lock) and **ingest** (write one prepared document), so the single and the batch path are one path. The full suite passed on the restructure before batch was added.
- **`kb add --batch`** reads one JSON object a line on stdin (title, collection, content; url, mime, meta optional). Every line is prepared before the store opens, so a bad line — or non-JSON, or an empty batch — **files nothing** and names its line. Then all are filed under one lock with **one index rebuild**. The same locator twice in a batch is one document.
- **kb-js:** `addBatch(documents)`; `readAdded` shared with `add`.
- **kb-mcp:** `kb_add` is one batch call; a refusal returns `filed: 0` and says none were filed. Its description tells agents so. The guard now also forbids `forget` and `refreshSource` from the tools.

Tests: e2e 156 (3 new: batch filed together, same locator once, bad line leaves the log byte-identical), kb-js 109, kb-mcp 134 (three add tests rewritten for batch semantics), index-vscode 96/97, combined check green.

lap note: the restructure of `cmd_add.c` came out as 30 fragments and kb-mcp's rewritten tests as 11; they share numbered messages saying what the whole change is, since lap's diff cannot follow a moved function.

item.title: Structured error details (§11), and unsupported_mime
item.description:
Errors are `{ok:false, error, message}`; the details §11 lists exist only as prose inside `message`: `collection_in_use` has no count, `store_locked` no pid, `index_stale` no structure name, `model_missing` no path. `unsupported_mime` is never raised (any `--mime` is accepted and unknown types fall back to text/plain).

author: agent
body:
Done in lap session S11 (git `a863dd9`).

- **CLI:** errors are `{ok:false, error, message, details?}`. A small `errdet` module holds one pending details object per process, **owned by a code**, so details recorded by a lower layer (the lock in `store_open`, staleness in `fts_open_store`) print only under that code and never ride on an unrelated error.
  - `store_locked` → `{store, pid}`
  - `collection_in_use` → `{collection, documents}`
  - `index_stale` → `{structures: ["keyword"], path}` / `{structures: ["chunks"], document}`; `kb status` carries it inline
  - `fetch_failed` → `{locator}`
  - `unsupported_mime` → `{mime}`: `kb add` (single and batch) now refuses anything not `text/*` or a text-like `application/*` (JSON, XML, YAML, TOML, JS, TS, shell, XHTML), before the store is opened.
  - `model_missing`'s `path` lands with T-10, when the embedder is actually built.
- **kb-js:** `KbError.details` (raw) and `detailsOf(code)`, typed per code in `KbErrorDetails` and shape-checked, so a mis-shaped object reads as null rather than a lie.
- **kb-mcp:** refusals pass `details` to the agent.
- **Knowledge:** delete asks the store first; an empty collection just goes, and one that holds documents is confirmed with the **store's** count from `collection_in_use` — not the row's count from the last refresh.
- **Spec §11** names the fields.

Tests: unit 2319, e2e 158, kb-js 110, kb-mcp 135, index-vscode 96/97 (T-14).

author: agent
body:
Done in lap session S12 (git `09bf272`). All seven:

- [x] **Source etag/status.** `kb add --etag` (and batch `etag`) records the ETag the caller's fetch saw; a source's `etag` is its newest document's, cleared when new text arrives without one. `status` is recorded: a refresh that cannot read the file marks it `fetch_failed` (once), and the next successful filing sets it back to `ok`. `kb sources --status S --q text`.
- [x] **Meta filter.** `ls`/`search --meta '{"year":2024}'`: every key must match, and an array value matches any element. It uses the same shape as `add --meta`.
- [x] **ls q + collection list.** `--q` is a case-insensitive substring of the title or locator; `--collection a,b`. `ls` and `search` now share one `DocQuery`.
- [x] **Piped Markdown.** With no `--mime` and no extension, the text is sniffed. HTML is recognised when it says so on its first line; Markdown when it opens with a heading or has two section headings. A stray `# comment` stays plain text.
- [x] **Re-filing drops title/meta.** The same text split the same way still re-indexes nothing, but a new title, meta or etag is now written as a whole record over the same chunks. Meta that is not given is kept.
- [x] **`--since`.** It takes a date or a kb timestamp and compares instants; anything else is `usage` (e.g. `2026-9-1` was silently wrong before).
- [x] **Browse cap.** The sidebar asks for 201. When the list is cut it says so and offers **Show all**, which reloads with no limit.

Tests: e2e 165 (7 new), unit 2319, kb-js 111 (one test had encoded the old plain-text behaviour and was updated), kb-mcp 135, index-vscode 97/98 (T-14).

item.title: Spec: kb indexes reference material, not the workspace's own code

author: agent
body:
Done in lap session S13 (git `07cdcd8`).

- The spec's opening now says kb holds what was **read** (docs, papers, reference source at a pinned version), never the code being **written**, and why: that code is stale as soon as it is indexed, and grep and the LSP already answer it.
- `kind: dir` is gone from §1.2 and from the kb-js `SourceKind` type. `POST /sources` reads one file at a time, and the spec gives the reason: a walk pointed at `.` would index the workspace.
- §12.2 is marked **decided**: the binary fetches nothing. Whoever fetched a page files it through `POST /documents`, with its `etag`. Refreshing a `url` source is the caller's job; the CLI refuses it with `fetch_failed`.

item.title: Register the MCP servers with Claude Code once per machine, and keep them current

author: agent
body:
Done in lap session S17 (git `e1af625`).

- **Syntax verified** from the installed CLI: `claude mcp add-json [--scope user] <name> <json>` and `claude mcp remove --scope user <name>`. `add-json` refuses an existing name, so each server is removed first.
- **New command:** *procode: Register MCP Servers with Claude Code (All Projects)*. The old one is renamed *…(This Project's .mcp.json)* and kept.
- **On start:**
  - If the `claude` CLI is found and nothing has been asked yet, procode offers to register **once**; *No thanks* is remembered.
  - Once registered, the signature of what was registered is kept. When an update moves the extension folder, the two entries are silently re-registered; only a failure is shown.
  - The CLI is looked for on PATH, then in `~/.local/bin`, `~/.claude/local`, `/opt/homebrew/bin` and `/usr/local/bin`, because a VS Code started from the Dock doesn't inherit the login PATH.
- **Without the CLI**, the command copies the two ready `claude mcp add-json …` lines to the clipboard, shell-quoted.
- **`COBOARD_AUTHOR=claude`** is set on the coboard entry for Claude Code, at both user and project scope, so board comments stop being signed "agent". VS Code's own agent keeps the default.
- **check.mjs** puts a stand-in `claude` on PATH that records its arguments, so the check never touches the real configuration. It covers:
  - a stale registration: remove + add-json for both servers, with the installed script, the bundled kb and the author;
  - a current registration: nothing is run;
  - a declined offer: nothing is run;
  - quoting of the clipboard line.

**Not verified by experiment:** that user-scope stdio servers start in the project directory. That would mean registering a throwaway server in the user's real Claude config. It is the same spawn path as project scope, which finds this repository's `.coboard/` today. To use this: `npm run package --workspace combined`, reinstall the vsix, and accept the offer. Then this repo's `.mcp.json` can be deleted.

item.title: Wire the embedder into the build and record the model
Store and scan vectors, and make hybrid the default

author: agent
body:
Done in lap session S19 (git `3bd227d`).

- **`index/vectors.bin`**: one int8 vector per chunk, keyed by **chunk id**, with the model fingerprint. Chunk ids name one passage forever, so a stored vector stays right as long as the model does:
  - `kb add` and `kb rebuild` embed only chunks with no vector, and drop vectors whose chunks are gone;
  - `kb reindex` re-embeds everything;
  - `rebuild` reports `vectors: {kept, embedded, dropped}`; `reindex` reports the real `reembedded` count.
- **Speed:** a 375-token chunk took **7.3 s**. Two changes brought it to **0.58 s**:
  - `quant_matmul` dequantises each super-block once per sequence instead of once per token (3.6 s);
  - `plat_parallel` (pthreads / Win32) runs the matmul rows and the attention heads on every core.
  - A query takes about 16 ms to embed and about 35 ms end to end.
  - The vectors are **bit-identical** to the old single-threaded pass (hashes compared on three texts), so the llama.cpp comparison still holds.
- **Search:**
  - The default is **hybrid** whenever the store's vectors cover it under the model on disk; otherwise it is keyword, and `mode` in the response says which ran.
  - `--mode hybrid|semantic` refuses with `model_missing`, `model_mismatch`, or `index_stale` on `["vectors"]` with `missing: n`.
  - Both lists go to depth max(3k, 50), then RRF. A chunk found by both paths is one candidate with `matched: ["keyword","semantic"]`.
  - `scores.bm25` and `scores.vector` appear only for the paths that found the hit.
  - Text output shows kw / sem / kw+sem.
- **`kb status`** adds `index.vectors: {count, missing, current}`.
- **kb-js:** `KbScores.bm25` and `.vector` are optional, and `readScores` keeps an absent score absent (the comment on this ticket). One test had pinned the old zeros; it now pins absence.
- **e2e:** `make e2e` picks up the `.gguf` in the real `~/.kb/models` automatically (or `KB_TEST_MODEL`) and skips the model tests without one.
  - The model tests cover: hybrid by default with both scores; semantic ranking the bread note first for a query that shares no word with it; the collection filter; rebuild keeping and dropping vectors; and the missing-vector refusal, keyword fallback and re-embedding.

Tests: unit 2380, e2e 165 (171 with the model), kb-js 112, kb-mcp 135, index-vscode 98.

item.title: Spec: the .artifact/ format, the tokens an artifact may use, and the MCP tools

author: agent
body:
Done: `specs/artifacts.md` (lap session S20).

- **Layout:** `.artifact/A-<n>/index.html` + `artifact.json` (`id, title, description, createdAt, updatedAt`). `.artifact/` is found by walking up; ids are monotonic and never reused; writes are atomic, page first.
- **What a page may assume:** baukasten's `--bk-*` tokens bound to the theme (the spec lists the real names from `baukasten-vscode.css`) and a default stylesheet for plain elements. **What it cannot do:** use the network, or run scripts outside the sandbox.
- **MCP:** `artifact_publish {title, html, description?, id?}`, `artifact_list`, `artifact_get`. Refusals are `invalid`, `not_found` and `bad_id`. There is **no delete for agents**; deleting is a person's call in the editor.
- **Viewer:** a sandboxed frame with a CSP that allows no network, baukasten's stylesheet, the live `--vscode-*` values and the defaults, all injected before the page's own styles. Theme changes re-inject; republishing reloads.

author: agent
body:
Done in lap session S21.

`packages/artifacts` (npm workspace):
- **store.ts:**
  - `.artifact/` is found by walking up, or created at the git root.
  - Each artifact is `A-<n>/index.html` + `artifact.json`, written page first and each atomically.

item.title: artifacts-vscode: the list and the themed viewer

author: agent
body:
Done in lap session S22.

`packages/artifacts-vscode`:
- **List:** an Artifacts activity-bar view, newest update first. Each row shows the title and "3 h ago"; the tooltip has the description, id and dates. Rows are read fresh from the store, and a watcher on `**/.artifact/**` refreshes the list and **reloads any open tab** when an agent republishes.
- **Viewer:** one tab per artifact, titled after it.
  - `frame.ts` builds the frame document. Ahead of the page it injects a **CSP with no network**, `baukasten-vscode.css`, a slot for the live `--vscode-*` values, the default stylesheet `artifact.css` and a small theme bridge. `artifact.css` sits in a CSS layer, so anything a page writes wins.
  - The webview fills the slot before first paint, loads the frame with `sandbox="allow-scripts"` only (no same-origin, so no `acquireVsCodeApi`), and pushes new variables to the bridge when the theme changes. It ignores every message whose source is the frame.
- **Commands:** Open, Open HTML Source, Refresh. Delete is only in the item's context menu, behind a modal confirm, and removes only a validated `A-<n>` directory.
- **Tests:** 7 for the pure parts: injection order, both policies, stylesheets that can't close their element, variable filtering, title escaping, list order and dates.
- **Headless Chrome:** a realistic artifact rendered in a mocked light and dark VS Code webview. Both themes read correctly, and a page script ran **inside the sandbox**. That proves the srcdoc frame works under the inherited webview policy, which is why the webview's CSP allows inline script.

Skill: the ticket workflow across the board, lap and git

item.title: Knowledge: Add URL — fetch a page in the editor and file it
item.description:
The CLI fetches nothing (index-api §12.2). Knowledge fetches the page in the extension host, extracts its readable text as Markdown or keeps the HTML, and files it with `kb add --url … --etag …`. The same path makes a url source's Refresh work.

**Done when** Add URL files a page with its etag, refresh re-fetches it (conditional on the etag), and failures are said plainly.

author: agent
body:
Done in lap session S32.

Knowledge already had **Add URL**. It asks before fetching, fetches in the extension host, and files the page as it arrived (HTML is rendered as prose at read time, so the stored bytes stay the page's own). What it lacked, and now has:
- **The ETag.** Add URL files it (`kb add --etag`), so the source records it.
- **Conditional refresh.** A document's Refresh sends `If-None-Match` with the recorded ETag. A **304** re-files the stored text, which only moves `fetchedAt`. A changed page is re-indexed and its new ETag recorded.
- **Url sources.** On a url source's page, Refresh now works: it goes through the same fetch in the extension, since the CLI still has no network, and the answer has the shape the page already shows.
- **Plain failures.** An unreachable host is named with its error code ("Could not reach 127.0.0.1:1: ECONNREFUSED."), and a non-2xx says the status and that **nothing was filed**.

**Test:** a local HTTP server that honours `If-None-Match`, run against the real kb binary. It covers fetch and ETag, an unchanged refresh (with the conditional header checked), a changed page with its new ETag, a 500 that changes nothing, and an unreachable host. index-vscode: 99 pass.

item.title: Knowledge: file a paper from its PDF
item.description:
Papers are a stated target (index-api §12.3). Extract a PDF's text outside the CLI and file it through `kb add` with the PDF's path as locator. Decide the extractor (a JS library in the extension, or an external tool) before building.

**Done when** a PDF can be added from the Collections view and its text is searchable.

author: agent
body:
Done in lap session S33.

**Extractor decided: pdf.js (`pdfjs-dist` 6.3, Apache-2.0).** It is pure JavaScript, so there's nothing for the user to install and the vsix stays universal. An external tool like `pdftotext` would be one more thing to set up. It ships as its minified module and worker (1.8 MB) **beside** the bundle and is loaded with a real dynamic import, because it is ES modules that load their worker by relative path. The vsix is now 1.06 MB. Knowledge's dependency guard test names it with the reason, rather than being loosened.

- **Add Files** accepts PDFs. The text is filed as **Markdown**:
  - a `#` title (the PDF's own, or the file name) and its author;
  - one **`## Page N` section per page**, so the heading chunker splits on pages and **a search hit says which page it's on**;
  - lines and paragraphs rebuilt from baselines;
  - prose that would read as Markdown structure escaped.

  The locator is the PDF's path, and the meta records its page count and author.
- **Refresh** on a PDF document reads the file again and re-extracts it.
- **Tests:** 3 new, 102 in total. One takes a hand-built two-page PDF through pdf.js and the real kb binary: search finds page-2 text with heading "Page 2". That test also caught a paragraph-detection bug (upper median of gaps), which is fixed.
- **Checked the packaged vsix:** its pdf.js extracts text without the optional canvas module. The canvas warnings only concern rendering pages as images and will appear in the extension log.

Not done: scanned PDFs (images with no text layer) produce empty pages, because that would need OCR.

item.title: Board: archive
item.description:
Epics, milestones and tickets can be **archived**: hidden from lists, search, the sidebar and Kanban by default, and still readable by id. Archiving is reversible, and agents may do it (they still never delete).

**Design:**
- **Storage:** new `archive` / `unarchive` records in the same `.coboard/log.jsonl`, not a field on the item and not a second file.
  - Old readers ignore the new records, and an old writer's whole-item `put` cannot silently un-archive.
  - One file keeps a write atomic under the one lock, and keeps archived ids reserved so they are never reused.
- **Scope:** an item is hidden when it or anything above it (milestone, epic) is archived. Nothing is written to the children, so unarchiving the epic brings everything back.
- **Compatibility:** every existing API and MCP tool keeps its shape. New parameters are optional, the default excludes archived items (which changes nothing until something is archived), and archiving itself is new tools on top.

body:
Done in lap session S40, git 467d5aa.

- **Log:** `{"op":"archive"|"unarchive","id","at"}`, kept by the fold apart from the items. A `put` never carries the archive (`stored()` strips it), so neither an update nor an older coboard's whole-item put can drop one.
- **Inheritance:** an item reads as `archived: { at, via }`. `via` is `null` when it was archived itself, or else the milestone or epic it is archived with. Archiving an epic appends one record; unarchiving it brings back everything under it. An item archived itself stays archived when its epic comes back.

- **Ids:** archived ids stay taken.
- **Compatibility:** the current loader skips records it doesn't know (older loaders already did), and a test pins that. Nothing uses archiving yet: T-40 (MCP) and T-41 (UI) wire it in.

item.title: Board UI: archive, unarchive, and an Include archived filter
Board: archive
item.description:
Epics, milestones and tickets can be **archived**: hidden from lists, search, the sidebar and Kanban by default, and still readable by id. Archiving is reversible, and agents may do it (they still never delete).

**Design:**
- **Storage:** new `archive` / `unarchive` records in the same `.coboard/log.jsonl`, not a field on the item and not a second file.
  - Old readers ignore the new records, and an old writer's whole-item `put` cannot silently un-archive.
  - One file keeps a write atomic under the one lock, and keeps archived ids reserved so they are never reused.
- **Scope:** an item is hidden when it or anything above it (milestone, epic) is archived. Nothing is written to the children, so unarchiving the epic brings everything back.
- **Compatibility:** every existing API and MCP tool keeps its shape. New parameters are optional, the default excludes archived items (which changes nothing until something is archived), and archiving itself is new tools on top.

author: claude
body:
A real case from filing the demo workspace's knowledge base (2026-09-26, `.playground`, nomic Q4_K_M, this Mac):

- 13 Markdown documents (164 KB, 142 chunks) filed in about a minute in all.
- **One HTML page took about 13 minutes:** artifact A-1 (33 KB, 28 chunks), which is mostly inline SVG path data (`M12 13.125 A2.25 2.25 0 1 1 …`) and a long line of script JSON. A stack sample showed all the time in `embed_tokens → forward → quant_matmul`: the chunker's size estimate is far below what WordPiece makes of numbers and path syntax, so each chunk runs near the model's token limit.
- The same sample showed about **160 threads** alive, which suggests `plat_parallel` starts a new pool per matmul. That's worth checking for T-45 as well.
- For this ticket: HTML that is mostly markup or data (SVG, scripts) should be neither embedded nor chunked as prose. Stripping `<svg>`/`<script>` before chunking would likely remove most of the cost.

A first number for the benchmark: with the model installed, **hybrid search over 170 chunks takes 0.22–0.31 s per query** end to end (process start, model map, query embedding, search), measured with four queries in `.playground` on 2026-09-26. That doesn't argue for a long-lived process at this size. T-42 should confirm at 1k and 10k chunks.

author: claude
body:
Fixed in lap session S50, git 3cef96a. Nothing under `~` was written by the work or its tests; `~/.kb` still holds only `models/`.

- **Discovery** (`store_is_store`): a `.kb` directory is a store only when it holds `documents.jsonl`. `store_create` has written that since the start, so every real store still qualifies. **The home directory's `.kb` never qualifies**, even with logs planted in it, so the store the bug wrote is not adopted either. Both are walked past, like a plain file named `.kb`. HOME and the directory are compared through `realpath` (new `plat_realpath`), because `HOME` can be a symlink.
- **`kb init` in the home directory** is refused with `init_failed` ("the home directory holds kb's models, not a store").
- **No implicit store:** `kb add` under the home directory, outside any workspace store, answers `not_found` and writes nothing.
- **§1.4** says all of this in words.
- **Tests:**
  - kb unit 2395/2395, with a home of its own under TMPDIR: models-only `.kb`, planted logs, a workspace store under home, a stray `.kb`.

Once a model sat in `~/.kb/models`, two kb-js tests and one kb-mcp test failed because of it. item.description: **Done when** kb tokenizes exactly as the reference does: ids, specials and truncation. It is checked on the fixtures and on every file of this repository (docs and code), with zero mismatches. The old WordPiece tokenizer stays for as long as stores embedded with nomic exist.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S52, git 09eaadf.

- **`src/bpe.c`:**
  - NFC through vendored **utf8proc v2.10.0** (MIT, Unicode 16; `src/third_party/utf8proc`, with its tag, commit and license). Invalid UTF-8 becomes U+FFFD first.
  - The 116 **added tokens are split out first**, leftmost-longest, including the 2–24-space runs that code indentation becomes.
  - The GPT-2 split as a hand-written scanner, with the alternatives in order, `\s` as Oniguruma's Unicode White_Space, and categories from utf8proc.
  - GPT-2's byte alphabet, then merges by rank, with every occurrence of a pair merged left to right.
  - `[CLS] a [SEP]` and pairs `[CLS] q [SEP] p [SEP]`, with the passage cut first.
- **Exact:** kb's ids equal the Hugging Face tokenizer's on **651/651 files, 3,350,148 tokens**:
  - every tracked text file in this repository (docs, C, TypeScript, CSS, JSON, shell, Python);
  - `.lap/log.jsonl` (3.7 MB) and utf8proc's 2.3 MB data file;
  - 327 adversarial cases: NFC compositions, exotic whitespace (NBSP, U+2028, ideographic space), emoji ZWJ and flags, contractions in both cases, non-Latin digits, space runs of 25+, tabs mixed with spaces, placeholders and specials, control characters, and 300 random Unicode strings.
- **Bounded:** when the output will be truncated, only as much of a giant piece as could be kept is merged. A 1 MB piece at a 512-token budget finishes well under the 2 s the test allows. Text that is not truncated is unaffected.
- **Speed:** 6 MB tokenized in 0.33 s, model load included.
- **Absent bytes:** the vocabulary lacks the byte tokens that never occur in UTF-8 (0xC0, 0xC1, 0xF5+); they are allowed to be absent.
- **Tests:** `test_bpe.c` checks the fixture's texts and pairs id for id, truncation keeping `[CLS]`/`[SEP]`, the pair cut, and the time bound. It reads the model's vocabulary via `KB_TEST_MODERNBERT` (read-only) and skips without it.
  - kb unit 2515/2515, e2e 177/177.
  - `bin/kb-bpe-dump` and `tools/modernbert/check_tokenizer.py` rerun the whole-corpus check.
- **Size:** the binary grew from 227 KB to 596 KB, mostly utf8proc's tables. The Makefile pins e2e's model to the nomic file until the switch (T-56).

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S53.

- **Forward pass is exact.** Every fixture text matches the reference at cosine 1.000000. The first run disagreed on 3 of 11 texts (0.97–0.997). The C code was already equal to Hugging Face's `AutoModel`. The difference came from sentence-transformers, which applies `str.strip()` to each text before tokenizing, so the reference embeddings are of stripped text. kb now strips the same way (`bpe_strip`). MODERNBERT.md records this.
- **Speed.** F16 matrices had used one single-threaded matvec per token, about 100 s for 600 tokens. They now reuse each widened row across all tokens, in parallel. The test suite went from 104 s to 1.9 s. A reindex of 33 chunks takes about 15 s. The rest of the speed work is T-58.
- **Default model.** gte-modernbert-base is the default.
  - Reranker files are skipped when choosing the model.
  - When there are several embedders and none is the default, kb refuses.
  - A nomic store reports `model_mismatch` until `kb reindex` (e2e covers this).
  - `kb status` now prints the model finder's own reason instead of "no model in …".
- **Docs.** Spec §8 and the README are updated.
- **Tests.** Unit 2559/2559, e2e 179/179, kb-js 115/115, kb-mcp 135/135.

item.title: ModernBERT: the forward pass and gte-modernbert-base as kb's embedder
Code: file a whole folder, incrementally

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S54. Commits: 28da2a6 (CLI) and 84f59b9 (kb-js, MCP, Knowledge view).

- **`kb add --dir D --collection C [--no-forget]`** files a folder as one `dir` source, with one document per file at its `path`. Spec §2.1 describes it.
  - It reads the folder the way git does: nested `.gitignore` files with git's full rules (negation, anchoring, dir-only, `**`), from the repository root down, plus `.git/info/exclude`. The rules were checked against `git check-ignore`.
  - It skips hidden files, vendored directories, generated files (lock files, `.min.js`, generated protobuf code, `@generated` or DO NOT EDIT markers), binary and empty files, and anything over 1 MiB (JSON over 64 KiB).
  - Running it again is incremental: unchanged files are touched, changed files get a new version under the same id, new files become new documents, and gone files are forgotten. With `--no-forget` gone files are listed as `missing` instead.
  - `kb refresh S-n` on a dir source walks the folder again.
- **MCP:** `kb_add` takes `dir` + `collection` and always runs with `--no-forget` (§9).
- **Knowledge view:** an Add Folder… action. Refresh also works on folder sources and on single documents inside a folder.
- **Tests:**
  - C: unit 2623/2623, e2e 185/185.
  - Packages: kb-js 118/118, kb-mcp 141/141, index-vscode 110/110.
- **Demo store (`.playground`):**
  - reindexed under gte-modernbert-base;
  - filed its own tree (4 files);
  - filed `cli/kb-cli` (93 files, 2575 chunks).
- **Speed:** the first filing of kb-cli took 8 m 52 s, almost all of it embedding; T-58 covers this. A re-run with no changes takes 14 ms.
- **Open:** kb-js `refreshSource` still reads a dir source's answer as the single-file shape. The view goes around it by calling `addDir` directly.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S56, commit 25d7dc6.

**Measured:** `kb-embed-bench` on 48 chunks of about 530 tokens each, from the pinned corpus:

| step | gte ms/chunk | |
|---|---|---|
| before | 940 | |
| persistent thread pool with ranges handed out on demand; per-token work (norms, RoPE, GeGLU, residuals) on the pool | 732 | 1.3× |
| 4×4 register-blocked matrix kernel (16 multiply-adds per 8 loads) | 310 | 3.0× |
| rows widened once, whole; each output written once | 268 | 3.5× |
| attention split by head × 32-token block instead of 12 units | 243 | 3.9× |
| NEON for the attention inner loops (q·k, p·v) | 214–226 | ~4.2× |

- nomic (Q4_K) goes through the same kernel: 935 → 274 ms per chunk (3.4×).
- **End to end:** the benchmark's gte build takes 237 s for the 3,119 code chunks (was 909 s, 3.8×) and 13 s for the docs (was 52 s). kb now runs at about 1,000% CPU.
- **Same results:**
  - Vectors differ from the old build by at most 4.8e-7; the change is only the order in which sums are added.
  - The ModernBERT reference test still passes at cosine 1.000000.
  - The rebuilt benchmark gives identical ranks for all 262 queries.
- **Portability:** every SIMD path sits behind `(__ARM_NEON || __ARM_NEON__) && !KB_NO_SIMD`. `make SIMD=0` builds the portable C loops on ARM, and the unit tests (including the reference test) pass that way too. x86 has no intrinsics yet and runs the portable path, at about 1.4 s per chunk.
- **Tests:** unit 2623/2623, e2e 185/185.
- **Not done:** batching several chunks into one forward pass. With the pool, the remaining idle time is small, so I left it out. Worth revisiting only if profiles show sync overhead again.
- **Follow-up to decide:** x86 kernels (SSE2 baseline, AVX2+FMA+F16C chosen at runtime), which could be tested here under Rosetta 2.

author: claude
body:
x86 now gets the same speed-ups: lap session S57, commit 53a08bf.

- **`src/simd.h`:** a four-lane layer, NEON on AArch64 and SSE2 on x86-64. Both are guaranteed by their targets, so no CPU check is needed and no machine can meet an instruction it lacks. `dot256`, the 4×4 matrix kernel and the attention loops are written once against it. Anything else, or a build with `KB_NO_SIMD` (`make SIMD=0`), takes the plain C loops.
- **Tested here as x86_64 builds under Rosetta 2:**

  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | x86 SSE2 | 2623/2623 | cosine 1.000000 | largest difference 2.1e-7 | 474 |

  | x86, code before this ticket | | | | 1724 |

  That's a 3.6× speed-up on x86 under the same conditions, against 4.2× on ARM. Rosetta's absolute times don't reflect real x86 hardware.
- **ARM:** unchanged at 215 ms per chunk. Unit 2623/2623, e2e 185/185.
- **AVX2/FMA:** not added. Rosetta here stops at SSE4.2, so an AVX2 kernel couldn't be run on this machine, and I won't ship one that hasn't run. It needs a runtime CPU check and a real x86 machine or CI to test on.

item.title: Code: tree-sitter for C, TS/JS, Python, Go, Rust and Assembly

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S58, commit b4d150b.

- **Vendored and statically linked:** tree-sitter v0.25.10 plus grammars for C, TypeScript and TSX, JavaScript (with JSX), Python, Go, Rust and assembly. Assembly uses RubixDev/tree-sitter-asm: one grammar that reads GNU as (AT&T and Intel), NASM-style, ARM, RISC-V and MIPS.
  - Everything is MIT. Each grammar keeps its own LICENSE, and the runtime's ICU headers keep ICU's.
  - `src/third_party/TREE-SITTER.md` records the version, commit and files for each, the one local change (a copy of three identical headers for TypeScript's shared scanner), and how to update.
  - No runtime dependency.
- **Size:** about 35 MB of generated C, compiled once into `obj/` with warnings off (about 3 s in all) and linked into every binary. **kb's binary grows from 0.6 MB to 6.6 MB.** CMake lists the same sources.
- **Language from the extension (`syntax_lang`):**
  - C: `.c .h`
  - TypeScript: `.ts .mts .cts`; TSX: `.tsx`
  - JavaScript: `.js .mjs .cjs .jsx`
  - Python: `.py .pyi`
  - Go: `.go`; Rust: `.rs`
  - Assembly: `.s .S .asm .nasm`

  `.pyi` and `.nasm` also joined the mime table, so folder filing takes them.
- **`syntax_outline`:** parses with a 2 s budget, returns the root's nodes with byte spans, and counts bytes inside ERROR nodes and missing tokens. A file with errors still gets an outline.
- **Fallback rule, `syntax_usable`:**
  - An outline is used only when it exists and at most 10% of the file is error.
  - Otherwise the caller splits the file into line windows, so a parse error never fails a filing.
  - T-60 wires this into the chunker; this ticket leaves chunking unchanged, so the benchmark isn't moved.
- **Measured on the repository:** all 279 C/TS/TSX/JS/Python files parse well enough to split by the tree (three have 0.1% error). Parsing all of them takes 141 ms.
- **Measured on assembly:** six dialect samples (GAS AT&T, GAS Intel, NASM, ARM64, RISC-V, MIPS) all parse well enough, at 0–4% error, and function labels come out as `label` nodes.
- **Tests:**
  - unit 2673/2673 (50 new: extensions, one sample per grammar, four assembler dialects, the fallback);
  - e2e 185/185;
  - the CMake build is clean;
  - an x86_64 build under Rosetta passes the unit tests.
- **Dev tool:** `bin/kb-syntax-dump` shows how each file parses.

item.title: Code: tree-sitter for C, TS/JS, Python, Go, Rust and Assembly
Code: syntax-aware chunks with a path, container and signature header
item.description:
cAST's split-then-merge: whole definitions when they fit the budget, split along the tree when they do not, small siblings merged. Every chunk carries `path > container > signature` in the text it is embedded and indexed with.

**Done when** chunking is tested per language on real files from this repository and the benchmark records before and after.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S59, commit 26e867b.

**What kb does now:**
- **Split-then-merge (`syntax_cuts`):**
  - Siblings are grouped into units, with comments and attributes above a definition kept with it.
  - Units are merged while they fit 1,600 bytes.
  - A unit that doesn't fit is split along its children. A definition becomes the container; blocks and statements don't, so the path reads `fn > if (x) {`, not `fn > { > …`.
  - A small open chunk before a too-big unit goes into that unit's first piece, so a signature never stands alone.
  - A final pass merges pieces left over by a split.
  - Chunks tile the file from byte 0.
- **Headings:** `container > signature`, taken from the first definition-like node in the chunk. Definition-like is judged by whole words of the node type, so an assembler's `instruction` isn't taken for a `struct`.
- **Header line:** every code chunk is indexed and embedded under `title > heading` (the file, then the function) ahead of its text (`chunk_header`).
- **Choosing the grammar:** `doc_syntax` uses the document path, or the mime type for single files. TypeScript that won't parse is retried as TSX.
- **Fallback:** a file whose tree is more than 10% error is cut into line windows. Code without a grammar keeps the old line-based splitting.
- **Chunker version:** now `structural-2`, so stores built with structural-1 show "reindex owed".

**Tested per language on snapshots of real repository files** (`tests/fixtures/syntax/`): C (`gitignore.c`), TypeScript (`client.ts`), TSX (`Body.tsx`), JavaScript (`playground.mjs`) and Python (`convert.py`), plus Go, Rust and GNU-as fixtures.
- Every file is checked for tiling, size budget and headings.
- Named headings are checked, such as `export class Kb { > async addDir(...)`, `def main(): > …`, `impl<'a> Lexer<'a> { > fn ident(...)` and `kb_memchr:`.
- Unit 2857/2857, e2e 187/187.

**Benchmark, gte, before → after** (`results/gte-syntax-chunks.json`; * = the paired 95% interval excludes 0):

| code | hit@1 | hit@3 | MRR@10 |
|---|---|---|---|
| hybrid | 0.55 → **0.75*** | 0.85 → **0.92*** | 0.70 → **0.84*** |
| semantic | 0.42 → 0.62* | 0.62 → 0.83* | 0.54 → 0.73* |
| keyword | 0.47 → 0.53 | 0.75 → 0.80 | 0.63 → 0.69* |

- By tag (hybrid hit@1): identifier 0.66 → 0.89*, paraphrase 0.47 → 0.69*, purpose 0.53 → 0.67.
- Docs are unchanged apart from keyword noise from word statistics shared with the code (hybrid hit@3 0.80 → 0.83*).
- The code corpus makes 1,319 chunks instead of 3,119, and embedding time is about the same (218 s).

body:
Done. Commits b36ade9 (CLI), f281f68 (kb-js, MCP, Knowledge), 0792dfd (int8, depth 10).

- **Scoring:** `rerank_open` and `rerank_score` compute mean pooling, then dense → GELU → LayerNorm → logit.
  - Against the CrossEncoder reference the worst difference is 1.25e-3; four of the five pairs are within 5e-4.

  - Reranked hits carry `scores.rerank`.
  - Without the reranker file the search is refused with `model_missing`.
- **Clients:**
  - kb-js has `rerank` and `scores.rerank`;
  - MCP `kb_search` takes `rerank`;
  - Knowledge has the `knowledge.rerank` setting (default off).

**Benchmark** (results/gte-rerank.json, gte-all.json, gte-q8.json). hit@1 and p50 latency:

| | docs | code |
|---|---|---|
| hybrid | 0.76–0.77 (47 ms) | 0.80 (53 ms) |
| + rerank, top 20, float | 0.89 (2.25 s) | 0.83 (3.3 s) |
| + rerank, top 20, int8 | 0.89 (1.6 s) | 0.85 (2.4 s) |

author: claude
body:
Done in commit b36ade9.

- **Identifier splitting:** keyword search already keeps the whole identifier and adds its camelCase/snake_case parts (token.h). Path segments have been indexed through the title field since T-63.
- **Definitions** per file come from tree-sitter tag queries: name, kind, signature and doc comment (`syntax_symbols`).
  - The queries are upstream's tags.scm, split into patterns by `tools/gen_syntax_tags.py` and compiled into `src/syntax_tags.c`. A pattern a grammar rejects (JS patterns run against TS) is skipped rather than fatal.
  - Assembly uses its labels.
- **Keyword index:** a chunk's symbol names count 3 times (BM25F by repetition).
- **Metadata:** a filed folder's code files carry `{"language", "symbols": [{name, kind, line}]}` in `meta`, capped at 500 symbols (§2.1).
- **Benchmark** (results/gte-symbols-scorefusion-untuned.json, keyword mode so fusion doesn't blur it):
  - code keyword hit@1 0.55 → 0.58* (MRR +0.02*);
  - identifier-tag keyword hit@1 0.79 → 0.87, hit@3 0.92 → 0.95.

author: claude
body:
Done in commit b36ade9.

- **Hybrid search now fuses by score** (`score_fuse`):
  - each list's scores are min-max normalised, then combined as `a·vector' + (1−a)·bm25'`;
  - `a` = 0.60, or 0.30 for an identifier-shaped query (one word with `_`, an inner capital, a digit, `::`, `->`, `.`, `()`, or a leading dash);
  - RRF is kept as `--fusion rrf`.
- **Weights chosen by 5-fold cross-validation** (`bench/tune_fusion.py`): held-out hit@1 **0.774 vs 0.706 for RRF**, and every fold picked a(other) = 0.60.
- **"A confident semantic winner keeps rank 1"** is implemented as `KB_FUSION_LEAD`, but **turned off**: cross-validation tried leads from 0.02 to 0.10 and every one lowered hit@1, so the data rejected it.
- **Before → after, same store** (hybrid RRF → score fusion; results/gte-all.json):

  | | docs | code |
  |---|---|---|
  | hit@1 | 0.67 → **0.77** | 0.75 → **0.80** |
  | MRR | 0.78 → 0.85 | 0.84 → 0.87 |

  By tag (docs, hit@1): identifier 0.69 → 0.88, paraphrase 0.59 → 0.69, purpose 0.72 → 0.73.
- **Tests:** e2e covers fused scores and `--fusion rrf`.

author: claude
body:
Done in commit b36ade9 (chunker structural-4).

- **Not worth embedding:** chunks under 40% letters, or 400+ bytes with almost no whitespace (SVG path data, digit tables, minified or encoded text), get a keyword-only vector entry (scale 0). Semantic search skips them, and they don't count as missing (`chunk_embeddable`).
- **Tiny siblings:** runs of sibling sections each under 1/8 of the budget, under the same parent heading, share a chunk.
- **The 33 KB SVG page** (artifact A-1) now files in **8.9 s**, down from 13 minutes. That figure was measured with the benchmark running at the same time.
- **Benchmark:** no measurable change on this corpus (keyword and semantic identical, 138 → 137 doc chunks). It has no junk to skip, so this is the expected result.
- **"Sized by the model's real token count": not done as written.**
  - Chunking stays model-independent (bytes/4). A keyword-only store has no tokenizer, and chunk ids must not depend on the model file.
  - It does no harm: across the benchmark corpora no chunk hit gte's 1,024-token limit (`truncated` stays 0).
- **Side effect:** a PDF page under about 200 bytes now shares a chunk with the next page. The Knowledge PDF test fixture was given realistic page lengths.

author: claude
body:
Done. Commits 25d7dc6, 53a08bf, 0792dfd.

- **Quantised matmul (int8):**
  - Weights and activations are quantised per 32-value block (`Q8Matrix`, `q8_from`, `q8_matmul`).
  - There are four kernels, each tested with the full unit suite plus the reference tests:
    - dot-product instructions (4×4 register-blocked);
    - plain NEON;
    - SSE2 (x86_64 under Rosetta);
    - portable C (`KB_NO_SIMD`).
  - It's used for bulk embedding (filing, `kb embed`, rebuild, reindex) and the reranker. A search's single query stays in float. Converting the model takes about 35 ms.
- **Speed:** 204 → 151 ms per chunk on the timing tool. The benchmark's code corpus embeds in 151 s instead of 217 s.
- **Quality:** real text stays within cosine 0.9996 of float. The benchmark is unchanged: code hybrid 0.80 → 0.80, docs reranked 0.89 → 0.89 (results/gte-q8.json). The vector fingerprint marks int8, so float and int8 vectors are never mixed.
- **Batching:** measured, and worth at most about 8% at today's chunk sizes. Code chunks got larger after T-60 (about 1,200 bytes), which leaves even less to gain, so it wasn't built.
- **Reranker latency:**
  - p50 2.25 s → 0.87 s on docs, and 3.3 s → 1.27 s on code;
  - from int8 plus depth 10 instead of 20, with the same quality at both depths.
- **Earlier on this ticket:** thread pool, blocked F16 kernel, parallel attention (4.2×), and x86 via SSE2.

author: claude
claude
body:
Done in commit f281f68.

- **Layout algorithm:**
  - Above 300 nodes, a Barnes–Hut quadtree (theta 0.8) on typed arrays, deterministic.
  - At 300 nodes or fewer, the exact path gives the same positions, bit for bit, as the old `layout()`.
- **2,000 nodes with about 3 links each:** 18.1 s → **0.68 s** (5,000 nodes: about 2.0 s).

author: claude
body:
Done. `cli/kb-cli/bench/perf.py` (results/perf.json) and `KB_TIMING=1` phase timings in `kb search`.

- **Stores:** deterministic synthetic Markdown with the real model. The two sizes came out at 2.1k and 21k chunks.
- **Results** (float embedding; int8 now makes filing about 1.4× faster, T-58):

| | 2.1k chunks | 21k chunks |
|---|---|---|
| filing, keyword only | 0.8 s | 3.2 s |
| embedding | 150 s (14/s) | 1516 s (13.8/s) |
| add 1 doc of 21 chunks, embedded | 1.6 s | 1.6 s |
| add a batch of 20 docs, embedded | 6.1 s | 6.0 s |
| keyword search | 4.4 ms | 13.6 ms |
| hybrid search | 45 ms | 63 ms |
| hybrid + rerank (top 20, float) | 1.75 s | 1.77 s |
| full rebuild | 0.04 s | 0.19 s |

- **Hybrid split at 21k chunks:** embedding the query 26 ms, opening the model 17 ms, vector scan 6 ms, opening the store 5 ms, keyword search 3 ms, process start 4 ms.

author: claude
body:
**Closed as not needed**, on T-42's numbers.
- **Searches:** at 21k chunks a hybrid search takes 63 ms end to end (26 ms embedding the query, 17 ms opening the model). A dozen in a row is under a second, so a long-lived process or query cache isn't worth its complexity.

lap: intent and behavior, and commits that name each other
item.description:
A lap commit's single message becomes two required fields: **intent** (why the edit exists, shared by edits that serve one goal) and **behavior** (what this edit makes the code do, its own for every edit). `lap commit` refuses weak messages with simple word-overlap checks, prints the new commit's hash, and every command that takes a commit accepts a hash; a commit's text refers to another as `#<hash>`, which the UIs turn into links.

Why: one edit per commit is what makes large agent changes reviewable, but a single message invited the `(1/n) … (n/n)` pattern, where one reason was copied across fragments and each hunk stopped explaining itself. Splitting intent from behavior lets the shared part be shared honestly and makes each hunk say what it does.

**Decided**
- `-m` is removed outright; every command refuses flags it does not know (`unknown_flag`).
- Old commits keep `msg` forever; readers show it as the intent. No migration command.
- No relationship types: "needs" or "fixes" are just words next to a `#hash`.
- lap stays single-developer: no branches, logs are never merged.

**Out of scope:** branches, the GitLab/GitHub mirror, lap suggesting links by reading code.

**Cutover:** the CLI, both extensions and the skills land together; binaries older than v0.2 refuse a log holding v0.2 commits.

The draft spec is attached to the spec ticket.

item.title: lap: intent and behavior, and commits that name each other
item.description:
A lap commit's single message becomes two required fields: **intent** (why the edit exists, shared by edits that serve one goal) and **behavior** (what this edit makes the code do, its own for every edit). `lap commit` refuses weak messages with simple word-overlap checks, prints the new commit's hash, and every command that takes a commit accepts a hash; a commit's text refers to another as `#<hash>`, which the UIs turn into links.

Why: one edit per commit is what makes large agent changes reviewable, but a single message invited the `(1/n) … (n/n)` pattern, where one reason was copied across fragments and each hunk stopped explaining itself. Splitting intent from behavior lets the shared part be shared honestly and makes each hunk say what it does.

**Decided**
- `-m` is removed outright; every command refuses flags it does not know (`unknown_flag`).
- lap is unreleased: the spec changes in place, with no version bump and no compatibility rules. A commit without both `intent` and `behavior` is malformed; `msg`-only commits are not read.
- This repository's log is converted once, in place, by a throwaway script (not a lap command): each `msg` becomes the `intent` with its `(i/n) ` prefix stripped, and `behavior` is the fixed string `The data of this field is not present`. Ids are kept; the hash chain is recomputed.
- Grouping by intent (in `rr` and the board) is display only: every hunk stays its own commit.
- No relationship types: "needs" or "fixes" are just words next to a `#hash`.
- lap stays single-developer: no branches, logs are never merged.

**Out of scope:** branches, the GitLab/GitHub mirror, lap suggesting links by reading code.

**Cutover:** the CLI, both extensions and the skills land together, with the log converted at the same time; the installed lap cannot read a converted log.

Where the draft spec is: the first comment on T-66.

An epic or milestone is closed only from its tab's Status field; the sidebar's right-click menu has no way to do it, and nothing points at one whose tickets are all done (E-7, E-9 and M-6–M-9 stayed open after their last tickets closed).

- The row context menu gets **Close** on an open epic or milestone and **Reopen** on a done one (status `done` / `open`, the same update the Status field sends).
- Closing one that still has tickets not done asks first, naming how many.

**Done when:**
- the host test drives Close (with and without open tickets) and Reopen through the command, as the context menu passes it;
- the combined build check passes.

item.title: Knowledge: performance at scale
Knowledge: code indexing on a stronger model
item.description:
kb indexes source code as well as documents, on one model good at both, and finds the right section first at least 80% of the time on docs and code alike.

**Decided (2026-09-26, from artifact A-2):**
- **One embedder for docs and code:** gte-modernbert-base (149M, Apache-2.0; BEIR 55.2, CoIR 71.5). It replaces nomic-embed-text-v1.5, so there is one vector space.
- **Reranker:** gte-reranker-modernbert-base (150M, Apache-2.0), the same architecture and tokenizer. It sits behind a switch until the forward pass is fast.
- **Model files** go in `~/.kb/models`. The user allowed writing them there, and nothing else under `~`.
- **Reference:** a throwaway Python venv (transformers, sentence-transformers) checks the C tokenizer, forward pass and reranker.
- **Languages:** C, TypeScript/JavaScript, Python, Go, Rust, Assembly.

**Target:** hit@1 ≥ 0.80 on a benchmark of 150+ doc queries and 100+ code queries, with bootstrap intervals. The baseline is today's hit@1 0.63–0.67 on 30 doc queries.

item.title: procode: an extension icon
item.description:
The combined procode extension has no `icon`, so the Extensions view and its details page show the default placeholder.

- Draw candidates in the family's grammar (one 2px round stroke on 24×24, like lap, Board, Knowledge and Artifacts) and compare them on one artifact page: large, at the sizes VS Code shows (128, 42, 32, 16), in both themes.
- The user picks one; its SVG is the source, and `packages/combined/scripts/build.mjs` writes a 128×128 (or larger) PNG into `dist/` and sets `icon` in the generated manifest (VS Code does not accept SVG there).

**Done when:**
- the user has chosen;
- the packaged vsix carries the PNG and the Extensions view shows it.

item.title: lap: fast on large repositories
item.description:
lap on a real codebase: `/Users/praisethemoon/code/typec`, ~14,600 tracked files (≈230k lines of C, ≈376k lines of Type-C tests), every file baselined (14.5k commits, a 34 MB log, 6.6 MB gzipped).

Measured there on 2026-09-27: `log`, blame, `rr`, `verify` and `search --text` take 0.01–0.2 s; **`lap status` takes 3.75 s**, and agents run it before nearly every commit.

Goal: every command an agent runs in its commit loop stays well under a second at this size, without changing the log or any output.

item.title: lap status: skip unchanged files with a stat cache
lap: intent and behavior, and commits that name each other
item.description:
A lap commit's single message becomes two required fields: **intent** (why the edit exists, shared by edits that serve one goal) and **behavior** (what this edit makes the code do, its own for every edit). `lap commit` refuses weak messages with simple word-overlap checks, prints the new commit's hash, and every command that takes a commit accepts a hash; a commit's text refers to another as `#<hash>`, which the UIs turn into links.

Why: one edit per commit is what makes large agent changes reviewable, but a single message invited the `(1/n) … (n/n)` pattern, where one reason was copied across fragments and each hunk stopped explaining itself. Splitting intent from behavior lets the shared part be shared honestly and makes each hunk say what it does.

**Decided**
- `-m` is removed outright; every command refuses flags it does not know (`unknown_flag`).
- lap is unreleased: the spec changes in place, with no version bump and no compatibility rules. A commit without both `intent` and `behavior` is malformed; `msg`-only commits are not read.
- This repository's log is converted once, in place, by a throwaway script (not a lap command): each `msg` becomes the `intent` with its `(i/n) ` prefix stripped, and `behavior` is the fixed string `The data of this field is not present`. Ids are kept; the hash chain is recomputed.
- Grouping by intent (in `rr` and the board) is display only: every hunk stays its own commit.
- No relationship types: "needs" or "fixes" are just words next to a `#hash`.
- lap stays single-developer: no branches, logs are never merged.

**Out of scope:** branches, the GitLab/GitHub mirror, lap suggesting links by reading code.

**Cutover:** the CLI, both extensions and the skills land together, with the log converted at the same time; the installed lap cannot read a converted log.

Where the draft spec is: the first comment on T-66.

item.title: lap status: skip unchanged files with a stat cache

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S80 (L2740–L2780), git `df6154c`.

**Measured** on a byte-identical copy of typec (rsync -a, mtimes kept; 14,653 working files, 3 pending), nothing changed between runs:

| | cold | warm |
|---|---|---|
| before | 6.37 s | 1.39 / 1.44 s |
| after, first run (builds the cache) | — | 1.52 s |
| after | — | 0.43 / 0.36 / 0.35 s |

Output is byte-identical before and after. What remains (0.08 s user, 0.27 s sys) is the working-tree walk itself: readdir and one lstat per entry, about what `find` costs over the same tree.

**What changed**
- **Stat cache** `.lap/statcache` (new `statcache.c`): per tracked file last found clean, its size, mtime (ns where kept) and the index entry of its last commit (head). A walked tracked file whose stat and head match is not read. Keying on the head rather than on the shadow's stat means a commit invalidates the entry with no second stat.
- **No second stat:** `plat_walk` now hands each callback the lstat it already made (`PlatStat`; Windows fills it from the find data).
- **No shadow walk:** with an index, `status` merges the sorted walk against the index's live files (last commit not a delete); tracked files the walk did not see are the deletions. Without an index it walks the shadow store as before.
- **The reader exception** (spec): `status` writes the cache only when its entries changed, only under `plat_trylock` (non-blocking flock; one attempt on Windows), atomically (temp + rename), and only for files this run read and found clean.
- **Racy rule:** an entry is added only when the file's mtime is older than the run's start second.
- Spec: repository layout, cache contract (the exception named), and a Stat cache entry in the acceleration layer.

**Tests:** unit 1811/1811; e2e 89/89. New scenarios: entries only for settled clean files (a future-dated file is never cached); new bytes with the size and old mtime restored stay "clean" until the cache is deleted (which shows the file was not read); same-size and racy edits found; a commit's new head invalidates the entry; deletions found through the index and without it; no refresh while another process holds the lock (python3 holds it). The per-file cache-contract loop now deletes `statcache` too.

**Not verified:** the Windows paths (FILETIME conversion, `plat_trylock`) compile only in theory; no Windows build here. Measured on the copy, not in `/Users/praisethemoon/code/typec` itself, so nothing was written there.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S82 (L2781–L2792), git `74eec7a`.

- `lap commit … --dry-run` runs the same code as a commit up to the append: file and ignore checks, session gate, edit selection (`--edit`/`--lines`, `no_changes`, `multiple_edits`), the message checks against the session's previous behavior. Then it prints and stops.
- **A reader:** `repo_open(…, for_write = !dry)`, so no lock, no torn-tail cut, no `state.json` rewrite; counters are healed in memory, which is where the predicted id comes from.
- **Human:** `dry run, nothing written: would record L2 in S1`, then op, file, region (and `(forced)`), the intent and the behavior.
- **JSON:** `{"ok":true,"dry_run":true,"record":{…}}`, the record as `rec_encode` would write it with its `prev` removed, so no hash either.
- Spec (`lap commit` section), help, and the lap skill (both copies) document it.
- **Tests:** e2e 90/90. The new scenario checks: human and JSON output; no `prev`/`hash`; `message_too_short`, `behavior_repeats_intent`, `unknown_file`, `no_changes`, `multiple_edits`, `behavior_repeats_previous`; every file under `.lap/` byte-identical before and after (shasum); the predicted id equals the id the real commit then gets; with `state.json` removed and a torn tail appended, the dry run still predicts correctly and leaves both as they were.

Correction to the session id above: it is S81, not S82.

item.title: Lap History: group a session's commits by intent, behavior on each row
item.description:
Today each commit row shows `L14565 9091b3d <intent> <file> · lines …` and expands to two lines, `Intent: …` and `Behavior: …`. The intent then appears twice per commit, and again on every commit that shares it (three identical intents in a row for S3 on typec). The expansion adds only the behavior.

Tree shape instead, the same grouping `lap rr` and the board use:

```
▾ S3 T-1: declare time() on Windows                          6 commits
  ▾ Log what Windows must check for the plugin portability fixes.   3
      L14565 9091b3d  Lists the explicit <time.h> include that …   windows.md · lines 1221-1222
      L14564 dcc7630  Retitles the entry and its intro, since …    windows.md · lines 1217-1219
  ▸ Make the stdsocket plugin build on macOS and Windows.           2
```

- Under a session, one collapsible node per run of consecutive commits sharing an intent (a single-commit intent still gets its node), labelled with the intent and the commit count.
- A commit row is a leaf, not expandable: id, short hash, **behavior**, then file and lines. Clicking opens its diff as today; the tooltip carries the full intent and behavior when the label is truncated.
- Converted commits (behavior `The data of this field is not present`) show the file and lines in the behavior's place, not the placeholder.
- The filter still matches intent, behavior, id and hash; a match inside a group reveals the group.

**Done when:**
- tree-building tests cover consecutive and interleaved intents, a single-commit intent, and converted commits;
- the view is rendered in a light and a dark theme on a session with several intents.

item.description:
A commit's author line reads `L14562 f10e721 @ 09/27/2026:11:36 AM claude:`. The colon between date and time reads as part of the time, and minutes are too coarse: an agent records several commits a minute, and they all show the same time.

Two copies of the formatter, both `localTime`, both documented as `"<date>:<time>"`:
- `packages/lap-vscode/src/extension.ts` (the diff editor's commit comments)
- `packages/coboard-vscode/src/lapview.ts` (the board's commit comments)

Both change the same way, with their doc comments.

author: claude
body:
**Widened by the user to the CLI too. Decided:**
- **Stored:** UTC, unchanged (log `ts`, JSON output).
- **CLI human output** (`log`, `search`, `rr`, `session list`): local time as `2026-09-27 11:36:48` (fixed year-month-day order, not the locale's). `lap show` adds the offset: `2026-09-27 11:36:48 +02:00`.
- **Filters** (`--since`/`--until`): a time with `Z` or an offset is taken as given; a zone-less time is local (`2026-09-27`, `2026-09-27 11:00`, `2026-09-27T11:00:00`), so anything copied from the output filters correctly. In the repeated hour when clocks go back, the first of the two moments is taken.
- **Editor views:** both `localTime` formatters print the locale's date, a space, and the time with seconds.
- Spec's timestamp paragraph says all of this.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S83 (L2796–L2816), git `00d1ea0`.

**CLI**
- `plat_ts_local` renders a stored UTC time in the machine's zone: `2026-09-27 11:36:48`. The offset (`+02:00`) is computed from the local fields read back as UTC, so it needs no `tm_gmtoff` and works on Windows.
- Used by `log` and `search` rows, `search --file --line` ("last touched by … (2026-09-27 11:46:59)"), `rr`'s span, and `show`, which adds the offset: `date: 2026-09-27 11:46:59 +02:00`.
- `plat_ts_parse` turns a filter time into a log timestamp: a date, or a date and time (`T` or space, seconds optional). `Z` or an offset (`+05:30`, `-0400`) is taken as given; zone-less is local; in the repeated hour the earlier moment wins; anything else is `bad_time`. `search --since/--until` convert both bounds before comparing. This also fixes date-only bounds, which the index's prefilter used to ignore.
- JSON and the log are unchanged (UTC ISO). The spec's timestamp paragraph says all of it.

**Editor views:** both `localTime` formatters print `09/27/2026 11:36:48 AM` (the locale's date, a space, time with seconds). Lap History's moved from `extension.ts` into `model.ts` so it can be tested.

**Tests**
- Unit 1828/1828. `test_time` sets `TZ`: UTC, Kolkata `+05:30`, New York in summer and winter, and Berlin parsing including 2026-10-25 02:30 → 00:30Z (the earlier moment).
- e2e 91/91. JSON is UTC; `TZ=Asia/Tokyo` shows `+09:00`; a time copied from `log` works in `--since` and `--until`; the same text under `TZ=UTC` matches nothing; `bad_time`.
- lap-vscode 37/37, coboard-vscode 36/36, each with a `localTime` test.

**Checked instead of rendered:** the author line lives in VS Code's native comment thread, not a webview, so it was printed from the built modules rather than rendered. Board: `L14562 · f10e721 @ 09/27/2026 11:36:48 AM claude:`; Lap History: `L14562 f10e721 @ 09/27/2026 11:36:48 AM claude:`.

**Not verified:** Windows builds.

item.title: lap: intent and behavior, and commits that name each other
item.description:
A lap commit's single message becomes two required fields: **intent** (why the edit exists, shared by edits that serve one goal) and **behavior** (what this edit makes the code do, its own for every edit). `lap commit` refuses weak messages with simple word-overlap checks, prints the new commit's hash, and every command that takes a commit accepts a hash; a commit's text refers to another as `#<hash>`, which the UIs turn into links.

Why: one edit per commit is what makes large agent changes reviewable, but a single message invited the `(1/n) … (n/n)` pattern, where one reason was copied across fragments and each hunk stopped explaining itself. Splitting intent from behavior lets the shared part be shared honestly and makes each hunk say what it does.

**Decided**
- `-m` is removed outright; every command refuses flags it does not know (`unknown_flag`).
- lap is unreleased: the spec changes in place, with no version bump and no compatibility rules. A commit without both `intent` and `behavior` is malformed; `msg`-only commits are not read.
- This repository's log is converted once, in place, by a throwaway script (not a lap command): each `msg` becomes the `intent` with its `(i/n) ` prefix stripped, and `behavior` is the fixed string `The data of this field is not present`. Ids are kept; the hash chain is recomputed.
- Grouping by intent (in `rr` and the board) is display only: every hunk stays its own commit.
- No relationship types: "needs" or "fixes" are just words next to a `#hash`.
- lap stays single-developer: no branches, logs are never merged.

**Out of scope:** branches, the GitLab/GitHub mirror, lap suggesting links by reading code.

**Cutover:** the CLI, both extensions and the skills land together, with the log converted at the same time; the installed lap cannot read a converted log.

Where the draft spec is: the first comment on T-66.

A missing shadow is rebuilt without reloading the log or index for every file
item.description:
On a fresh Windows clone of typec (only `.lap/log.jsonl` from git, `lap rebuild` failing, so no caches), `lap status` died asking `malloc` for 68,719,476,736 bytes.

Cause: `file_diff_load` → `shadow_from_log` (`cmd_common.c`) rebuilds a missing shadow by calling `idx_ready` (which loads the whole index) and, without an index, `rec_log_load` (the whole 34 MB log, parsed) — **once per file**, into the command's one arena, which frees nothing and doubles each new chunk. ~14,600 files × tens of MB → a 64 GiB chunk request.

Fix: load the index, or the log, at most once per command and reuse it for every file. Keep it valid only while the log has not changed size (a writer in the same command appends after reading).

**Done when:**
- `shadow_from_log` loads the index or the log once per command, however many files it is asked about;
- a reproduction (many files, caches deleted, `lap status`) is measured before and after (peak memory and time) in the closing comment;
- lap's unit and e2e suites pass, with an e2e case for status with every cache deleted over many files.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S98 (L2946–L2951), git `320e206`.

**Fix.** `Repo` carries `shadow_idx` / `shadow_log` / `shadow_log_size` / `shadow_loaded`. `shadow_from_log` loads the index (`idx_ready`) or, without one, the parsed log (`rec_log_load`) on the first missing shadow, and reuses it for every other file while the log keeps the same size (a stat per call; a writer's append invalidates it). `Idx` gained a struct tag so `repo.h` can point at it without including `idx.h`.

**Reproduction** (macOS, 400 files × 200 lines, 4.8 MB log, `lap status`, every cache but the log gone):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| log only (the Windows case) | 9.16 s, **3.58 GB** peak | 0.39 s, 57 MB |
| log + index, no shadows | 0.11 s, 86 MB | 0.02 s, 25 MB |

Output identical before and after, text and `--json`, both clean and with two edits (a changed line, an appended line).

**Real case:** a `git clone --local` of typec (14.6k files, 33.8 MB log, no caches): fixed `lap status` takes 2.21 s, 622 MB peak, reports clean. The old binary was not run on it — by the reproduction's ~9 MB per file it would need well over 100 GB, which is the 64 GiB `malloc` the Windows run died on.

**Tests:** unit 1,828 pass; e2e 92 scenarios pass, including a new one (120 committed files cloned with only the log, one edited: status reports exactly that file and writes no index; under `ulimit -v 512 MB`, which Linux enforces and macOS ignores).

**Left:** 622 MB on typec is each file's contents accumulating in the command's one arena (a per-file scratch arena would bound it); arena chunks still double without a cap; `idx_file_id` is a linear scan per file. The Windows `lap rebuild` failure ("cannot write shadow for tc_flow.c") that left the caches missing is unexplained. Not verified on Windows.

item.title: lap reads CRLF as LF, so a Windows checkout shows the same status as the Mac

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S99 (L2952–L2956), git `907aa76`.

**Change** (`cmd_common.c`, `file_diff_load`): a new `without_cr` copies a file's lines with the `\r` of every CRLF ending dropped (line count unchanged; a `\r` on a last line with no `\n` is kept). The working file's lines go through it, so they are compared and recorded as LF. The diff runs against a `without_cr` copy of the shadow, while the shadow itself is untouched: it stays exactly what the log replays to, so `verify --deep` still compares bytes. `split_lines` is unchanged (it also parses the log and `.lapignore`; its byte-faithful unit test stands).

**SPEC**, Edit detection: "CRLF is preserved byte-faithfully" is replaced by the rule above, including that lap does not read `.gitattributes` and that a line-ending change alone is no change.

**Tests:** unit 1,828; e2e 93 scenarios, all pass. New scenario: LF-recorded files checked out CRLF are clean; an edit in the CRLF copy is one edit, committed without a `\r`; status clean after; `verify --deep` passes; a lone final `\r` is an edit.

**Checked by hand** against a log written by the previous lap with CRLF lines: CRLF and LF working copies both clean; an edit is one edit, recorded as LF while the old line keeps its recorded `\r`; `verify --deep`: 0 mismatches.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S101 (L2959–L2980), git `e47a5ef`.

**Changes**
- `status` reads and diffs each file in a scratch arena, reset before the next (`arena_reset`, new: frees all chunks but the largest). What the output needs is copied out as the file is reported.

item.title: kb builds on Linux: tree-sitter finds its own unicode headers
item.description:
On Linux, building kb fails: `src/third_party/tree-sitter/lib/src/unicode/utf8.h:37: fatal error: unicode/umachine.h: No such file or directory`.

The vendored copy has the file (`lib/src/unicode/umachine.h`), but `utf8.h` includes it as `"unicode/umachine.h"`, which needs `lib/src` on the include path; both builds add only `lib/include`. gcc and clang look for a quoted include beside the header that includes it (`lib/src/unicode/`), then on the path, then in the system headers. So:
- **macOS** built by taking Apple's ICU header from the SDK (`MacOSX.sdk/usr/include/unicode/umachine.h`) instead of tree-sitter's — wrong, silently;
- **Linux** has no ICU headers unless `libicu-dev` is installed, so it fails;
- **Windows** built because MSVC also searches the directory of the file that started the include chain (`lib.c`, in `lib/src`).

Add `lib/src` to the include path for tree-sitter's `lib.c` only (as tree-sitter's own build does), in CMake and the Makefile, so its headers cannot shadow kb's.

**Done when:** on macOS, `lib.c` compiles against the vendored `umachine.h`, not the SDK's (checked with `-H`); kb's suites pass; the user's Linux build succeeds.
