Best built after M-14's merge work (T-124, T-125, T-127, T-157), which changes `lap merge`.

item.title: Older lap reads what it understands of a newer history, and never writes to it
item.description:
**Why.** `rec_decode` refuses unknown record types, so any new type (`branch`, `merge`, and soon `amend`) makes an older lap unable to read the history at all — as the installed pre-chunks lap cannot read this repository today. Harmless while lap has one user who rebuilds; not once it has others. Lap History already ignores unknown types; only the CLI refuses.

**Rule**
- **Readers skip record types they do not know**, with one notice per command: "this history has newer records (type …); update lap to see them". Everything they understand is shown (for `amend`: the original text).
- **Writers refuse** to append to a history containing a record type they do not know (`newer_history`): a write on top of records whose meaning it cannot see (e.g. `merge`) could be wrong.
- The hash chain still covers every record, known or not; `verify` checks the chain of unknown records too and says it could not interpret them.

This has to ship **before** the record types it should tolerate, so it protects the version after it; say so in the SPEC ("from this version on, a lap reads newer histories as far as it understands them").

**Done when:** e2e with a hand-written record of an unknown type: `log`/`show`/`rr`/`status` work and print the notice; `commit` refuses with `newer_history`; `verify` passes the chain and reports the unknown type; `SPEC.md` states the rule.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session **S124**, git `4b26885`.

**What changed**
- New `plat_same_file(a, b)`: two paths are one when `stat` gives the same device and inode (on Windows: the same volume serial and file index, through `GetFileInformationByHandle`). It returns false when either path is missing.
- `lap branch start` refuses `same_folder` when the two paths are equal as text or are the same directory on disk. The check runs before anything is read or written, so a case variant, a symlink or a `..` path can no longer make a folder a branch of itself or delete its registry.
- SPEC: the `branch start` entry defines `same_folder` by the directory on disk.

**Decided while building (please check)**
- I compare the two folders themselves rather than their `.lap` directories. For an existing folder the answer is the same, and the check doesn't depend on `.lap` existing yet.
- The `realpath` step from the ticket's fix isn't needed for this check: device and inode already cover every spelling. Canonicalising stored paths is T-129's job.

**Tests**
- Unit: 4,214 pass. A new `test_platform.c` suite checks:
  - the same directory, directly and through `..`;
  - two different directories, or a missing one;
  - a symlink;
  - a case variant, asserted either way depending on whether the disk folds case.
- e2e: 128 pass (+1). In the parent folder, a symlink, a `..` path and (this Mac's disk folds case) `../BP` are each `same_folder`, and `.lap` is byte-identical afterwards (checksummed before and after).

**Not verified:** the Windows branch of `plat_same_file` compiles only on Windows; it wasn't built or run here.

item.title: branch start: a folder can become a branch of itself through another spelling of its path
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed).** `same_folder` compares paths as strings (`cli/lap-cli/src/cmd_branch.c:152-163`), without resolving them.

**Repro** (macOS, case-insensitive disk): in a lap repo at `/x/s7e-p`, run `lap branch start self --from /x/S7E-P`. Also through a symlink to the folder itself (once the parent's open chunk is empty, e.g. right after another branch start).

**Observed:** `{"ok":true}`; `.lap/lineage` names `self`; `lap branch list` says "this folder is branch self … of main"; `lap commit --branch main` → `wrong_branch`. The registry just written, and every earlier branch entry, is deleted, because "here" and "there" are one folder and the copied-registry cleanup removes it (`cmd_branch.c:306-312`, lineage written at `:332`).

**Fix:** compare canonical paths (realpath, and on Windows the final path of the handle), and also refuse when both folders' `.lap` are the same directory (same device and inode / file id), which catches every spelling.

**Done when:** e2e refuses `same_folder` for a case variant, a symlink, and a `..` path, and nothing in the folder changes.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session **S125**, git `b52f3d8`.

**What changed:** `board_sessions` passes `session.branch` to `sessionCommits`. A session still only in a branch folder now gets that branch's commits (`lap log --session S<n> --branch <b>`), not this folder's session with the same id.

**Tests:** coboard 37 pass (+1). The new test uses real lap:
- a plain-copy branch and its parent each start their first session (both `S1`), tagged for two different tickets, and change `a.txt` differently;
- `board_sessions` for each ticket, through the MCP handler, returns that session's own commit.

I checked that the test fails with the old line (36 passed, 1 failed), then restored the fix.

item.title: board_sessions gives a branch session the parent's commits
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed).** The `board_sessions` MCP tool calls `sessionCommits(board.root, session.id)` without the session's branch (`packages/coboard/src/mcp.ts:208`). Branch and parent both number sessions from the base, so a session that exists only in a branch gets the parent's session with the same bare id. The Board view already passes it (`packages/coboard-vscode/src/extension.ts:353`).

**Repro:** a branch `feat` has S1 tagged `ticket=T-7`; the parent has its own S1 tagged T-9. `board_sessions T-7` returns session `{id:"S1", branch:"feat"}` with the T-9 commit.

**Fix:** pass `session.branch` (it is already in `ticketSessions`' result).

**Done when:** a coboard test with a branch and a parent sharing a session id returns each session's own commits through `board_sessions`.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session **S126**, git `1b52460`.

**What changed**
- The main fix already landed with T-127 and T-157. `lap merge` now builds and checks the whole stream in memory, writes chunks here only after every check, and never seals or writes anything in the branch folder. This ticket adds the proof and one ordering fix.
- **Ordering fix:** the base check (`unrelated_history`) now runs before the hash-chain check (`log_broken`). An unrelated branch's record can't chain from this history either, so it used to be reported as `log_broken` whenever its base chunk number happened to exist here.

**Tests:** e2e 129 pass (+1). With a plain-copy branch, the case where a merge would copy chunks:
- the branch's session start (its chunk's second line) is damaged → `log_broken`;
- an unrelated project's branch, whose chunk reached this folder as a `git merge` could bring it → `unrelated_history`.

After each refusal, both folders' `.lap` are byte-identical (every file checksummed before and after).

**Note:** damaging a folder's *last* record doesn't break the hash chain, since nothing chains from it. My first version of the test did that and the merge went through. That's an existing limit of append-only chains, not a merge bug, but a torn or edited tail is T-131's territory.

item.title: lap merge validates before it writes anything
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed).** `lap merge` copies the branch's chunks into the parent and seals the branch's chunk (`bring_chunks`, `cli/lap-cli/src/cmd_merge.c:128-132`) before its checks (`:159-176`).

**Repro:** tamper the second line of the branch's `<id>.000001.jsonl`, then `LAP_BRANCH=main lap merge feat` in the parent. Refused with `log_broken`, but the broken chunk is already in the parent's `.lap/log/` and the branch's chunk sealed; the parent's `lap verify` now fails (`branch feat: CHAIN BROKEN`). Same ordering for `unrelated_history`.

**Fix:** read and verify the branch's history (chain, base in this history, lineage) from wherever it is first; bring chunks and seal only once the merge will go ahead.

**Done when:** e2e: a merge refused for a broken branch log, and for `unrelated_history`, leaves both folders' `.lap` byte-identical.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap sessions **S127** and **S128**, git `937f644` and `7d639c3`.

**Chosen fix:** a rerun recognises records already adopted, by their `from` links. I didn't choose the atomic write: appending several lines in one write can still be torn part-way, and a crash after the log records is already healed by the next writer (state, shadow and snapshots are rebuilt from the log when the state lags the tail), so only the log needed an answer.

**What changed**
- Before placing, `lap merge` looks for records here whose `from` names one of this merge's new branch records: the records an interrupted run appended.
- When those records are the last thing recorded here (`merge_redo_point`), the merge places every commit against this folder's files from just before them, exactly as the uninterrupted run did. It then appends only what's missing: a commit already copied isn't appended again and is reported under its existing id; session starts and ends were already skipped by their `from`.
- The result is the uninterrupted merge's, ids and counts included.
- When other work was recorded after them, placement uses the latest files, and T-158's rule reports those commits as already done. The merge still completes, but the counts differ from an uninterrupted run.
- Test-only hook `LAP_TEST_MERGE_FAIL_AFTER=N`: stops a merge with `io_error` after N appended records, like `LAP_TEST_CHUNK_BYTES`.
- SPEC: the crash-safety section covers an interrupted merge.

**Tests**
- e2e: 130 pass (+1). A git-merged parent is copied, and one copy is merged without a stop as the reference. Copies stopped after 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5 records (session start, three commits, session end, merge record) are then rerun. Each reports `adopted 3 of 3`, holds the reference's history byte for byte apart from timestamps, is clean, and passes `verify --deep`.
  - I checked the test catches the bug: with the redo disabled, the stops after 2 to 5 records give a different history.
- Unit: 4,218 pass (+4, `merge_redo_point`): no earlier run; an earlier run's copies at the end; other work after them.

item.title: lap merge recovers from a failure part-way through
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed).** Adopted records are appended one at a time (`cli/lap-cli/src/cmd_merge.c:287-348`) and the merge record comes last. A rerun starts again from the previous merge's head; only `session_start` is de-duplicated by `from` (`:296-297`), commits and `session_end` are not.

**Repro:** a branch with 3 commits to `f.txt` (lines 2, 5, 9). In the parent, make `.lap/log` unwritable part-way (e.g. `LAP_TEST_CHUNK_BYTES=1400` so a new chunk is needed, then `chmod a-w .lap/log`), `lap merge b` → io_error after appending the session and two commits, no merge record. Restore, rerun: "adopted 0 of 3", `f.txt` stopped at a commit that was already adopted ("overlaps a change the parent made" — lap's own adoption), the third commit never adopted, the branch "partly merged" for good.

**Fix (pick one, say which in the SPEC):** a rerun recognises records already adopted (by `from`) and continues after them; or the merge is made atomic (write the whole run, then publish it). Either way the SPEC's crash-safety section covers merge.

**Done when:** e2e: a merge interrupted at each record boundary, then rerun, ends with the same history (up to ids) as an uninterrupted merge; `verify --deep` passes.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session **S129**, git `4b4d1b9`.

**What changed**
- `adopt_place` takes `parent_has` (lap merge already computed it) and follows whether the parent's file exists as commits are placed. Existence is judged before lines:
  - an **edit** of a file the parent deleted → conflict, `the parent deleted the file`;
  - a **create** of a file the parent has → already done if the lines and final newline are the same (this includes empty on both sides), else conflict, `both sides create it`;
  - a **delete** of a file the parent deleted → already done (the both-deleted case now depends on existence, not on "no lines");
  - after each placed commit the file exists unless it was a delete.
- The line-based already-done rule from T-158 no longer applies to deletes. A delete that reaches it has a parent file that still exists, even if empty, so it isn't identical.
- SPEC Merging rule 3 states the existence rules.

**Decided while building (please check):** only the parent's existence is passed, not the base's. The branch's own commits already say whether they create, edit or delete, so the base side adds nothing.

**Tests**
- Unit: 4,231 pass (+13). The three repros and their mirror images:
  - an edit to an empty file the parent deleted, and a delete of an empty file the parent wrote into;
  - one side creating empty and the other with content (both ways); empty on both is already done; the branch's create alone is placed;
  - an empty file deleted on both sides is already done, and a later re-create is placed.
- The existing call sites now pass `parent_has`; `none` parents pass `false`.
- e2e: 131 pass (+1), the audit's first repro with real git: the branch writes into an empty `e.txt` the parent deleted, and git's modify/delete is resolved by keeping the delete. `lap merge` stops `e.txt` with `the parent deleted the file`, the file stays gone, `status` is clean, and `verify --deep` passes.

item.title: Adoption tells an empty file from a missing one
item.description:
**Found by the audit's property test (confirmed).** `cmd_merge.c:254-257` computes whether the file exists at the base and on the parent (`base_has`, `parent_has`) but never passes that on; `adopt_place` (`adopt.c:69-74`) sees only 0-line `Lines`, the same for "empty" and "absent".

**Repros:**
- base has an empty `e.txt`; the parent `lap commit`s its deletion; the branch writes `hello\n` into it; `git merge`; `lap merge` → "adopted 1 of 1": the parent's history is create, delete, then an edit of a deleted file. Expected: stop (git reports modify/delete).
- base has no `n.txt`; parent creates it empty, branch creates it with content → a second `create` of an existing file adopted.
- base has an empty `e.txt`, both sides delete it → a second `delete` adopted.

**Fix:** give placement the existence of the file on each side and treat create/delete/edit against existence mismatches as conflicts.

**Done when:** unit tests for the three cases (and their mirror images) in the adoption module, and an e2e case; `verify --deep` passes.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session **S130**, git `47ffc06`.

**What changed**
- **`name_taken`** now also counts a name used by a branch whose chunks are in the parent's log (`branch_find`) or recorded by a merge there (a `merge` record's `name`), not only one in the registry. A merged and pruned branch's name can't be reused, and the message says a name stays with one branch.
- **`<branch>/S<n>`** resolves only sessions in the branch's own part, after its own branch record (`own_part_start`; for a branch of a branch, not its parent branch's record either). A session from before the base is `unknown_session`, both in another folder's view and in the branch's own folder, where it used to resolve silently.
- SPEC, Naming sessions: both rules.

**Tests**
- Unit: 4,235 pass (+4, `own_part_start`): a nested branch's own part starts after its own branch record; main and an unknown lineage start at 0.
- e2e: 132 pass (+1). Main has its own `S1` before the base.
  - `b/S1` is `unknown_session` in the branch, and in the parent before and after the merge. `b/S2` finds the branch's session, then its adopted copy.
  - After `b` is merged, its worktree removed and its entry pruned, `branch start b` in a new worktree is `name_taken`, and a new name works.

**Not covered:** histories that already hold two branches with one name (made before this change) keep resolving that name to whichever is found first. Only new duplicates are prevented.

item.title: Branch names stay unique for good, and name/S<n> never means an inherited session
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed).** After branch `feat` is merged, its folder removed and pruned, a new `lap branch start feat` is accepted: `name_taken` checks only the registry (`cli/lap-cli/src/cmd_branch.c:241`).

**Observed:** `lap rr feat/S2` in the parent then prints the parent's own pre-base S2 labelled as feat's (instead of the first feat's session). Once the second `feat` is merged and pruned too, the name resolves to whichever lineage sorts first (`branch_find` in `cmd_common.c`: registry, then walk order), so the first feat's sessions are unreachable by name. `session_resolve` searches the branch's whole view, inherited records included.

**Fix:** `name_taken` also covers every lineage whose chunks are present (and adopted `from` references); `name/S<n>` resolves only sessions of that lineage's own records.

**Done when:** e2e: reusing a merged branch's name is refused; `feat/S2` for an id that exists only before the base is `unknown_session`, not the parent's session.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session **S131**, git `bdec0e6`.

**What changed**
- `plat_mkdir` accepts an existing symlink to a directory. On `EEXIST` it checks with `stat`, which follows the link; `plat_is_dir` stays `lstat`-based for the tree walk. Sealing, new chunks and merge's chunk writes now work through a symlinked folder.
- New `plat_realpath`: `realpath` on POSIX; on Windows, the handle's final path with `/` separators.
- `repo_abspath` resolves an existing folder to its canonical path, so `branch start` (both folders) and `branch move` store and compare one spelling. This also fixes the absolute `/var/...` failure T-157 hit (macOS's `/var` is a symlink).
- SPEC, Registry: the path is stored canonical.

**Tests**
- Unit: 4,243 pass (+8): `plat_mkdir` on a symlink to a directory; `plat_mkdirs` creating through it; `plat_realpath` giving the same path through a symlink and through `..`, and false for a missing path.
- e2e: 133 pass (+1):
  - `branch start --from ../link` (a symlink to the parent) works, and the registry holds the real path;
  - `branch start --from $WORK/...` (under `/var`) works;
  - the branch folder, moved and reached through a symlink, is re-pointed with `branch move ../link` and merged; `status` is clean and `verify --deep` passes.

**Not verified:** the Windows `plat_realpath` wasn't built or run. I also left T-157's e2e helper on relative paths; it would work with absolute ones now.

item.title: Paths through a symlink work for branch start, merge and the registry
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed).** `plat_mkdir` treats an existing symlinked path component as a failure: `EEXIST`, then `plat_is_dir` uses `lstat` (`cli/lap-cli/src/platform.c:205,218`). Reached from `hist.c:336` (new chunk / seal) and `cmd_merge.c:78`; `repo_abspath` does not canonicalise.

**Repros:** `ln -s parent link; cp -R parent w; cd w; lap branch start x --from ../link` → `parent_read_only: cannot create …/link/.lap/log` (the real path works). After `lap branch move feat <symlinked path>`, `lap merge feat` → `io_error: cannot create …/.lap/log`.

**Fix:** follow symlinks when checking an existing directory (`stat`), and canonicalise folder paths where lap stores or compares them (with the self-branch ticket).

**Done when:** e2e passes `--from`, `branch move` and `merge` through a symlinked path.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session **S132**, git `96c1b98`.

**What changed**
1. **The real fix:** `repo_write_gitignore` writes `.lap/.gitignore`:

   ```
   /*
   !/.gitignore
   !/log/
   ```

   The pattern is anchored because a bare `*` would also ignore the chunk files inside `log/`. An existing file is kept. `lap init` writes it; `lap branch start` writes it in the new branch folder (the start fails if it can't) and in the parent's `.lap` when missing.
2. **Safety net:** `hist_folder_lineage` ignores a `.lap/lineage` whose `.lap/parent` names this folder itself, compared as a directory on disk (T-122's `plat_same_file`). The folder reads as `main`, with a notice once per command naming the files to remove.
- SPEC (Branches overview) and lap's README (the git advice: only the history goes to git, how to keep it local too, and lap branches for parallel work) are updated.

**Decided while building (please check):** I built only the self-parent check. The ticket's second check ("no branch record with the lineage's id in this folder's own lineage") can't tell a leaked lineage from a real one: both folders hold the same `<id>.000001.jsonl`, and nothing marks which folder a chunk "belongs" to. The self-parent check is what catches the repro.

**Tests**
- Unit: 4,254 pass (+11):
  - a lineage stands when its parent is another folder, and is ignored when it's this folder;
  - `repo_write_gitignore` writes the three rules and keeps an existing file.
- e2e: 134 pass (+1), the audit's repro in a project with **no** `.gitignore` of its own:
  - after `lap init` and `git add -A`, git tracks only `.lap/.gitignore` and `.lap/log/`;
  - the branch's `git add -A` leaves out its `lineage` and `parent`;
  - after `git merge`, the parent is still `main` (`"self":null`) and merges the branch;
  - a `lineage`/`parent` pair then copied in by hand is ignored with the notice, and main keeps committing; `verify --deep` passes.

**Note:** existing repositories get `.lap/.gitignore` only when a branch starts from them (or through `lap init` for new ones). This repository's root `.gitignore` already ignores `.lap/*` except `log/`.

item.title: A branch folder's identity files never travel through git
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed, design gap).** `.lap/lineage` and `.lap/parent` are machine-local, but lap does nothing to keep them out of git: `lap init` writes no ignore rules, and `cli/lap-cli/README.md:195-202` offers "track it or ignore `.lap/`".

**Repro:** a repo that `git add -A`s without ignoring `.lap/*`; a worktree branch; parent `git merge feat` → clean merge that brings `.lap/lineage`, and the parent silently becomes branch `feat` (`merge_in_branch`, `wrong_branch` on main).

**Fix** (folded in from the review comment):
1. **The real fix:** `lap init` and `lap branch start` write `.lap/.gitignore` that ignores everything in `.lap/` except `log/` and the `.gitignore` itself — self-contained, no change to the project's `.gitignore`.
2. **Safety net:** refuse to act as a branch when the folder's recorded parent (`.lap/parent`) is this folder itself (compare canonical paths or device + inode, as T-122 does), or when no `branch` record with the lineage's id is in this folder's **own** lineage (as opposed to chunks copied in from elsewhere).

*Not* the check "the branch record opens this folder's chunks": after `git merge` or `lap merge` the parent holds the branch's `<id>.000001.jsonl`, which does open with it, so that check passes in the repro.

**Done when:** the repro above leaves the parent `main` (with the `.gitignore`, and separately with a leaked `lineage`/`parent` pair, caught by the safety net); README's git advice matches.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session **S133**, git `49f7800`.

**What changed**
- New `hist_check(h, chain)`, which checks without reading the whole history:
  - **every sealed chunk** (any but the last) must end in a newline, else "sealed chunk X ends in a torn line: it was cut or copied short";
  - **with `chain`:** each chunk's first record must chain from the last record of the chunk before it (tail hash vs `prev`), else "X does not continue Y: the hash chain is broken there". This covers a stray chunk, one truncated at a line, and a wrong `prev`.
- `repo_open_at` runs it before any repair or write: the torn check for **every** command, so readers name the chunk instead of failing with "expected ':'", and the chain check for **writers**, which refuse.
- `hist_first_record`'s body became `chunk_first_record(path)`, reused by the check.
- SPEC, crash-safety section: damage is not a crash.

**Decided while building (please check)**
- **Writers don't parse the whole history on every write.** On this repository's 48 MB that would cost every commit a full re-hash. The check reads each chunk's last line and next chunk's first line; `lap status` here still takes about 17 ms. Tampering in the *middle* of a sealed chunk, where every line stays whole and the boundaries still chain, is still found only by `lap verify` (and when the index sync fails). I'd call that the right split: cheap structural checks on every write, the full proof on `verify`.
- **Readers refuse a torn sealed chunk outright** rather than reading around it. The history can't be parsed correctly past it (the torn bytes run into the next chunk's first line), so a partial answer would be wrong.

**Tests**
- Unit: 4,263 pass (+9), over three truly chained records:
  - chunks that chain pass, with a torn *open* chunk;
  - a sealed chunk with a torn line is refused by name, even behind an empty open chunk;
  - a chunk that skips a record passes without the chain check and is refused, named, with it.
- e2e: 135 pass (+1). On a history in several chunks, each of the ticket's cases (a torn line behind an empty open chunk, a sealed chunk cut 30 bytes short, a stray chunk):
  - `verify` names the damage;
  - `commit` is refused;
  - `.lap` is byte-identical afterwards (the lock file aside).

**Related:** T-139 (which chunk `verify` blames) is unchanged here. The stray-chunk case still reads "CHAIN BROKEN" in `verify` with the old blame.

item.title: A torn line in a sealed chunk: readers and writers agree, and nothing builds on a broken history
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed).** Readers look for a torn tail at the end of the whole history stream (`cli/lap-cli/src/rec.c:320-326`); the writer repairs only the last chunk and returns when it is empty (`hist.c:292-301`).

**Repro:** a repo in 5 chunks; `printf '{"type":"commit","partial' >> .lap/log/main.000005.jsonl`; create an empty `main.000006.jsonl`; `lap verify` → "chain ok … note: torn trailing record ignored … the next commit repairs it" (`cmd_verify.c:~258`); commit an edit → succeeds with "index sync: … expected ':'"; `verify` → "main.000005.jsonl line 5: expected ':'" — the torn bytes now run into chunk 6's first line. Not produced by lap itself (seal and merge repair first); it comes from git or copying.

**Related:** cutting 30 bytes off a sealed chunk makes `verify` report a parse error rather than "sealed chunk … was modified", and `commit` still succeeds on the unreadable history, only warning that the index sync failed (`idx.c:334`).

**Fix:**
- a torn tail outside the open chunk is damage, not a crash: readers report it, naming the chunk;
- **writers refuse to append on any history that does not read cleanly or whose chain is broken** — this ticket owns that rule for every case (torn sealed chunk, truncated chunk, stray chunk, wrong `prev`); T-139 only fixes which chunk `verify` names.

**Done when:** e2e for both repros and for a broken chain at a chunk boundary: `verify` reports the damage, `commit` refuses, nothing is written.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session **S134**, git `1d63dd8`.

**What changed**
- **Conversion publishes whole.**
  - Chunks are written into `.lap/log.converting/`.
  - An existing `log/` (an older lap's partial conversion) is moved aside whole to `.lap/log.replaced/`, other lineages' chunks carried over first. During that moment readers see only the old file, which is complete.
  - The working folder then becomes `log/` with one rename, and only then is `log.jsonl` removed.
  - Leftovers of a crashed run are cleared first; the fixed names are safe because conversion runs under the lock.
  - New `plat_rename` and `plat_rmdir`.
- **Readers:** `hist_open` reads the old file whenever it exists, unless the chunks hold all of it (they begin with every complete line of it), never a history cut short. The plain listing became `list_chunks`, which the converter uses, so it still refuses chunks that *differ* instead of silently replacing them.
- **Found by the live test:** a reader that chose `log.jsonl` read it by path later, and the conversion could remove it in between (1 of 40 reads failed). A reader now reads the old file whole when it opens the history (`Hist.mem`, used by `hist_read` and `hist_tail_hash`), and falls back to the chunks if it's already gone. This costs memory only while a folder is still in the old format, before its first write.
- SPEC (Chunks) and the converter's header now describe the one-rename publish; the false "a crash leaves one or the other complete" is gone.

**Tests**
- Unit: 4,270 pass (+7):
  - readers take the old file over partial chunks, and the chunks once they hold all of it;
  - a conversion leaves no working or set-aside folder;
  - the "differ" case still refuses and keeps both, and readers now take the old file there.
- e2e: 136 pass (+1). A 150-commit history turned back into `log.jsonl`:
  - an older lap's partial conversion, a crash before publishing (a partial `log.converting/`), and a crash after publishing each read the full record count;
  - a writer then converts cleanly and leaves no working folder.
- **Live loop:** 40 `lap verify` runs beside a conversion into 120-byte chunks all pass. The test also asserts that at least one read overlapped the conversion, so it can't pass vacuously. It was the loop that caught the race above. Three full e2e runs in a row were green.

**Related:** this also covers T-141. Leftover higher chunks from a run under another limit go aside with the rest of the old `log/`, so the chain stays whole. I'll close T-141 with its own test.

item.title: Readers never see a half-converted history
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed).** The conversion from `log.jsonl` publishes chunks one at a time (temp file + rename, `cli/lap-cli/src/hist.c:446-467`, `:458`), and readers use the legacy file only when there are no chunks (`hist.c:113`), listing the directory while renames happen (`hist.c:96-108`, `platform.c:566-588`).

**Repros:**
- crash: `log.jsonl` plus only chunks 1–2 of its conversion present → `lap log -n 1` shows L8 as head (real: L20); `lap verify` says "chain ok: 10 records" (real: 22), exit 0, nothing mentions `log.jsonl`.
- live: converting a typec clone with a small `LAP_TEST_CHUNK_BYTES` while looping `lap verify` → 39 of 40 runs fail with "history chunk main.001349.jsonl is missing".

The SPEC's "a crash leaves one or the other complete" is false for a split into several chunks.

**Fix:** convert into a temporary directory and publish it with one rename (then remove `log.jsonl`); readers that find both shapes read `log.jsonl` unless the chunks are a complete conversion of it.

**Done when:** e2e: an interrupted conversion at every chunk boundary is either invisible to readers or read in full; the live loop shows no failures.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session **S135**, git `ecc20a9`.

**What changed**
- `chunks.ts`:
  - `missingChunk(names, lineage)` finds the first number missing from a lineage's chunks while later ones exist.
  - `historyProblem(lapDir)` reports it in lap's own words ("history chunk main.000002.jsonl is missing from …"). It checks the folder's lineage, and in a branch folder also main, which its history starts with.
- The log source runs the check on every refresh. With a chunk missing it drops what it had read and reads nothing. The page message carries `problem`.
- The view shows the problem as an alert (error icon in the danger color) instead of any history, and says how to restore the chunk: from git or the folder it was copied from, then `lap verify`. Long paths wrap.

**Decided while building (please check):** only a *gap* is detected, as the Done when asks. A chain broken at a chunk boundary (a stray or edited chunk) isn't checked here: it needs hashing each boundary in TypeScript, and the CLI now refuses such a history on write (T-131) and names it in `verify`. I can add it if you want Lap History to catch that too.

**Tests**
- lap-vscode 51 pass (+1):
  - `missingChunk` finds the first gap (chunk 1 included), and none when the numbers run on;
  - `historyProblem` names a middle chunk removed from main and, in a branch folder, one missing from its own lineage.
- **Rendered** through the real host over a fixture of 6 chunks with chunk 2 removed, in light and dark (headless Chrome at 520 px). At 460 px the text looked cut off, but that's Chrome's minimum window width in headless mode, not the page.

**Note:** in lap, four behaviors in S135 were shifted by one (a too-short behavior was refused mid-loop). #2f83cb0 carries the correction; T-163's `lap amend` would be the proper fix for this kind of slip.

item.title: Lap History reports a broken history instead of showing part of it
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed).** `lineageChunks` (`packages/lap-vscode/src/chunks.ts:39`) stops at the first gap in chunk numbers, and `historyFiles` shows that prefix with no warning, as if it were the whole history. The CLI refuses the same state: with chunks 1 and 3 only, `lap log` → `history chunk main.000002.jsonl is missing`.

**Fix:** a gap (or a chain break at a chunk boundary) puts the view in an error state that names the missing chunk, like the CLI.

**Done when:** a unit test with a missing middle chunk gets the error, not a shorter history; rendered once.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session **S136**, git `af36de4`.

**What changed**
- **A branch is read incrementally, and only its own records.** `IncrementalLog` keeps a reader and a byte offset per branch. Each refresh reads only the whole lines past what it read, over `ownFiles` (the branch's own lineage chunks, from its folder while that's there, else from the chunks here). It starts over only when the files are another folder's or shrank. The inherited part is main's, already loaded; `ownPart` would drop it anyway.
- **`lap branch list` runs only when something it depends on moved.** `listSignature` covers the registry file's stat, the number of merge records in this folder's history, and the branch chunks here with their sizes. When it's empty (no registry, no branch chunk, no merge), lap is never run and the list is simply empty. A change in a registered folder (watcher), a registry fix, and activation force the list; a main-log change runs it only if the signature moved.
- **`firstLine`** reads a chunk's first line through a doubling window. `viewNames` uses it instead of reading a whole chunk (up to 4 MB) for its branch record.

**Timing on this repository's history** (47 MB, 13 main chunks; a branch based after chunk 13 with 50 records of its own; compiled code, one run each):

| | before | now |
|---|---|---|
| first read of the branch | 161 ms | 0.3 ms |
| after the branch grew by one record | 156 ms | 0.21 ms |

Before, every change re-parsed and re-hashed the parent's 47 MB. In this repository (no branches), `lap branch list` no longer runs at all on log changes.

**Tests:** lap-vscode 53 pass (+2):
- the incremental log reads only the branch's own chunk; reads only new whole lines as it grows (an unfinished line waits); reads on into a new chunk; starts over when the files shrank; returns null for no files;
- `firstLine` reads a 200 KB first line, and a file with no newline.

**Not verified:** in a live VS Code session. The signature gating was checked by reasoning and the compile, not by driving the extension host through registry changes.

item.title: Lap History reads a growing branch incrementally, off the UI's critical path
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed).**
- `BranchSource.read` (`packages/lap-vscode/src/extension.ts:201-208`) re-reads and re-parses the branch's whole history — the parent's chunks up to `base_chunk` plus its own; ~12 chunks / 49 MB in this repo — with a SHA-256 per line, synchronously in the extension host, every time its size changes, although only the branch's own part is kept.
- Every change to the main log runs `branches.refresh()` (`extension.ts:634`), which spawns `lap branch list --json`, even in repositories with no branches.
- `lineageFiles` (`chunks.ts:91`) reads the whole first own chunk (up to 4 MB) just to get its first line, on every refresh in a branch folder.

The main folder's own reading is already incremental (readdir + stat per chunk).

**Fix:** read a branch incrementally from the offset already read, and only its own lineage's chunks (the inherited part is main's, already loaded); run `branch list` only when the registry or a registered folder changed; read just the first line of a chunk.

**Done when:** tests for incremental branch reading; a note in the closing comment of the time taken by a refresh on this repo before and after.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session **S137**, git `8ca43ad`.

**What changed** (`Board.write`, `packages/coboard/src/store.ts`)
- A lock that can't be created for any reason other than `EEXIST` (another writer holds it) fails at once with a new `BoardError` code **`unwritable`**: "cannot take the board's lock in <dir> (EACCES): is the folder writable?".
- The 5 s deadline is checked on **every** pass, before the stale-lock test. The old path that `continue`d when `stat` failed can no longer spin forever.
- Creating the board folder or its `.gitignore` fails the same way (`unwritable`, naming the folder) instead of with a raw exception.

**Tests:** coboard 38 pass (+1). With the board folder read-only (the test is skipped when run as root):
- `create` throws `unwritable` in under a second;
- `board_create` through `COBOARD_DIR` comes back as a tool refusal whose text asks whether the folder is writable.

item.title: coboard never waits forever for a lock it cannot create
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed, pre-existing, now reachable through the board override).** In `Board.write` (`packages/coboard/src/store.ts:296-305`), when the lock file cannot be created (e.g. a read-only `.coboard/`), `statSync` throws, the loop `continue`s, and the 5 s deadline is never reached: the write hangs forever (`timeout 15 node t.js` → rc 124).

**Fix:** check the deadline on every iteration, and fail at once with a clear error when the lock cannot be created for a reason other than "exists" (EACCES, EROFS, ENOENT of the folder).

**Done when:** a test with an unwritable board folder gets an error promptly; the MCP tool returns it as a refusal.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session **S138**, git `5c117e3`.

**Cause:** without an index, `lap status` walks the shadow tree for tracked files, but only added a tracked file when its working copy was *missing* (a delete). A tracked file still on disk but ignored since was skipped by the ignore-filtered working walk, and then by the shadow walk too.

**What changed**
- The shadow walk adds **every** tracked file the working walk didn't list, found by binary search over the sorted working-walk entries: deleted files as before, and ignored-since-tracked files with their stat. That's the same set the index gives.
- New `plat_stat` (a regular file's size and mtime, as the walk takes them; `GetFileAttributesEx` on Windows).

**Decided while building (please check):** the ticket suggested taking the tracked set from the history. I used the shadow tree instead: it holds exactly the files with a live last commit, and walking it doesn't parse the whole log on every `status`. (If the shadow tree itself is damaged, a writer heals it from the log, as before.)

**Tests**
- Unit: 4,275 pass (+5, `plat_stat`: a regular file's size and mtime; a directory or a missing path is not a regular file).
- e2e: 137 pass (+1). A file tracked before its folder went into `.lapignore` gives an identical `lap status --json` with every cache (index, snapshots, statcache, heads, paths) moved away as with them, both **modified** and **deleted**.

item.title: lap status without caches still sees files tracked before they were ignored
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed, pre-existing — breaks the cache contract).** With no index, `lap status` builds the tracked set only from the ignore-filtered walk plus the shadow walk (`cli/lap-cli/src/cmd_status.c:125-135`), so a file lap tracked before it was added to `.lapignore` disappears from the output when the caches are gone.

**Repro:** a typec clone (its `.coboard/log.jsonl` was committed as L52, `.coboard/` is now in `.lapignore`): cold `lap status` → "clean"; after `lap rebuild` → "modified .coboard/log.jsonl [1] lines 18-63". The SPEC says deleting a cache "must change speed only, never output".

**Fix:** without an index, take the tracked set from the history (every file with a live last commit), the same set the index gives.

**Done when:** e2e: a tracked-then-ignored file shows the same status with and without caches (in both directions: modified, and deleted).

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session **S139**, git `868bc6d`.

**What changed**
- **Decoding:** a record whose `type` this lap doesn't know decodes as `REC_UNKNOWN` (its type name kept) instead of failing the whole read. Its `ts`, `prev` and hash are read like any record's, so the chain covers it; everything that works on known types simply skips it.
- **Readers:** one notice per command on stderr: *note: this history has records of a newer type ("amend") that this lap does not know: they are skipped here. Update lap to see them.* It comes from a full parse, or from the index, which now counts them.
- **Index:** a new `IDX_UNKNOWN` kind. The header's padding field became `unknown`, the count; indexes from before read 0 there, so the format didn't change.
- **Writers refuse** with **`newer_history`**, naming the count and type, *before* the torn-tail repair, the state heal, or any cache write. The check is read-only: the index header's count, plus a parse of only the bytes past what the index covers (all of them without an index). A refused writer leaves `.lap` byte-identical.
  - My first version synced the index first; the e2e caught that as a write.
- **Error codes:** `repo_error_code()` gives the reason a `repo_open` failed (`newer_history`, else `no_repo`). The twelve commands that reported every open failure as `no_repo` now use it (a scripted, mechanical change, committed per call site).
- **verify:** checks the chain across unknown records and reports them ("note: 1 record of a type this lap does not know ("amend"): in the chain checked above, not interpreted"; `unknown_records`/`unknown_type` in JSON).
- SPEC (The log): the rule, and that it protects versions from this one on.

**Tests**
- Unit: 4,287 pass (+12):
  - a newer-type record decodes as unknown, with its type, prev and a 64-hex hash; one without `prev` still fails;
  - a log with one between two known records parses all three, counts it by type, and its chain holds.
- e2e: 138 pass (+1). A hand-written, correctly chained `amend` record is appended to a real history:
  - `log`, `show`, `rr` and `status` work, and the notice names the type;
  - `verify` says "chain ok: 6 records" and reports the record;
  - `commit` and `session start` are refused as `newer_history`, and `.lap` is byte-identical.

This unblocks T-163 as ordered: a lap built from here will read histories holding `amend` records and refuse to write to them.

item.title: Older lap reads what it understands of a newer history, and never writes to it
item.description:
**Why.** `rec_decode` refuses unknown record types, so any new type (`branch`, `merge`, and soon `amend`) makes an older lap unable to read the history at all — as the installed pre-chunks lap cannot read this repository today. Harmless while lap has one user who rebuilds; not once it has others. Lap History already ignores unknown types; only the CLI refuses.

**Rule**
- **Readers skip record types they do not know**, with one notice per command: "this history has newer records (type …); update lap to see them". Everything they understand is shown (for `amend`: the original text).
- **Writers refuse** to append to a history containing a record type they do not know (`newer_history`): a write on top of records whose meaning it cannot see (e.g. `merge`) could be wrong.
- The hash chain still covers every record, known or not; `verify` checks the chain of unknown records too and says it could not interpret them.

This has to ship **before** the record types it should tolerate, so it protects the version after it; say so in the SPEC ("from this version on, a lap reads newer histories as far as it understands them").

**Done when:** e2e with a hand-written record of an unknown type: `log`/`show`/`rr`/`status` work and print the notice; `commit` refuses with `newer_history`; `verify` passes the chain and reports the unknown type; `SPEC.md` states the rule.

item.title: lap amend: correct a commit's intent and behavior without rewriting history
item.description:
**Why.** A commit's intent or behavior is sometimes written wrong. Today it is permanent, so corrections end up in later commits' messages (which should describe only their own edit) or in board comments — and whoever reads the commit with `lap show`, `rr` or Lap History sees the wrong text with nothing pointing to the fix. Seen in practice in the E-14 work.

**Decided with the user (2026-09-27): append-only, never a rewrite.** Rewriting a record (even only its message) changes its hash and every hash after it: branches' bases, `from` and `#hash` links, sealed chunks under git and the chain's tamper evidence would all break. Storing a `forward` field in the original record was also considered and dropped: it edits a line already written (often in a sealed chunk), which conflicts in git and breaks append-only crash safety. The forward pointer is derived instead.

**Build**
- `lap amend <commit> (-i "intent" -b "behavior" | -F <file|->)` appends `{"type":"amend","of":"<the commit's hash>","intent","behavior","user","ts","prev"}`. Both fields are required, as for commits (repeat one to keep it), and the **same message checks** apply.
- **`of` always names the commit**, never an earlier amendment (simplified from a chain, agreed with the user). Amending twice = two amend records with the same `of`; **the latest is the last one in log order**. No chain to resolve, and nothing ever addresses an amend record.
- **Messages only.** Code is never touched; a wrong edit is fixed by a new commit.
- **Derived pointer.** commit → latest amendment is built in memory, and cached in the index under the cache contract — never written into the log.
- **Hidden, overriding.** `amend` records do not appear as history entries in `log`, `rr`, `search` results or the views; wherever the commit appears, its latest text is shown, marked "amended" (with the count). `show <commit>` also lists the earlier texts, oldest first. `search --msg` matches the latest text (earlier ones behind a flag, if cheap).
- **Scope.** Only commits of **this folder's own lineage** can be amended: a branch cannot amend what it inherited from its parent (records before its base) → refused (`not_own_commit`).
- **Merge.** `lap merge` carries a branch's amendments: each amend's `of` maps to the adopted commit through that commit's `from` link, in one step, appended in order; amendments of commits that were not adopted (stopped files) stay in the branch.
- **Views.** Lap History and the board review show the latest text with an "amended" marker; the earlier texts on demand.
- **Skills.** The lap skill and the tickets skill say: correct a wrong intent or behavior with `lap amend`, not in later commits' messages or board comments.
- **Older lap versions.** An older lap refuses a history containing `amend` records (it refuses unknown record types). Accepted: the SPEC says a history with amendments needs this lap version or later. The general fix (readers skip unknown types, writers refuse) is its own ticket.

**Done when**
- e2e: amend a commit, amend it again → `show`/`log`/`rr` show the latest text, `show` lists the earlier ones, no `amend` entry in `log`/`rr`; message checks refuse a weak amendment; amending an inherited commit from a branch is refused; `verify --deep` passes and no existing byte of the log changed (compare before/after); deleting the index changes nothing but speed;
- e2e: a branch amends one of its commits, `git merge` + `lap merge` → the adopted commit shows the amended text on the parent;
- views: unit tests for the latest-text model; rendered once;
- `SPEC.md` (record type, command, scope, merge, the version note), lap's README and both skills document it.

Best built after M-14's merge work (T-124, T-125, T-127, T-157), which changes `lap merge`.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session **S140**, git `7c61788`.

**What changed**
- **Record.** `{"type":"amend","of","from"?,"user","intent","behavior","forced"?,"ts","prev"}`. `of` always names the commit; the last amendment in log order wins. Decoding refuses a record missing `of`, `intent` or `behavior`.
- **`lap amend <commit> (-i -b | -F) [--force-message] [--branch B] [--json]`** (`cmd_amend.c`). Needs no session. It runs the commit message checks: the previous behavior is the one before the commit in its session, and the code is the commit's own lines. Refusals: `not_own_commit` (in a branch folder, anything before its base), `not_a_commit`, `same_message`, `unknown_ref`/`ambiguous_ref`. Output: `[L42 fa9cebd] amended (n)`.
- **Readers.** `repo_log_load` applies amendments (`rec_amend_log`). The index gets an `IDX_AMEND` entry kind, and `idx_fetch` gives each commit its latest text. It decodes the amend entries once per index and keeps them in the index's arena. The index magic is now **LAPIDX03**, so the T-164 lap finds no index it knows, scans the history, sees the amend records and refuses to write. Every commit's JSON carries `"amended":n`. `log`/`search` add `(amended)` / `(amended N times)` after the intent and `rr` adds it after the behavior. `show` adds an `amended:` line and lists the earlier texts after the behavior (JSON: `amended_by`, `amended_ts`, `earlier[]`). `search --msg` matches the latest text; searching earlier texts was not built.
- **Merge.** Each branch amend is appended with `of` set to the adopted copy, found through that copy's `from`. For a commit the branch itself had adopted, the lookup goes through its `from` instead. Amendments whose commit was not adopted stay in the branch and are counted as left. An amendment already here (straight or via a middle branch) is not appended again, and an interrupted run redoes cleanly (from links). The report shows `amendments carried/left` (JSON `amendments:{carried,left}`). A dry run does not count them.
- **Views.** Lap History's model applies amend records; they produce no row. A row shows an `amended` tag; the detail has a collapsible list of earlier texts with local time and author; the inline comment mentions the amendment. The board review shows an `amended` tag on the step. coboard's `commitDiff` carries `earlier`, and the editor comment quotes the earlier texts. The `board_sessions` description mentions `amended`.
- **Docs.** SPEC covers the record, the §Amendments paragraph, the index, the version note, merge step 4, `lap amend`, and the show/merge outputs. The README covers use and the command table. The lap skill and the tickets skill both say to correct a wrong message with `lap amend`, not in later messages or board comments.

**Decided**
- The T-164 fixtures used `amend` as their "unknown type". They now use `annotate` (unit test and e2e).
- No `not_own_commit` check for adopted commits on main: they are in main's own chunks, so main may amend them.

**Tests.** lap unit 4315 (new: amend round-trip, malformed records, apply order/latest/earlier, unknown hash, amendment before its commit). lap e2e 140 (2 new scenarios, one per Done-when bullet). lap-vscode 55 (+2), coboard 38 (lap-backed test extended), coboard-vscode 37 (+1). Combined check is clean. Rendered headless in light and dark: Lap History (earlier texts open) and the board review.

**Note.** I used `lap amend` in this session to fix three commits whose behaviors landed on the wrong fragment (L3953–L3955). So this repo's history now holds amend records, and reading it needs this lap build: the installed lap refuses it, and a T-164 build reads it without the corrections.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session **S141**, git `6832eec`.

- **coboard:** `board_get` on a ticket now adds `lapError` (lap's message) whenever `ticketSessions` fails, the same way `board_sessions` does. An agent reading `sessions: []` alongside a `lapError` can tell lap failed rather than that the ticket has no work.
- **lap-vscode:** new setting `lap.path`. When it is empty, the Board's `coboard.lapPath` is used, and after that `lap` on PATH. All four lap runs go through it: resolving references, branch list, show original, branch move/forget.
- **lap-vscode:** a failed `lap branch list` is now reported instead of reading as "no branches". The message comes from lap's JSON error, or is "lap could not run: …" when the executable is missing. Lap History shows it in a warning box above the list, and the log is still shown underneath. A folder with no branches never runs lap, so it never gets this box.
- **Tests:** coboard 39 (new: a failing lap stand-in makes both `board_get` and `board_sessions` return its message). lap-vscode 57 (new: `lapFailure` against a real failing stand-in, a missing binary and a good answer; `lapBin` fallback order). The host test's fake VS Code gained `getConfiguration`. The combined check is clean.
- **Rendered:** the warning box in light and dark, headless. The page message was injected with a `lapError`, so the render checks the webview's drawing, not the host's execFile path; the unit tests cover that path.

item.title: board_get says when lap failed, instead of showing no sessions
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed).** When lap fails (missing, too old for the repository's history, broken history), `board_get` returns `"sessions": []` because `packages/coboard/src/mcp.ts:146` drops `ticketSessions`' `ok:false` and its error; `board_sessions` does surface it as `lapError`. An agent concludes the ticket has no work. lap-vscode also runs bare `lap` from PATH with no lap-path setting, so its Branches group and "show original" fail quietly in the same case.

**Fix:** `board_get` carries `lapError` like `board_sessions`; lap-vscode shows lap's error (and takes the same lap path setting the Board already has).

**Done when:** tests with a failing lap stand-in: `board_get` returns the error; Lap History shows it.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session **S142**, git `0dd9de3`.

**Fix, in lap.** `lap branch list` now also lists every branch lineage whose chunks are in `.lap/log/` but which no registry lists. That covers a branch `git merge` brought from another clone, and one pruned from the registry after it was merged and its folder went away. Each such row:
- is built from the branch's own branch record (name, base, time);
- carries `registered:false` with an empty `path`;
- is never `missing`, since no folder is known for it; a branch that isn't merged shows as `active`;
- gets `via` set when its parent is another branch listed here.

Lineages this folder's own history reads (main, itself, and in a branch folder the branches it started from) are skipped.

Both views already build on `branch list`, so the fix reaches them without new session logic:
- **coboard:** `mergeSessions` still finds the pruned branch, so its adopted session keeps `adoptedFrom`. `session list --branch <name>` reads the branch's chunks here, so a merged-in branch's unadopted sessions are listed.
- **Lap History:** such branches appear in the Branches group, read from their chunks. The row's tooltip says "not registered here: read from its chunks" instead of an empty path and "(gone)". `parseBranchList` reads `registered`; when the field is absent (output from an older lap) the row counts as registered.

**Decided.** Taking the name from the `from` link or the merge record was the ticket's first idea, but listing the lineages already makes each adopted session resolve to the right branch through `branch list`. That keeps one source for names. For a merge chain it is also more exact than picking the nearest merge record, which could name the wrong branch.

**Tests**
- lap e2e 141. The pruning scenario now checks the registry file drops the branch, and that `branch list` still shows it as merged and unregistered. New scenario: a branch git merge brought, unknown to this registry, shows as active and unregistered, its tagged session lists via `--branch`, and it is merged after `lap merge`.
- coboard 39: the sessions test deletes feat's folder, a write prunes it, and the adopted session still says `adoptedFrom: "feat"`.
- lap-vscode 58: new row-parsing test. coboard-vscode 37.

**Not verified:** only the tooltip changed in Lap History; I did not render it.

item.title: Views keep a merged branch's name after it leaves the registry, and see merged-in branches
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed).** `mergeSessions` marks adopted sessions with their branch only for branches `lap branch list` returns. Merged-and-gone branches are pruned from the registry (by design), after which adopted sessions show without their branch. Likewise, a branch present only as chunks (brought by `git merge`, never registered here) is invisible: neither Lap History nor the board lists its unadopted sessions — consistent with the SPEC, but a gap.

**Fix:** take the branch name of an adopted session from its `from` link / the `merge` record (history, not the registry); list lineages present in `.lap/log/` alongside registered ones (lap's `branch list` could report them as `present`).

**Done when:** tests: an adopted session keeps its branch name after the branch was pruned; a merged-in unregistered branch's sessions are listed.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session **S143**, git `397b6e7`.

**What changed.** Naming a chain break moved out of `repo_log_load` into `hist_name_break` (hist.c), so it can be unit-tested. At a chunk's first record it now follows that record's `prev`, as the ticket's review comment set out:
- `prev` is a record *inside* the chunk before (not its last) → that chunk was appended to → "sealed chunk X was modified", as before.
- `prev` is the *last* record of another chunk → this chunk is a stray or a duplicate → "chunk main.000006.jsonl does not belong after main.000005.jsonl: it continues main.000002.jsonl".
- Otherwise both chunks are named → "chunk main.000003.jsonl does not continue sealed chunk main.000002.jsonl". "sealed chunk" is written when the chunk before is sealed.

A break inside a chunk still blames that chunk (when sealed), as before.

**Changed expectation.** The existing e2e "verify names a sealed chunk that was modified" edits the text of a chunk's only record. That leaves no clue which side changed, so it now names both chunks instead of blaming chunk 2. This follows the ticket's rules; a truncated sealed chunk ends the same way.

**Tests.** e2e 142 (new scenario: a stray chunk is blamed; a sealed chunk appended to is blamed; a truncated sealed chunk and a wrong first `prev` in the open chunk both name both). Unit 4335 (new `hist_name_break` tests: stray, appended, a `prev` leading nowhere, and a break inside a sealed chunk). The SPEC's verify paragraph describes the three cases.

**Not in scope:** readers still follow a stray chunk (`log` shows its records as head). Refusing to write on a broken chain is T-131's.

item.title: verify blames the right chunk at a chunk boundary
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed).** When the chain breaks at a chunk's first record, `verify` always blames the previous chunk (`cli/lap-cli/src/repo.c:536-556`). That is right when chunk N-1 was truncated or appended to (deliberate since T-104), and wrong for a stray or duplicated chunk N.

**Repro (wrong blame):** a repo in 5 chunks; copy `main.000003.jsonl` to `main.000006.jsonl` → "sealed chunk main.000005.jsonl was modified: hash chain broken at main.000006.jsonl line 1". Chunk 5 is intact; 6 is the stray. Same when only the open chunk's first `prev` is wrong. (Readers also silently follow the stray chunk — `log` shows L12 as head.)

**Fix** (folded in from the review comment) — the boundary alone cannot tell which side changed, so use what the chunks show:
- N's first `prev` matches a record inside N-1 that is not its last → N-1 was appended to: blame N-1;
- N-1's last hash is another chunk's first `prev` (a duplicate or stray N) → blame N;
- otherwise name both: "main.000006.jsonl does not continue main.000005.jsonl".

"Writers refuse a broken chain" is **not** here: it is T-131's fix (one implementation, one ticket).

**Done when:** e2e for a stray chunk (blames N), a sealed chunk appended to (blames N-1), a truncated sealed chunk, and a wrong first `prev` with no other clue (names both).

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session **S144**, git `12740f7`.

- **Decided:** a `log.jsonl` with no complete record (0 bytes, or only a torn line) converts into **one empty `main.000001.jsonl`**. The folder keeps a history with nothing in it yet, and the first write fills it exactly as it would have filled the old file (first `prev` = zeros). I did not synthesise an `init` record: conversion never writes records, and an old empty log never had one. The torn line is dropped with the usual "repaired torn log tail" notice.
- **Second bug found on the way:** `idx_sync` returned early when the index "covered" all 0 bytes even though no index file existed, so a writer on an empty history failed with "index unavailable after sync". It now returns early only when an index was actually loaded; an empty history gets its empty index.
- SPEC's single-file-log paragraph says so.
- **Tests:** e2e 143. New scenario, for both an empty and a torn-only log: readers say "no commits yet", the first write converts into 1 chunk, and a commit, `log`, `verify` (2 records) and `verify --deep` then work. Unit 4347 (new: both kinds of old file become one empty chunk and are removed).

item.title: Conversion refuses an empty legacy log instead of deleting it
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed).** A 0-byte (or torn-only) `.lap/log.jsonl` converts into 0 chunks and is deleted (`cli/lap-cli/src/hist.c:446-467`, `repo.c:370-374`): "moved .lap/log.jsonl into 0 chunks", then "error: no history in …/log" — and readers, which printed "no commits yet" before, fail too.

**Repro:** `mkdir -p e1/.lap; : > e1/.lap/log.jsonl`, then any writing command.

**Fix:** an empty legacy log is left alone (or treated as a fresh repository with an `init` record, whichever the SPEC says); never a repository with no history.

**Done when:** e2e: the repro leaves a working repository.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session **S145**, git `bf00e4e`.

The atomic publish (T-132) did **not** cover this repro. With chunks 1–3 from a limit-4000 run plus leftover chunks 4–5 from a limit-1000 run, the chunks start with the old file and run past it. The "already converted" test accepted that, removed `log.jsonl` and left a broken chain.

**Fix.** Chunks that run past the old file are now judged by what follows it:
- If the extension continues the old file's chain (records appended since), the conversion is finished and the old file is removed, as before.
- If it breaks the chain and every record in it is one the old file already holds, it is leftovers of another run. The conversion is redone: the chunks are rebuilt from the old file and published atomically, and the old `log/` moves aside and is cleared.
- Bytes that don't parse are not judged, so behaviour there is unchanged. I chose this to avoid discarding anything that might be real history.
- Chunks that differ from the old file are still refused.

SPEC's single-file-log paragraph says so.

**Tests.** e2e 143: the half-converted scenario gains the repro (a finished large-limit run plus two small-limit leftovers). The next write converts again, `log.jsonl` is gone, and `verify` reports every record plus the new one. Unit 4355: new tests for "old file + appended record → kept as converted" and "old file + repeated records → converted again to exactly the old file".

**Not changed:** a *reader* finding this state reads the chunks, since they hold all of the old file, so before the first write it sees the broken chain. The first write repairs it.

item.title: A conversion resumed under another chunk limit keeps the chain whole
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed; reachable only when the limit changes between runs, i.e. with `LAP_TEST_CHUNK_BYTES`).** The "already converted" test accepts chunks longer than the old file that start with it (`cli/lap-cli/src/hist.c:421-428`), so leftover higher chunks from a run under another limit survive; stale higher chunks are removed only after the rewrite (`hist.c:468-474`). A crash between the two deletes `log.jsonl` and breaks the chain.

**Repro:** a legacy log, chunks 1–3 converted at limit 4000, leftover chunks 4–5 from a limit-1000 run, then `lap session end` → `log.jsonl` deleted; `verify` → "CHAIN BROKEN: sealed chunk main.000003.jsonl was modified … main.000004.jsonl line 1".

**Fix:** likely solved by publishing the conversion atomically (the half-converted-history ticket); otherwise remove stale chunks before trusting the set.

**Done when:** e2e for the repro keeps a whole chain.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session **S146**, git `cf9a7d9`.

**What changed**
- New `plat_write_file_atomic_in(path, tmpdir, …)`; `plat_write_file_atomic` is now that with no temp folder. On top of it, `hist_write_chunk(logdir, name, …)` puts the temp file in the folder above `log/` (`.lap/`, same filesystem, so the rename stays atomic).
- Every writer that creates a whole chunk in `log/` now uses it:
  - `lap branch start`: copies of the parent's chunks, and the branch's first chunk;
  - `lap merge`: chunks copied from a branch folder.
- Appends and seals only append to or create chunk files, so they never made temp files. The conversion already wrote into `.lap/log.converting/`, which is published whole.
- **Cleanup:** a writer that holds the lock, right after conversion, runs `hist_clear_tmp`, which removes every `*.tmp.<digits>` in `.lap/log/`. There is no pid check, as agreed. Readers never took such a file for a chunk (chunk names must parse), and they leave it alone.
- SPEC's chunks section says so.

**Tests**
- Unit 4360. A chunk write succeeds while a *folder* sits where `log/`'s temp file would be, which only works if the temp goes elsewhere; the old code fails here. Leftover temp files are removed by `hist_clear_tmp` and never read as chunks.
- e2e 144: a temp file left in `.lap/log/` survives `verify`/`log` (readers), is not read as history, and is removed by the next writer (`rebuild`).

**Not done as written:** the Done-when's "e2e interrupts each writer". There is no hook to crash `branch start` or a merge's chunk copy mid-write, so I used the deterministic unit check above instead of an interruption test.

item.title: Temporary files never land in .lap/log, and old leftovers are cleaned up
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed).** An interrupted conversion leaves `.tmp.<pid>` files in `.lap/log/` that nothing removes; git commits them if the project tracks `.lap/log/`.

**Fix** (folded in from the review comment):
1. **Keep temp files out of `.lap/log/`:** write them in `.lap/` (same filesystem, so the rename stays atomic) and rename into `log/`. git never sees them and readers never have to skip them. T-132's temp-directory conversion does this for the conversion; `plat_write_file_atomic` for new chunks and seals follows the same rule.
2. **Cleanup only for leftovers from older versions:** a writer holds the repository lock, so any `*.tmp.*` it finds in `.lap/log/` under the lock is a leftover and is removed. **No pid check** — `.lap/log/` travels between machines through git, so a pid means nothing here.

**Done when:** no lap command creates a temp file inside `.lap/log/` (e2e interrupts each writer and checks); a leftover temp file there disappears on the next writing command and is never read as a chunk.

body:
Done in lap session **S147**, git `4ad2d31` (see `git log`; commit "branch start holds this folder's lock throughout…").

**What changed**
- `branch_start` now does only argument handling. It then creates `.lap/` if needed and takes **this folder's lock** before anything else, holding it for the whole start.
- The old body is now `start_locked`, which runs the `already_branch` check under that lock and still takes the parent's lock from its checks through registration, as before. It releases this folder's lock just before reopening the folder to build its caches, since that reopen takes the lock again.
- If the start is refused and `.lap/` was created only for the lock, the lock file and the folder are removed again. The existing "a refused start made .lap here" check still passes.
- The SPEC's `branch start` entry says so.

**Tests.** New e2e scenario, run three times: two concurrent `branch start`s in one fresh folder. In each run exactly one succeeds, the other is `already_branch`, the parent's registry holds one entry for the folder, and the folder holds one lineage. e2e 145, unit 4360. I also built the previous `cmd_branch.c` and ran the new scenario against it: all three runs failed (both starts succeeded, two lineages, a phantom registry entry), so the test does catch the race.

**No unit test:** the fix is lock orchestration inside a command, which the e2e exercises for real.

item.title: Two branch starts in one folder cannot both succeed
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed, 5 of 5 tries).** Two concurrent `lap branch start` in one folder both succeed: the folder gets two `<id>.000001` lineages and the parent's registry a phantom `missing` entry. The `already_branch` check runs before any lock, and the branch folder itself is never locked (`cli/lap-cli/src/cmd_branch.c:164-177`).

**Fix:** take this folder's lock for the whole of `branch start` (then the parent's for sealing and registration), and check `already_branch` under it.

**Done when:** e2e: concurrent starts in one folder — exactly one succeeds, the other gets `already_branch`, the registry has one entry.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session **S148**, git `8dffeda`.

- New `plat_is_writable_dir` (POSIX `access(W_OK|X_OK)`, `_access` on Windows).
- `branch start` now checks, **before taking the parent's lock or sealing anything**, that the parent's `.lap/` and `.lap/log/` can be written in. If not, it refuses with `parent_read_only` and names the folder. This covers both of the audit's cases:
  - a fully read-only `.lap` (it was `no_parent: cannot acquire repository lock`);
  - `.lap` read-only with `log/` writable (the seal used to leave an empty new chunk behind).
- Refusals that come later still use the existing codes. With T-143's change, a refused start also removes a `.lap/` it made here.

**Tests.** e2e 145: the read-only-parent scenario now also checks both cases. Each gives `parent_read_only`, and the parent's `.lap` files are byte-identical before and after (shasum of every file). Unit 4365: the new helper on a folder, a file, a missing path and a 0555 folder (writable only for root). Like the existing scenario, the e2e is skipped when running as root.

**Not covered:** a parent whose permissions change between this check and the seal. The seal failing still refuses with `parent_read_only`, as before.

item.title: branch start refusals: the right code, and no chunk left behind
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed).**
- A fully read-only parent (`chmod -R a-w parent/.lap`) gives `no_parent: cannot acquire repository lock` instead of `parent_read_only` (`cli/lap-cli/src/cmd_branch.c:182-185`) — atomic, but the wrong code.
- With `parent/.lap` read-only but `log/` writable, the refusal (`parent_read_only`) comes after the seal already created an empty `main.000002.jsonl` in the parent (`cmd_branch.c:251` before `:275`).

**Fix:** check everything that can refuse (writability of the parent's `.lap` and `log/`, registry) before sealing; map a lock failure caused by permissions to `parent_read_only`.

**Done when:** e2e: both cases refuse with `parent_read_only` and leave the parent byte-identical.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap sessions **S149** and **S150**, git `dad3038` (+ `e28ba20`, lap history only).

**What changed.** The pruning gate in `prune_branches` used to look further only when a registered folder's `.lap` was missing. It now also does so when that folder's `.lap/lineage` is unreadable or names another lineage than the entry's, i.e. the folder now holds another branch. The rest was already right: `branches_status` counts a folder as present only while it holds that branch, so a merged branch in a reused folder is `merged` and not present, and the next writer drops it. SPEC's Registry section defines "gone" as missing or holding another branch.

**Tests.** e2e 146. New scenario: branch `b` is merged; its folder is reset to the parent's commit, its `.lap` removed, and branch `c` started there. After one write in the parent, the registry holds only `c` and `branch list` shows the folder once. `b` is still listed from its chunks as merged and unregistered (T-138). I also ran the scenario against the previous `repo.c`, and it fails there (b stays registered, the folder is listed twice). Unit 4365, unchanged: the logic is a static function exercised end to end.

**Process note:** I ended S149 with three of the four `repo.c` fragments still pending, and the one I committed (L4072) had the logic change's behavior on it. I corrected L4072 with `lap amend` and recorded the other three in S150.

item.title: A merged branch whose folder now holds another branch is pruned
item.description:
**Found by the audit (confirmed).** The pruning gate only checks that the folder's `.lap` exists (`cli/lap-cli/src/repo.c:306-312`), so a merged branch whose folder was reused for another branch is never pruned: `lap branch list` shows two entries on one path.

**Fix:** an entry is "gone" when its folder is missing **or holds another branch** (by id), as the registry's own validity rule already says.

**Done when:** e2e: merge `a`, reuse its folder for branch `b` → after the next writing command only `b` is listed.
