Robustness
item.description: Findings of the E-14 audit (2026-09-27): four read-only audits of chunks, branches and registry, merge by adoption (a property test of ~4,300 real git+lap merges: no wrong placement), and the views/SPEC/docs. The design held; these are the edges — odd paths, failures midway, damaged files, the views. Ranked by severity in each ticket; decisions for the user are marked **Decision**.

item.title: Robustness, round 2
item.description:
Findings of the second audit (2026-09-28) of the M-14 work: merge, nested branches, amend, chunks and caches, branches and the registry, coboard, the views, SPEC and docs. The audit's agents reported them; every ticket here was then **reproduced or confirmed in the code by hand** (scratch repos under the session scratchpad, `verify/`). A ticket says when a part of the original claim did not hold.

What held up (not ticketed): no git conflict in `.lap/log/` in any layout tried (worktree, copy, lagging parent, siblings, nested, 460 random merge cases); `verify --deep` passed and `--dry-run` changed no byte in every merge; crash reruns matched; the M-14 fixes T-122..T-170 pass their original repros; suites unit 4411, e2e 149, coboard 42, npm 554 all green; no performance regression on a typec clone.

Not ticketed, on purpose: a refused `lap merge` repairs a torn tail (the writer repair every command does, of bytes never acknowledged); case-sensitive branch names (allowed by the SPEC); the conversion's chunk cap (only reachable at about 4 TB); two view suspicions (offset on a lineage change, the first whole read) and one unclear view claim that did not reproduce.

item.title: branch start: a parent cannot become a branch of its own child, and a live registry is never deleted
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced).** A folder that has branches can start a branch from one of them. It then records to the new lineage, and its `branches.json` is deleted without a word:

```
lap init in main; commit .lapignore and a.txt; git commit
cp -R main wt; cd wt; lap branch start feat --from ../main
cd ../main; lap branch start oops --from ../wt      # the folders swapped by mistake
```

Observed: `branch oops (…) started from …/wt`, rc 0. main's `.lap/branches.json` is gone, `.lap/lineage` names oops. `lap merge feat` → "feat is this folder's own history"; `lap session start … --branch main` → "records to oops, not main".

It triggers exactly when the parent is quiet (nothing to commit), the layout the SPEC recommends.

**Cause.** `cmd_branch.c:147-156` checks only `.lap/lineage` (this folder is main, so it passes). `cmd_branch.c:346-353` deletes `branches.json` unconditionally, as if it were always a copied registry. Here its entries are live branches whose `.lap/parent` names this very folder.

**Fix.** Refuse (a new code, e.g. `has_branches`) when this folder's registry lists a branch whose folder exists and whose `.lap/parent` resolves to this folder — above all the `--from` folder itself. Drop `branches.json` only when it is a copy (its entries' parents are another folder).

**Done when:** e2e: the repro above is refused and changes nothing in either folder (tree hashes before/after); a copied registry is still dropped (existing test); unit tests for the "is this registry mine" decision.

item.title: lap merge never adopts work twice when it reached this folder through another branch
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced).** b1 from main, b2 from b1. b2 merged into b1, b1 into main, then b2 merged straight into main: main adopts b2's commits, sessions and amendments a second time, and changes b1 made on top of them are undone.

```
b2: insert X after line 5 (session --meta ticket=T-9), git commit
b1: git merge b2; lap merge b2; delete X (commit); git commit
main: git merge b1; lap merge b1; git commit           → status clean
b2: edit g.txt (commit); git commit
main: git merge b2 (clean, no X); lap merge b2
```

Observed: "adopted 2 of 2 commits (L6, L7)" — L6 inserts X again (L4 is the same commit via b1); `lap status` shows `a.txt [1] line 6` pending; `session list --meta ticket=T-9` lists S1 and S2, both "b2 work session". A session is duplicated even when the branch had no commit in it. The audit also saw spurious stops where the re-adopted commit overlaps b1's later work, so b2's new work is never adopted.

**Cause.** main has no merge record of b2, so all of b2 counts as new; a duplicate is recognised only by a direct `from` on this side (`cmd_merge.c:440-446`, `639-644` cover only this run's interrupted redo; sessions `616-622` look at `b->from` only; amendments `664-666`; the chain start `406-422`).

**Fix.** Before adopting, collect every original hash already here, following `from` links transitively (an adopted copy of an adopted copy), and skip commits, sessions and amendments whose original is among them; start the chain after the last record already here by that route.

**Done when:** e2e for the orders b2→b1→main then b2→main, and b2→b1, b2→main, then b1: nothing adopted twice, status clean, sessions once, amendments once, `verify --deep` ok. Unit tests for the transitive `from` set.

item.title: A change made in several commits on both sides is already done, not a conflict (and a rerun finishes the merge)
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced).** T-158 recognises an identical change only when one branch commit equals the parent's whole net change to that region.

Flat: both sides do `5 → five → FIVE` as two commits each. git merges cleanly; `lap merge b` → "adopted 0 of 2 commits, stopped: a.txt at #… (it overlaps or touches a change the parent made)". Control: the branch doing `5 → FIVE` in one commit → "already done here". The file then stays stopped for good (later branch commits to it are never adopted).

The same breaks two promises built on it:
- **T-125, rerun of an interrupted merge.** Branch: the two-step edit plus a g.txt edit. `LAP_TEST_MERGE_FAIL_AFTER=2 lap merge b`, commit another file, `lap merge b` → "adopted 1 of 3 commits, stopped: a.txt" although its commits are in the log. SPEC says they "come out already done".
- **T-157, a nested branch merged by two routes** (b2→b1, b2→main, then b1): stops a.txt at b1's copy; b1 stays "partly merged". (Audit repro; same mechanism, not re-run by hand.)
- Also from the audit, confirmed only by reading: a chain merge interrupted between its two merge records reruns as "adopted 0, left 2, stopped", because the outer merge record has no `from` and `merge_redo_point` (`cmd_merge.c:76-89`) reads it as other work.

**Cause.** `adopt.c:103-121` compares one commit with the parent's net hunk (`ch[hit].len == c->old_lines`, same delta, same text).

**Fix.** Treat a run of branch commits whose combined effect on the region equals the parent's change as already done (compare the branch's text after each commit with the parent's text in that region, not the single commit's hunk); make the redo point skip this run's own merge records.

**Done when:** e2e: the flat two-step case, the rerun case and the nested two-route case end with everything "already done", no stop, status clean; unit tests in the adopt suite for multi-commit identical changes, including a partial match (only the first step identical → still a conflict).

item.title: A torn first line in a fresh open chunk is repaired, not taken for a broken chain
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced).** A crash during the first append after a seal (branch start, the 4 MB limit, a merge rolling chunks) leaves the new open chunk holding only a torn line. Every writer then refuses; only hand editing gets out.

```
lap init; commit; cp -R . ../b; cd ../b; lap branch start b --from ../main   # main.000002 is now empty
cd main; printf '{"type":"commit","id":"L9' >> .lap/log/main.000002.jsonl
lap verify     → chain ok: 3 records; note: torn trailing record ignored … the next commit repairs it
lap commit …   → error: main.000002.jsonl does not continue main.000001.jsonl: the hash chain is broken there
```

Control: the same torn line after complete records in a chunk is cut and the commit goes on ("repaired torn log tail").

**Cause.** `hist.c:835-851`: the chain check between chunks reads the open chunk's first record; `chunk_first_record` fails on a chunk with no complete record, and that failure is reported as a broken chain before the torn-tail repair runs.

**Fix.** In the open chunk, a chunk with no complete line is an empty chunk with a torn tail: skip the boundary check for it and let the writer truncate it under the lock.

**Done when:** e2e: the repro commits, the torn bytes are gone, `verify` ok; a torn line in a *sealed* chunk is still refused (T-131 stays green).

item.title: Converting an old log keeps git seeing the history: .lap/.gitignore written, an old root pattern named
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced).** A repository whose root `.gitignore` uses the pattern the docs gave before chunks —

```
.lap/*
!.lap/log.jsonl
```

— (typec has it, line 54; this repo had it until T-105) loses its history from git at conversion:

```
lap commit a.txt …   → lap: moved .lap/log.jsonl into 1 chunk in .lap/log/
git status --short   →  D .lap/log.jsonl       (the chunks do not appear)
git check-ignore -v .lap/log/main.000001.jsonl   → .gitignore:1:.lap/*
```

Committing that deletes the history from git and never adds the chunks. Nothing warns. SPEC says "git sees one deleted file and some new ones".

Related (from the same check): `.lap/.gitignore` is written only by `lap init` and `branch start` (`cmd_branch.c:327`, and `:332` in the parent), never on opening or converting an older repository.

**Fix.** At conversion, write lap's standard `.lap/.gitignore` (`/*`, `!/.gitignore`, `!/log/`) when there is none — tested by the audit: with it, git shows `.lap/log/` as untracked — and, if `.lap/log/` still resolves as ignored (a root pattern like the one above re-includes only `log.jsonl`), print a warning naming the file and line to change. Say it in the README's upgrade note.

**Done when:** e2e: a repo with the old root pattern converts and `git status` lists `.lap/log/` (or the warning is printed where a root rule still wins); unit test for writing `.lap/.gitignore` on conversion only when absent.

item.title: Converting an old log keeps git seeing the history: conversion writes .lap/.gitignore
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced).** A repository whose root `.gitignore` uses the pattern the docs gave before chunks —

```
.lap/*
!.lap/log.jsonl
```

— (typec has it, line 54; this repo had it until T-105) loses its history from git at conversion:

```
lap commit a.txt …   → lap: moved .lap/log.jsonl into 1 chunk in .lap/log/
git status --short   →  D .lap/log.jsonl       (the chunks do not appear)
git check-ignore -v .lap/log/main.000001.jsonl   → .gitignore:1:.lap/*
```

Committing that deletes the history from git and never adds the chunks. Nothing warns. SPEC says "git sees one deleted file and some new ones".

**Cause.** `.lap/.gitignore` is written only by `lap init` and `branch start` (`cmd_branch.c:327`, and `:332` in the parent), never when an older repository is opened or converted (`hist.c:542-674`, called from `repo.c:436-442`).

**Fix.** The conversion writes lap's standard `.lap/.gitignore` (`/*`, `!/.gitignore`, `!/log/`) when there is none. A root `.lap/*` ignores `.lap`'s children, not `.lap` itself, so git reads that file and its `!/log/` re-includes the chunks (the audit tested it: `.lap/log/` then shows as untracked). lap never runs git, so it does not check what git ignores; the conversion message says to commit `.lap/.gitignore` and `.lap/log/` with the removal of `log.jsonl`. The README's upgrade note says the same.

**Done when:** e2e: a repo with the old root pattern converts, `.lap/.gitignore` exists, and `git status` (run by the test, not lap) lists `.lap/.gitignore` and `.lap/log/`; an existing `.lap/.gitignore` is left as it is; unit test for the write-only-when-absent rule.

item.title: A branch name is unique across nested branches, as seen from main
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced, git worktrees).** From main start `b1` and a top-level `x`; from b1's folder start a nested branch also named `x`. It is accepted.

```
main: lap branch list
b1  active …/b1
x   active …/x
  x active …/xn  (from b1)
```

From main, `lap log --branch x` reads the top-level x silently (a commit made in the nested one is not there; it is readable only by its id). The audit also saw `rr x/S1` and `merge x --dry-run` take the top-level one, and coboard's `ticketSessions` run `--branch x` for both rows, reading the same branch twice.

SPEC §Naming sessions: "a branch name names one branch for good", and readers resolve nested names from main.

**Cause.** The `name_taken` check (`cmd_branch.c:257-280`) sees only the parent branch's registry, chunks and merge records.

**Fix.** At start, check the name against every branch main can see: walk up to the top folder through `.lap/parent`, then its registry and down nested registries (as readers do), plus chunk-only and merged names. Where two already share a name (made before the fix), readers refuse with `ambiguous_branch` listing the ids, rather than picking one.

**Done when:** e2e: the nested `x` is refused with `name_taken`; a pre-existing duplicate gives `ambiguous_branch` for `log --branch x`; coboard reads each branch by id when names repeat; unit tests for the name walk.

item.title: A plain copy of a branch folder is not that branch: two folders never write one lineage
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced).** A `cp -R` of a branch folder keeps `.lap/lineage` and `.lap/parent`, so the copy *is* that branch:

```
cp -R main b1; cd b1; lap branch start b1 --from ../main
cp -R b1 x2; cd x2
lap branch start x --from ../b1   → error: … is already branch d02033661320; a folder starts one branch
lap commit a.txt … --branch b1    → [L3 …] recorded, into d02033661320.000001.jsonl — the same chunk b1 writes
```

Two folders then append to one lineage's open chunk: diverging copies of the same file name, a git conflict (or a broken chain) as soon as both reach git. And the SPEC's "a branch of a branch starts from a branch folder the same way" (SPEC:352) fails in copy mode with no way out but deleting `.lap/lineage` by hand.

**Cause.** `cmd_branch.c:151` trusts `.lap/lineage`. A copied registry is detected and dropped (`:346-353`), a copied lineage is not, though the parent's registry puts that branch at another path.

**Fix.** A folder whose `.lap/lineage` names a branch that its parent's registry places at a different, existing folder is a copy: `branch start` treats it as a folder copied from that branch (its lineage file dropped, like the registry), and writers refuse to record there with a clear code (e.g. `copied_branch`) naming both folders.

**Done when:** e2e: nested branch start from a copy succeeds; a commit in an un-started copy is refused and writes nothing; a moved branch (old path gone, `branch move` not run yet) is still that branch; unit tests for the copy decision.

item.title: A lineage leaked through git is ignored in any folder that is not that branch, not only its parent
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced).** T-130 ignores a leaked `.lap/lineage` only in the folder its `.lap/parent` names. A clone of that folder trusts it:

```
wt (branch feat of main): git add -f .lap/lineage .lap/parent; git commit
main: git merge feat     → main keeps main, with the T-130 note (as designed)
git clone main clone; cd clone
lap session start "…" --branch main   → error: this folder (…/clone) records to feat, not main
```

No note; the clone would write feat's lineage. It needs a forced `git add -f` past `.lap/.gitignore`, or a repo that tracked `.lap/` before T-130 — hence medium, not high.

**Cause.** `hist.c:700-727` fires only when `.lap/parent` resolves to this very folder.

**Fix.** Also ignore (with the same note) a lineage whose `.lap/parent`'s registry does not list this folder for it — a clone, a copy moved elsewhere — and a lineage whose parent folder is missing while this folder is a git checkout of the parent's history. Keep a moved branch working (`branch move` exists for it).

**Done when:** e2e: the clone repro records to main with the note; a real branch folder and a moved-then-`branch move`d one are unaffected; unit test for the decision table.

item.title: coboard's session start follows lap on a leaked lineage instead of passing it as --branch
item.description:
**Verified (code and lap run).** `branchArgs` (`packages/coboard/src/lap.ts:333-343`) returns `--branch <the id in .lap/lineage>` whenever the file exists. In a main folder where a lineage leaked through git (the T-130 case, which lap ignores with a note), that is `--branch 426557a1eb8f`, and lap answers:

```
error: this folder (…/main) records to main, not 426557a1eb8f: … pass --branch main
```

So the VS Code "start session" for a ticket fails in exactly the folder lap keeps as main.

**Fix.** Do not second-guess lap: ask it which line this folder records to (e.g. `lap session current --json` or `lap branch list --json` already carry it; add a small field if needed) and pass that, or pass nothing and let `LAP_BRANCH`-less lap decide where it can.

**Done when:** coboard test: in a leaked-lineage main folder, `startSession` succeeds on main; in a real branch folder it records to the branch; in a folder with branches it passes `--branch main`.

item.title: lap status and commit report unreadable files and folders, never as deleted or clean
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced).** The class of bug T-167 fixed for branch start, still in status and commit:

```
commit d/q.txt; chmod 000 d
lap status                         →  deleted   d/q.txt
lap commit d/q.txt … --dry-run     →  would record: delete d/q.txt
(the audit: branch start lists d/q.txt as "changed", not unreadable)

echo 11 >> a.txt; chmod 000 a.txt
lap status                         →  clean: working tree matches the last commit
```

A real commit would record the deletion of a file that is there.

**Cause.** `cmd_common.c:418` takes `plat_is_file` false (EACCES) as "no file"; `cmd_status.c:217-218` skips an unreadable file silently; `platform.c:710` skips an unreadable directory quietly.

**Fix.** Tell "absent" from "cannot read" (stat vs open/opendir errors). Status lists `unreadable <path>`; commit refuses such a file with `unreadable`; an unreadable directory makes its tracked files unreadable, not deleted.

**Done when:** e2e for both repros (status lists them as unreadable, commit refuses, nothing recorded); unit tests for the platform walk reporting unreadable directories.

item.title: lap merge keeps a change both sides made when the branch later undid its copy
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced).** git merges cleanly, nothing stops, yet lap's result differs from git's:

```
b:    insert X after line 5 (commit); delete X (commit)
main: insert the same X after line 5 (commit)
git merge b     → clean, X kept (from base to b nothing changed)
lap merge b     → adopted 1 of 2 commits (L4); already done here: #… (this folder made the same change)
lap status      → modified a.txt [1] line 6 (insertion)
```

lap takes the insertion as already done, then places the branch's deletion on main's X; the shadow lacks X, the file has it.

**Cause.** `adopt.c:103-121` marks the first commit already done and makes the region common ground; the placement at `125-167` then applies the revert.

**Decision needed in the fix:** git's rule is "a side that ends where it started changed nothing". The simplest faithful rule for lap: when the branch's net change to a region is none, its commits there are adopted as history (with `from`) but not applied, or the file stops. Pick one and state it in SPEC §Merging.

**Done when:** e2e: the repro ends with status clean (or a stop reported, per the decision), `verify --deep` ok; unit test in the adopt suite.

item.title: lap merge refuses a branch history holding records of a newer type, and verify names them in branches
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced).** T-164's rule — a writer never builds on records it does not understand — is not applied to the branch history `lap merge` reads:

```
b: commit; append a validly chained {"type":"annotate",…} (a newer lap's record)
b: lap commit …  → error: this history holds 1 record of a type this lap does not know … (correct)
git commit; main: git merge b; lap merge b
→ merged branch b (…): adopted 1 of 1 commit (L3), rc 0, no notice
main: lap verify → "chain ok: 5 records" / "branch b: chain ok: 6 records" — the unknown record not mentioned
```

The merge record's `head` is the unknown record, so it is never looked at again.

**Cause.** `cmd_merge.c:333` parses the branch stream, `685-686` skip unknown types, `713` takes the head. `cmd_verify.c`'s branch pass does not count unknown records; branch JSON has no `unknown_records`.

**Fix.** `lap merge` (and `--dry-run`) refuses with `newer_history` when the branch part it would adopt holds unknown records; `verify` reports them per branch (text note and `unknown_records` in each branch's JSON).

**Done when:** e2e: the repro refuses and writes nothing; verify names the record under branch b; unit test for the branch-part scan.

item.title: lap status with only log/ (a fresh clone) sees what it sees with caches
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced).** T-136 holds only while the shadow store is there. With `.lap/` holding only `log/` — exactly what a `git clone` gives — status misses deletions and edits of files ignored after they were recorded:

```
commit a.txt, b.txt, ig/c.txt; rm b.txt; add ig/ to .lapignore; edit ig/c.txt; commit .lapignore
lap status                      → deleted b.txt; modified ig/c.txt
(.lap/index moved away)         → same (T-136 works)
(.lap/shadow moved away too)    → clean: working tree matches the last commit
```

On a typec clone with every cache removed, status omits `modified .coboard/log.jsonl` (committed at L52, ignored later). The cache contract (SPEC:59-62): deleting any cache changes speed only.

**Cause.** `cmd_status.c:138-145`: with no index, the tracked set comes from walking `.lap/shadow`, never from the log.

**Fix.** When the index is missing or not ready, rebuild it (or derive the tracked set from the log) before status compares — status already reads the log to heal state. A missing shadow for a tracked file is rebuilt from the history.

**Done when:** e2e: the repro gives the same output in all three states and in a fresh `git clone`; the "byte-identical with and without caches" test covers status with only `log/`.

item.title: Writers refuse a hash chain broken inside a chunk, not only between chunks
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced).**

```
duplicate the last line of the open chunk (a union-style git resolution does this)
lap verify     → CHAIN BROKEN: hash chain broken at main.000001.jsonl line 4 (record L2)
lap commit …   → [L3 …] recorded, rc 0
lap verify     → still CHAIN BROKEN
```

The writer builds on a history verify rejects, and the damage grows with every record. SPEC:1022 limits the writer's refusal to breaks between chunks; T-131 and the SPEC also say "lap never builds on a history it cannot vouch for".

**Cause.** `hist.c:814-856` checks only each chunk's first record against the previous chunk; `repo.c:458` then opens for writing.

**Fix.** Writers check the open chunk's chain (it is small, at most 4 MB, and the index's last covered hash lets them start there — T-166) and refuse with `history_broken`, naming the line, as verify does. Sealed chunks stay checked at their boundary only (verify covers them).

**Done when:** e2e: the repro's commit is refused and writes nothing; commit speed on a 4 MB open chunk measured before/after (stated in the ticket's comment); SPEC:1022 updated.

item.title: verify --deep checks the index instead of trusting it
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced).** SPEC:932: "Verification never uses the caches it is checking". Since T-170, `--deep` replays file by file along the index's chains and never checks the index itself:

```
set a.txt's entry in .lap/heads to -1; move .lap/shadow/a.txt away
lap verify --deep   → deep check: 1 file, 0 mismatches, rc 0
(.lap/index moved away)
lap verify --deep   → missing shadow: a.txt — deep check: 2 files, 1 mismatch
```

On an untouched typec clone the two agree; the gap is only that a damaged index hides damage.

**Cause.** `cmd_verify.c:365` takes `idx_ready` and `deep_indexed` (`231-322`) walks `idx->paths` and the heads chains as given.

**Fix.** Keep the per-file replay (T-170's bounded memory) but check the index while doing it: the set of files and each file's chain are rebuilt from one streaming pass over the log (paths and record offsets only) and compared with the index; any difference is a mismatch ("index: …"). Or fall back to the whole-log replay when the index disagrees.

**Done when:** e2e: the repro fails with the index present, naming the index; memory on the typec clone stays near T-170's 26 MB; the no-index path unchanged.

item.title: A nested branch merged straight into main counts as merged there
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced).** b1 from main, b2 from b1; b2 commits; main: `git merge b2`, `lap merge b2` → adopted 1 of 1.

```
main: lap branch list --json   → b2 state "active", merged null
(b2's folder removed)
main: lap branch list          → b2 missing (gone) (from b1) — "tend it from b1's folder"
```

It is never pruned, and reads as unmerged work that is lost. This follows SPEC:632-633 (a nested branch "judges its state against that branch's history", b1's, where no merge of b2 is recorded), which contradicts the registry rule (SPEC:427-433 and §Registry: merged-and-gone is pruned silently).

**Cause.** `cmd_branch.c:570-580` judge a nested branch only against its parent branch's merge records.

**Fix.** A nested branch is merged when its head is adopted into the folder listing it *or* any folder above that main can see (this folder's own merge records count). State that in SPEC, replacing the "judged against that branch's history" sentence.

**Done when:** e2e: after the straight merge b2 lists as merged in main (and in b1 once b1 merges main? — no: b1 still shows it active until b1 adopts it, say so); with its folder gone it is pruned; unit test for the state rule.

item.title: --copy-from-folder never rewrites a branch chunk git brought
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced).**

```
b: commit B1; git commit; commit B2 (not in git)
main: git merge b (brings b's chunk with B1); lap merge b --copy-from-folder
→ adopted 2 of 2 commits
git status --short .lap →  M .lap/log/<b>.000001.jsonl
```

The chunk git brought was extended with B2 from the folder. SPEC:441-443: "lap never rewrites a copy git brought, so the next `git merge` finds that file unchanged on this side and never conflicts on `.lap/log/`". Here the next `git merge` did not conflict only because b's side then held the same bytes; any difference (b sealed at another point, amended, crashed mid-append) conflicts.

**Cause.** `--copy-from-folder` copies the folder's chunks over whatever is here, including chunks git brought (T-127's "never overwrites a present branch chunk" is bypassed by the flag).

**Fix.** With `--copy-from-folder`, copy only chunks absent here; for a present chunk shorter than the folder's, adopt up to what is here and say that the rest comes with the next `git merge` (or refuse `git_merge_first` for that part). Update SPEC §Merging's flag description.

**Done when:** e2e: the repro leaves the git-brought chunk byte-identical; the SPEC's claim holds; the existing `--copy-from-folder` tests still pass.

item.title: A nested branch merged straight into main counts as merged there
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced).** b1 from main, b2 from b1; b2 commits; main: `git merge b2`, `lap merge b2` → adopted 1 of 1.

```
main: lap branch list --json   → b2 state "active", merged null
(b2's folder removed)
main: lap branch list          → b2 missing (gone) (from b1) — "tend it from b1's folder"
```

It is never pruned, and reads as unmerged work that is lost. This follows SPEC:632-633 (a nested branch "judges its state against that branch's history", b1's, where no merge of b2 is recorded), which contradicts the registry rule (SPEC:427-433 and §Registry: merged-and-gone is pruned silently).

**Cause.** `cmd_branch.c:570-580` judge a nested branch only against its parent branch's merge records.

**Fix.** A nested branch is merged, as listed from a folder, when its head is adopted into that folder or into the branch it started from. State that in SPEC, replacing the "judged against that branch's history" sentence. b1's own list keeps showing b2 active until b1 adopts it (b1 has not got that work).

**Done when:** e2e: after the straight merge, main lists b2 as merged; with b2's folder gone it is pruned from main's view without a word; b1's list still shows it active; unit test for the state rule.

item.title: verify reports a branch whose first chunk is missing, instead of leaving it out
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced, in part).** With `LAP_TEST_CHUNK_BYTES=500`, branch b writes chunks 000001–000005; main `git merge b`; then `<b>.000001.jsonl` is removed in main and b's folder is gone:

```
main: lap verify --json   → {"ok":true,"records":3,"chain_ok":true,"branches":[]}
```

A branch with four chunks here is silently left out. SPEC:274-278: every command refuses a history it cannot open whole — a chunk missing — with `history_broken`.

Part of the audit's claim did **not** hold: `lap log --branch b` does name the problem ("the history of … starts nowhere: …000001.jsonl is missing or empty"), it is not `unknown_branch`.

**Cause.** verify's branch pass lists branches by their first chunk; lineages with chunks but no chunk 1 are never visited.

**Fix.** verify lists every lineage with any chunk here and reports one without chunk 1 (or with a gap) as broken, naming the chunk; `ok:false`.

**Done when:** e2e: the repro fails verify naming `<b>.000001.jsonl`; unit test for the lineage listing.

item.title: Docs say which files in .lap/ are machine-local state, and rebuild notices a branch folder that lost its lineage
item.description:
**Verified.** SPEC:59-60 ("everything in `.lap/` except `log/` is a derived, disposable cache. Any of it may be deleted at any time"), the lap README:207 and the lap skill:241-244 say the same. But `.lap/lineage`, `.lap/parent` and `.lap/branches.json` are not derived from the log.

What deleting `.lap/lineage` does in a branch folder (reproduced):

```
b1 (branch, chunks ed347e15c334.000001-2): mv .lap/lineage away
lap rebuild   → rebuilt all caches from 3 records (chain ok)      — main's 3 records only
lap commit …  → "this folder has branches: … --branch main"       — it now takes itself for main
```

Following the docs turns a branch into main without a word; its own chunks are ignored.

**Fix.**
- SPEC, README and skill: the cache contract names the exceptions — `lineage`, `parent` and `branches.json` are machine-local state (never committed, not rebuilt), with what losing each means.
- `lap rebuild` (and writers) notice a folder that holds another lineage's chunks whose first record is a branch record started from this folder's history, with no `.lap/lineage`: a warning naming the lineage and how to restore the file.

**Done when:** docs updated in all three places; e2e: the repro's rebuild prints the warning; unit test for the detection.

item.title: Stop tracking files ignored after they were recorded (and untrack the vendored sources here)
item.description:
**Verified.** T-154 added `cli/kb-cli/src/third_party/tree-sitter*/` and `utf8proc/` to `.lapignore`, but files lap recorded before stay tracked (by design: `cmd_status.c:57-59`, "ignored since it was tracked"). In this repository: 108 vendored paths in the history, 109 files and 38 MB under `.lap/shadow/cli/kb-cli/src/third_party/`, carried by every status and rebuild. Neither the SPEC, the README nor the skill says how to stop tracking a file.

**Fix.** A way to untrack without rewriting history, e.g. `lap untrack <path>…` appending an `untrack` record (older laps skip it with the T-164 notice; writers of older laps refuse — say so), after which the path is ignored-and-untracked: status drops it, its shadow is removed, `log`/`show`/blame keep its history. Document it where `.lapignore` is explained. Then untrack the vendored sources here (its own board ticket loop: lap session, git commit).

**Decision needed:** a new record type (above) vs. treating "ignored + deleted-from-disk" as untracked (no new record, but then status must not show the deletion). The record is explicit; prefer it.

**Done when:** e2e: untrack a recorded file → status no longer lists it, shadow gone, `lap log --file` still shows its commits, verify ok; docs updated; this repo's shadow for `third_party/` is gone.

item.title: Lap History retries lap after a failure, and when lap.path changes
item.description:
**Verified (code).** In `packages/lap-vscode/src/extension.ts`, `BranchSource.refresh` stores the new signature (`this.signature = sig`) *before* `lap branch list` answers. When lap fails (not found, wrong `lap.path`, an older lap), the signature already matches, so the list is not asked again until something on disk changes. Nothing listens for configuration changes (no `onDidChangeConfiguration`), and the `lap.refresh` command (line ~732) refreshes the tree and the page but never calls `branches.refresh(true)`.

So after fixing `lap.path`, branches stay empty and the error stays until a commit happens somewhere.

**Fix.** Store the signature only when lap answered; on `lap.path`/`coboard.lapPath` changes and on `lap.refresh`, call `branches.refresh(true)` (and re-read the main log's problem state).

**Done when:** unit test with a fake exec: a failed list is retried on the next refresh; a configuration change and `lap.refresh` force it.

item.title: Lap History names a broken branch history: a missing first chunk, a gap, a nested branch's missing middle
item.description:
**Verified (code).** T-133 names a missing chunk only in some cases (`packages/lap-vscode/src/chunks.ts`):

- `historyProblem` (`65-84`) checks this folder's own lineage and main only. In a nested branch folder, the middle lineage (the branch it started from) is never checked.
- `missingChunk` (`45-60`) returns null when a lineage has no chunk 1 at all (its highest number counts from 0), so a branch whose first chunk is gone is "fine".
- Branch rows read `ownFiles` → `lineageChunks` (`35-44`, `230-247`), which stops quietly at the first gap: the row shows part of the branch's history with no error.

The CLI refuses all these with `history_broken` (SPEC:274-278); the view shows an empty or partial history instead.

**Fix.** One check, used by the folder's history and by each branch row: every lineage in the chain (own, each ancestor branch, main) must run from chunk 1 without a gap and start with the expected record; otherwise the row or view shows the problem in lap's words, never part of the history.

**Done when:** unit tests for: missing chunk 1, a gap, a nested branch's missing middle chunk, each giving the named problem; a branch row with a gap shows an error, not partial sessions.

item.title: An open branch row in Lap History collapses only on Enter, ArrowLeft or a click
coboard reports a branch it could not read, instead of dropping its sessions
item.description:
**Verified (code, and lap's message by a run).** T-137 reports lap failures for this folder's sessions, not for branches:

- `packages/coboard/src/lap.ts:124-126`: a failed `session list --branch <name>` becomes `sessions: []` in a catch, with no error kept.
- `lap.ts:128`: a failed `lap branch list` is swallowed as "a lap from before branches".
- `mcp.ts:224`: `board_sessions` keeps only `sessionCommits(…).value`, so a failed commit read becomes `commits: []`.

So `board_get`/`board_sessions` show a ticket with fewer sessions or commits and no `lapError`. The lap message for a registered branch whose `.lap/log` is unreadable (chmod 000) is also misleading: "the history of … starts nowhere: …000001.jsonl is missing or empty" — the chunk is there, just unreadable (the audit's "`unknown_branch`" did not reproduce; the message is this one).

**Fix.** Collect per-branch and per-session failures into `lapError` (naming the branch or session); lap says "cannot read" (with the OS reason) when a chunk exists but cannot be opened.

**Done when:** coboard tests: an unreadable branch log gives `lapError` naming the branch, and a failed commit read gives one too; lap e2e: the unreadable-chunk message names the permission problem.

item.title: Merging a branch with no commits records the merge
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced).**

```
worktree one; lap branch start one; git commit
main: git merge one; lap merge one   → "branch one: nothing new to adopt since the last merge"  (there was no earlier merge)
(no merge record written)
remove one's worktree
lap branch list                      → one  missing (gone) — "lap branch move … or lap branch forget …"
lap session start "…"                → this folder has branches: … --branch main
```

A branch started and abandoned without work shows as missing for good, and main keeps requiring `--branch` until `branch forget`.

**Fix.** A merge of a branch whose head is past its base only by its branch record (and sessions, if any) writes a merge record (adopted 0) so it counts as merged; the message says "nothing to adopt: it has no commits".

**Done when:** e2e: the repro prints the new message, the branch lists as merged, and once its folder is gone it is pruned and main no longer needs `--branch`.

item.title: An empty flag value is refused as a missing one
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced).** T-147 refuses a missing value ("needs a value"); an empty one passes:

```
lap log -n ""             → no commits yet            (the repo has commits)
lap session list --meta=  → every session, unfiltered
lap log --branch=         → error: no branch  here: not in this folder's registry …
```

(The audit also saw `--branch=` on session start give `wrong_branch "… not :"`.)

**Fix.** The shared flag parser treats `""` like a missing value for every flag that takes one (`bad_args`, "--x needs a value").

**Done when:** unit tests in the flag parser for `--x=`, `--x ""` and `-n ""`; e2e for the three lines above.

item.title: A branch folder inside its parent's folder is refused, or ignored by the parent
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced).** Tools put worktrees inside the repository (Claude Code's `.claude/worktrees/`, `git worktree add sub`). lap accepts that, and the parent then sees every branch file as its own:

```
main: git worktree add sub -b sub; cd sub; lap branch start sub --from ..
main: lap status   → new sub/.lapignore (6 lines), new sub/a.txt (10 lines)
```

A parent commit of those would record the branch's files into main's history.

**Decision needed:** refuse such a start (`nested_folder`, telling to put the worktree outside, or add it to `.lapignore` first), or have the parent's walk skip any subfolder holding its own `.lap/` (as git skips nested repositories). Skipping is friendlier and matches git; recommend it.

**Done when:** e2e: after starting a branch in `main/sub`, main's `lap status` does not list `sub/…`; SPEC §Branches says so.

item.title: "Already done" requires the same final newline
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced).** b changes the last line `10` to `TEN` keeping the final newline; main changes it to `TEN` with no final newline. git conflicts; resolved keeping main's side; then:

```
lap merge b   → adopted 0 of 1 commit; already done here: #… (this folder made the same change)
```

T-158/SPEC: already done means the same text *and* the same final newline.

**Cause.** `adopt.c:108-109`: `(c->eof_nl == branch.eof_nl || c->eof_nl == merged.eof_nl)` accepts either.

**Fix.** Require the commit's final newline to equal the parent's (`merged.eof_nl`) when the change touches the last line; otherwise it is a conflict.

**Done when:** adopt unit test for the case (conflict), and one where the newline matches (already done).

item.title: lap amend says not_a_commit for a session or amendment, as the SPEC does
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced).** SPEC:853 lists `not_a_commit` ("the reference names another record"). It can never be emitted:

```
lap amend <a session_start record's hash> … --json → {"error":"unknown_ref","message":"no commit has a hash starting cf94a79c0f90"}
lap amend S1 … --json                              → {"error":"unknown_ref","message":"S1 is not a commit: …"}
```

**Cause.** `ref_find` (`cmd_common.c:244-290`) resolves only commits, so the `c->type != REC_COMMIT` branch in `cmd_amend.c:50-53` is dead code.

**Fix.** Let `ref_find` resolve a hash to any record (reporting its type) and have amend refuse non-commits with `not_a_commit`; `S<n>` given to amend gives `not_a_commit` too. Or drop the code from the SPEC and the dead branch — choose one; the first matches the SPEC.

**Done when:** e2e for both lines above giving `not_a_commit`.

item.title: Leftovers outside .lap/log are cleared too: chunk temps in .lap/, shadow temps, log.replaced
item.description:
**Verified (code; the audit reproduced each by a crash or a hand-built state).**

- `hist_clear_tmp` (`hist.c:745-759`, called from `repo.c:442`) walks only `.lap/log/`. But since T-142 chunk temps are written in `.lap/` itself (`hist.c:741`, `tmpdir = .lap`), e.g. `.lap/main.000130.jsonl.tmp.4243`, and shadow temps next to their file (`platform.c:583-585`, e.g. `.lap/shadow/f04.txt.tmp.<pid>`, left by a merge killed during the shadow update — 3 of 40 kill trials). Neither the heal nor `lap rebuild` removes them.
- `hist_convert_legacy` returns early when the conversion already finished (`hist.c:572-577`) or when there is no `log.jsonl` (`547-548`), before clearing `log.replaced/` and `log.converting/`; a crash after publishing leaves `log.replaced/` for good.

Records, verify and status are unaffected; it is disk litter (a shadow temp can be megabytes).

**Fix.** Under the lock, writers clear `*.tmp.<pid>` names directly in `.lap/` and in the shadow tree (whose pid is not alive, or all of them — writers hold the lock), and `log.replaced/`/`log.converting/` whenever `log/` is complete; rebuild does the same.

**Done when:** e2e: hand-made leftovers of each kind are gone after one commit and after `lap rebuild`.

item.title: branch start reports why the parent could not be opened, with its own code
item.description:
**Verified (code).** `cmd_branch.c:175-177`:

```c
if (!repo_open_at(a, &pr, there, true, err, sizeof err)) {
    err_out(json, "no_parent", "%s", err);
```

Every failure to open the parent — `newer_history`, `history_broken`, a lock it cannot take — is reported as `no_parent` with another failure's message (the audit: a parent with a newer history gives `no_parent` carrying the `newer_history` text).

**Fix.** Use `repo_error_code()` (as other commands do) and keep `no_parent` for "no lap repository there".

**Done when:** e2e: a parent with an unknown record type gives `newer_history`; a missing parent still gives `no_parent`.

item.title: The newer-history check trusts the index only as far as its last covered hash
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced).** `newer_check` (`repo.c:356-360`) takes the index header's unknown-record count and `covered` whenever `covered <= size`, without T-166's check of the last covered record's hash (`idx_ready`/`tail_matches`, `idx.c:115-128`).

```
session start; commit; lap status (index built)
replace the last record with a validly chained {"type":"future_op",…} of the same length
lap session end   → note: this history has records of a newer type … ; session S1 ended, rc 0 — session_end appended after future_op
(.lap/index moved away) → error: this history holds 1 record of a type this lap does not know ("future_op") … (correct)
```

Low: it needs a record rewritten in place at the same size; a newer lap appends, and appended bytes are past `covered`, so they are scanned.

**Fix.** Trust the header only when the tail check passes (`idx_ready`-style); otherwise scan from 0.

**Done when:** e2e: the repro refuses with `newer_history` with the index present.

item.title: A reader racing a conversion's publish never sees "no history"
item.description:
**Verified (code; the audit hit it with a pause added in a scratch build — unmodified stress runs were clean).** `hist_open` (`hist.c:119-127`):

1. `list_chunks` finds no chunks in `.lap/log/` (not published yet);
2. the conversion renames `log.converting` → `log/` and removes `log.jsonl`;
3. `plat_file_size(legacy)` fails → `return true` with zero chunks.

The reader gets an empty history: `lap verify --json` → `{"ok":false,"error":"history_broken","message":"no history in …/.lap/log (expected log/main.000001.jsonl)"}`. The later path at `hist.c:152-155` already re-lists the chunks when the old file vanished; this one does not.

**Fix.** When the legacy file is gone and no chunk was found, list the chunks again before returning.

**Done when:** unit test with an injected step between the two checks (a test hook) showing the second listing is used.

item.title: verify reports an old log.jsonl that differs from the chunks beside it
item.description:
**Verified (code; the audit reproduced it).** When a `log.jsonl` comes back next to converted chunks and the chunks do not hold all of it (e.g. restored from a backup with one different record), readers read the old file silently (`hist.c:141-146`, per SPEC), writers refuse ("both … hold history, and they differ", `hist.c:579-586`) — but `lap verify` says `ok:true` over the old file's records, and `session list` misses what the chunks hold (S3 in the audit's run).

**Fix.** verify (and the reader notice) says both shapes are present and differ, naming both, with `ok:false` — what the writer refuses, verify reports.

**Done when:** e2e: the repro fails verify with that message; the "conversion finished, old file left" case (chunks hold all of it) stays ok.

item.title: Broken-history messages name the chunk and blame it the same way everywhere
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced with `LAP_TEST_CHUNK_BYTES=400`).**

- A sealed chunk reduced to a blank line (main.000003): verify → "chunk main.000004 does not continue sealed chunk main.000003"; a writer → "main.000003 does not continue main.000002". Two different blames for one fault.
- A sealed chunk emptied (main.000003): verify → "main.000004 does not continue sealed chunk main.000002" — chunk 3 is never named.
- A malformed record met by a reader's in-memory heal is named "log line %d" (`repo.c:200`), not chunk and line.
- (From the audit, same family) verify on an unknown record with a bad `prev` says "(record init)"; an edited sealed branch chunk is reported two ways.
- `lap merge` of amendments only prints "adopted 0 of 0 commits" before "amendments carried: 1".

**Fix.** One blame rule (the first chunk whose content is wrong: empty/blank/torn sealed chunk → that chunk) used by verify and writers; chunk-and-line in every message; merge says "no commits to adopt; amendments carried: n".

**Done when:** e2e for the blank and emptied chunk (both commands name main.000003) and the heal message; merge message test.

item.title: On macOS, durability uses F_FULLFSYNC
item.description:
**Verified (code).** `platform.c:485, 500, 601, 640` call plain `fsync`. On macOS, `fsync` hands data to the drive but does not flush the drive's cache; only `fcntl(fd, F_FULLFSYNC)` does (SQLite's `fullfsync` pragma exists for this). So T-165's power-loss ordering (a chunk and its directory entry durable before the next write) holds on Linux but is weaker on macOS, the platform lap is developed on.

**Fix.** On `__APPLE__`, `plat_fsync` and the directory fsync try `F_FULLFSYNC` first and fall back to `fsync` when it fails (some filesystems refuse it).

**Done when:** builds on macOS and Linux; a unit test that the call succeeds on a regular file in TMPDIR; commit timing on macOS measured before/after and stated in the comment (F_FULLFSYNC is slower; if it is too slow for per-commit use, keep it for seals and conversions only and say so).

item.title: Lap History in a branch folder does not run lap branch list on every commit
item.description:
**Verified (code).** `listSignature` (`packages/lap-vscode/src/extension.ts:188-213`) includes every non-`main` chunk with its size. In a branch folder the folder's *own* lineage is not `main`, so each commit changes the signature and spawns `lap branch list --json`. The per-branch watchers (`286-292`) also force a refresh on every change. And `refresh` has no in-flight guard: two lists can run at once and the older answer can land last, overwriting the newer views.

**Fix.** Leave this folder's own lineage out of the signature (the list does not depend on it); keep one list in flight and drop answers older than the latest request.

**Done when:** unit test: committing in a branch folder does not change the signature; two overlapping refreshes apply only the newer answer.

item.title: Lap History tends a missing nested branch in its parent branch's folder, and notices a deleted branch folder
item.description:
**Verified (code).**

- **Move/Forget for a nested branch.** The buttons (`webview/history.tsx:443-455`) send only the name, and the extension runs `lap branch move|forget` in the workspace root (`extension.ts:~400-415`, `cwd: root`). A nested branch is tended in the folder of the branch it started from (SPEC:634; lap itself says "tend it from b1's folder"), so from the root lap answers `unknown_branch`.
- **A deleted branch folder is not noticed.** The watchers (`extension.ts:280-292`) listen to `onDidChange` and `onDidCreate` only; removing a branch folder leaves the row "active" until something else changes.

**Fix.** Send the branch's `via` (or its parent folder) with the message and run lap there; add `onDidDelete` to the watchers.

**Done when:** unit tests: the fix message for a nested row runs in the parent branch's folder; a delete event triggers a refresh.

item.title: lap branch list indents a nested branch under the branch it started from
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced).** main has `b1` and `x`; a nested `x` starts from b1. `lap branch list` in main prints:

```
b1   active …/b1
x    active …/x
  x  active …/xn  (from b1)
```

The nested one is indented under the top-level `x`, not under `b1` — it follows the registry's order (`cmd_branch.c:566`), not its parent. With T-176 the names will differ, but the placement is still wrong for any order.

**Fix.** Print each nested branch right after the branch it started from (by `via`), recursively.

**Done when:** e2e: a nested branch started after another top-level branch prints under its parent.

item.title: SPEC names every error code and JSON field lap emits; merge says history_broken
item.description:
**Verified.**

- **Error codes.** Of 56 codes passed to `err_out` in `cli/lap-cli/src`, 25 appear nowhere in SPEC.md: `append_failed bad_args bad_edit_index bad_line bad_lineage bad_lines bad_meta bad_path chain_broken empty_range init_failed io_error lines_mismatch log_unreadable message_required no_active_session no_session no_target read_failed rebuild_failed replay_failed session_active shadow_failed state_failed unknown_file`. (The audit also found merge's list omitting `parent_read_only`/`log_unreadable`, and amend's `branch_required`/`wrong_branch`.)
- **Two names for one thing.** `lap merge` reports a broken history as `log_broken` (`cmd_merge.c:258, 357, 373`); every other command says `history_broken`.
- **JSON fields.** `verify --deep --json` returns `deep_checked`, `deep_mismatched`, `mismatched_files`, none in the SPEC. The audit listed more (session start `ref`, `rr`'s top level, the chain merge's combined JSON); SPEC:575 does document `ref` for sessions. (Its claim of a `root` field in `status --json` did not reproduce.)

**Fix.** An error-code table in the SPEC (code, commands, meaning), generated or checked by a test that greps `err_out` codes against it; merge uses `history_broken`; the JSON of each command listed where the command is described.

**Done when:** the test fails when a code is missing from the SPEC and passes now; merge's code changed (e2e updated).

item.title: Usage texts list --branch, and lap <cmd> --help prints the command's help
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced).**

```
lap commit          → error: usage: lap commit <file> (-i … | -F …) [--edit <n> | --lines <a>-<b>] [--force-message] [--no-session] [--dry-run] [--json]
                       — no --branch, which is required where branches exist
lap commit --help   → error: unknown flag --help
```

The audit found the same omission in the usage of amend, show and session (and session's lacking `-F`). `lap --help` itself is right (T-151).

**Fix.** Each command's usage line lists its flags as `lap --help` does (one table for both); `--help`/`-h` on any command prints that command's part of the help and exits 0.

**Done when:** e2e: `lap commit --help` prints commit's help rc 0; each usage error lists `--branch` where the command takes it.

item.title: Docs: amend with --branch, the real search output, Windows status, session list reads branches
item.description:
**Verified**, each by reading the file against lap's behaviour:

- **Amend in the skills** (`.claude/skills/lap/SKILL.md:96-113`, and the tickets skill line 42): the example has no `--branch`, but amend requires it wherever branches exist (`branch_required`), like commit.
- **The README's search example** (`cli/lap-cli/README.md:17-18`): shows `(2026-09-20T12:31:07Z)` and one line; lap prints `(2026-09-28 11:23:29)` followed by the commit's intent and behavior.
- **Windows** — `cli/lap-cli/README.md:353` says Windows builds with MSVC and runs the unit suite; SPEC:1042-1044 says the `_WIN32` branches are "best-effort and currently untested". One of them is out of date; say what is true (the unit suite runs; e2e does not).
- **SPEC:588** lists `log`, `show` and `rr` as taking `--branch`; `session list --branch` exists too (`lap --help` has it).

**Done when:** the four places match lap; the skill's amend example has `--branch <name>` with the rule when it is needed.

item.title: Usage texts list --branch, and lap <cmd> --help prints the command's help
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced).**

```
lap commit          → error: usage: lap commit <file> (-i … | -F …) [--edit <n> | --lines <a>-<b>] [--force-message] [--no-session] [--dry-run] [--json]
                       — no --branch, which is required where branches exist
lap commit --help   → error: unknown flag --help
```

The audit found the same omission in the usage of amend, show and session (and session's lacking `-F`). `lap --help` itself is right (T-151).

**Fix.** Each command's usage line lists its flags as `lap --help` does (one table for both); `--help`/`-h` on any command prints that command's part of the help and exits 0.

**Done when:** e2e: `lap commit --help` prints commit's help rc 0; each usage error lists `--branch` where the command takes it.

item.title: lap merge keeps a change both sides made when the branch later undid its copy
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced).** git merges cleanly, nothing stops, yet lap's result differs from git's:

```
b:    insert X after line 5 (commit); delete X (commit)
main: insert the same X after line 5 (commit)
git merge b     → clean, X kept (from base to b nothing changed)
lap merge b     → adopted 1 of 2 commits (L4); already done here: #… (this folder made the same change)
lap status      → modified a.txt [1] line 6 (insertion)
```

lap takes the insertion as already done, then places the branch's deletion on main's X; the shadow lacks X, the file has it.

**Cause.** `adopt.c:103-121` marks the first commit already done and sets the parent's change as used up (`ch[hit].len = -1`), so the region becomes common ground and the revert at `125-167` no longer touches a parent change.

**Decision (user, 2026-09-28): the undoing commit stops the file.** An "already done" commit leaves the parent's change counted: a later branch commit that overlaps or touches that region is a conflict, like any other overlap. Not chosen: adopting commits without applying them — it breaks "replaying the history rebuilds each file" (`verify --deep`) and would be a new kind of record meaning nothing.

With the stop, the reverting commit is not adopted; the shadow keeps main's X, which is git's result, and status is clean. Later branch commits to that file are left to commit by hand (the existing stop behaviour). No new concept, record or flag: a few lines in `adopt.c`. SPEC §Merging says that a change already done still counts as the parent's for the commits after it.

**Done when:** e2e: the repro reports `stopped: a.txt at #<the delete>`, status clean, `verify --deep` ok; adopt unit test for the case, and T-158's tests still green.

item.title: A folder with its own .lap/ inside the repository is skipped by the parent, as git skips nested repositories
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced).** Tools put worktrees inside the repository (Claude Code's `.claude/worktrees/`, `git worktree add sub`). lap accepts a branch there, and the parent then sees every branch file as its own:

```
main: git worktree add sub -b sub; cd sub; lap branch start sub --from ..
main: lap status   → new sub/.lapignore (6 lines), new sub/a.txt (10 lines)
```

A parent commit of those would record the branch's files into main's history.

**Decision (user, 2026-09-28): skip, do not refuse.** The folder walk that status and commit use does not descend into a subfolder holding its own `.lap/`. This is the downward half of the rule lap already has upward: every command works in the nearest `.lap/`, so files under `sub/` are recorded by sub's repository, never the parent's. It keeps `.claude/worktrees/` and `git worktree add sub` working, and covers an unrelated nested lap repository too. Not chosen: refusing such a branch start (it would block those layouts).

Files the parent recorded under that subfolder before it got its own `.lap/` stay tracked, like files ignored after they were recorded (no new rule).

**Done when:** e2e: after a branch starts in `main/sub`, main's `lap status` does not list `sub/…`, and `lap commit sub/a.txt` in main refuses it as outside this repository; unit test for the walk skipping a directory with `.lap/`; SPEC §Branches (and the folder-walk rule) say so.

item.title: Docs say .lapignore affects only files not yet recorded
item.description:
**Verified.** T-154 added `cli/kb-cli/src/third_party/tree-sitter*/` and `utf8proc/` to `.lapignore`, but files lap recorded before stay tracked (by design, T-136: `cmd_status.c:57-59`, so edits to a file ignored later are never lost silently). In this repository: 108 vendored paths in the history, 109 files and 38 MB under `.lap/shadow/cli/kb-cli/src/third_party/`. Neither the SPEC, the README nor the skill says that `.lapignore` does not stop tracking a recorded file.

**Decision (user, 2026-09-28): no `lap untrack`.** A new record type (to untrack without rewriting history) was considered and dropped: it touches replay, rebuild, the index's tracked set, status, verify --deep, merge (carrying untracks across branches), the views and the SPEC, and older laps would refuse to write to a repository holding one — too much for a small lap. What it would buy here is 38 MB of cache and a few stat checks the stat cache already makes cheap; the vendored files never change, so they never show as edits. Recording a delete instead was also dropped: a delete carries the whole old text (about 38 MB more log) and would claim the files were deleted.

**What this ticket does.** SPEC (the `.lapignore` section), the lap README and the lap skill say: `.lapignore` keeps lap from recording files it has not recorded yet; a file recorded before it was ignored stays tracked (its edits show in status); to shed tracked files for good, start a new history (rare, blunt, stated as such).

**Done when:** the three places say this in the same words; nothing in lap changes.

item.title: On macOS, a chunk's seal and a conversion use F_FULLFSYNC
item.description:
**Verified (code).** `platform.c:485, 500, 601, 640` call plain `fsync`. On macOS, `fsync` hands data to the drive but does not flush the drive's cache; only `fcntl(fd, F_FULLFSYNC)` does. So T-165's power-loss ordering holds on Linux but is weaker on macOS.

**Decision (user, 2026-09-28): minimal form.** `F_FULLFSYNC` only where a crash would cost history structure — sealing a chunk (and creating the next) and publishing a conversion — not on every commit's append, so commit speed is unchanged and there is nothing to measure. A per-commit full flush is a durability refinement lap can live without; an interrupted append is already handled as a torn tail.

**Fix.** One helper, `plat_fsync_full`, on `__APPLE__` `fcntl(F_FULLFSYNC)` falling back to `fsync` when refused, elsewhere `fsync`; used at the seal and conversion sites only.

**Done when:** builds on macOS and Linux; a unit test that the helper succeeds on a regular file in TMPDIR; the SPEC's durability note says which writes get the full flush.

item.title: SPEC lists every error code and JSON field lap emits; merge says history_broken
item.description:
**Verified.**

- **Error codes.** Of 56 codes passed to `err_out` in `cli/lap-cli/src`, 25 appear nowhere in SPEC.md: `append_failed bad_args bad_edit_index bad_line bad_lineage bad_lines bad_meta bad_path chain_broken empty_range init_failed io_error lines_mismatch log_unreadable message_required no_active_session no_session no_target read_failed rebuild_failed replay_failed session_active shadow_failed state_failed unknown_file`. (The audit also found merge's list omitting `parent_read_only`/`log_unreadable`, and amend's `branch_required`/`wrong_branch`.)
- **Two names for one thing.** `lap merge` reports a broken history as `log_broken` (`cmd_merge.c:258, 357, 373`); every other command says `history_broken`.
- **JSON fields.** `verify --deep --json` returns `deep_checked`, `deep_mismatched`, `mismatched_files`, none in the SPEC. SPEC:575 does document `ref` for sessions. (The audit's claim of a `root` field in `status --json` did not reproduce.)

**Decision (user, 2026-09-28): minimal form.** A table in the SPEC (code, commands, meaning), written by hand — no test that greps the source against it. Where two codes mean the same thing, one is kept (merge uses `history_broken`); where a code is internal-only, the table says so.

**Done when:** every code `err_out` passes appears in the table; merge emits `history_broken` (e2e updated); verify's `--deep` JSON fields listed under verify.

item.title: Usage errors list --branch where the command takes it
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced).**

```
lap commit          → error: usage: lap commit <file> (-i … | -F …) [--edit <n> | --lines <a>-<b>] [--force-message] [--no-session] [--dry-run] [--json]
                       — no --branch, which is required where branches exist
```

The audit found the same omission in the usage of amend, show and session (and session's lacking `-F`). `lap --help` itself is right (T-151).

**Decision (user, 2026-09-28): minimal form.** Fix the usage strings only. No per-command `--help`: `lap <cmd> --help` stays `unknown_flag`, whose message already points at `lap --help` (add that pointer if it is missing).

**Done when:** e2e: the usage errors of commit, amend, show and session list `--branch` (and session `-F`), matching `lap --help`; `lap commit --help`'s error names `lap --help`.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session **S169**, git `4921bb2`.

- New `branches_live_of(reg, folder)` (branches.c). It returns the first registry entry whose folder is still that branch (its `.lap/lineage` names the entry's id) and whose `.lap/parent` names `folder`, however spelled (text or `plat_same_file`). Any such entry makes the registry the folder's own; with none, it is a copy that came along with a copied folder.
- `branch start` checks this right after `already_branch`, under this folder's lock, before the parent is opened. A folder with a live branch is refused with the new code **`has_branches`**, naming the branch and its folder. So a parent cannot become a branch, least of all of its own child.
- A copied registry is still dropped as before; that is the only case that now reaches the deletion.
- SPEC's `branch start` entry lists `has_branches` and when a registry counts as a folder's own.

**Tests.** e2e 150, new scenario with the ticket's repro: main starts `oops` from its own branch → `has_branches`. Both folders' `.lap` files are byte-identical before and after (shasum), and `feat` is still listed. The existing copied-registry test still passes. Unit 4416: `branches_live_of` is live for its parent, and not for another folder, a changed lineage, or a missing `.lap/parent`.

item.title: branch start: a parent cannot become a branch of its own child, and a live registry is never deleted
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced).** A folder that has branches can start a branch from one of them. It then records to the new lineage, and its `branches.json` is deleted without a word:

```
lap init in main; commit .lapignore and a.txt; git commit
cp -R main wt; cd wt; lap branch start feat --from ../main
cd ../main; lap branch start oops --from ../wt      # the folders swapped by mistake
```

Observed: `branch oops (…) started from …/wt`, rc 0. main's `.lap/branches.json` is gone, `.lap/lineage` names oops. `lap merge feat` → "feat is this folder's own history"; `lap session start … --branch main` → "records to oops, not main".

It triggers exactly when the parent is quiet (nothing to commit), the layout the SPEC recommends.

**Cause.** `cmd_branch.c:147-156` checks only `.lap/lineage` (this folder is main, so it passes). `cmd_branch.c:346-353` deletes `branches.json` unconditionally, as if it were always a copied registry. Here its entries are live branches whose `.lap/parent` names this very folder.

**Fix.** Refuse (a new code, e.g. `has_branches`) when this folder's registry lists a branch whose folder exists and whose `.lap/parent` resolves to this folder — above all the `--from` folder itself. Drop `branches.json` only when it is a copy (its entries' parents are another folder).

**Done when:** e2e: the repro above is refused and changes nothing in either folder (tree hashes before/after); a copied registry is still dropped (existing test); unit tests for the "is this registry mine" decision.

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session **S170**, git `6b947a9`.

**What changed** (`cmd_merge.c`)
- **Merges by way of other branches.** For every merge record here (branch L, head H), `merges_by_way` reads L's history as this folder holds it, up to H. It collects L's own merge records, and recursively theirs, and puts every `from` link seen into a hashed map (copy → what it was copied from). Those merge records count as merges made here: each branch of the chain takes the furthest head any route reached, and their stops count too. So the chain starts after the last record already here by any route.
- **Transitive `from`.**
  - Sessions, session ends and amendments already here are recognised through a copy of a copy.
  - Commits: a branch commit is skipped in placement when a copy of a copy of it is here, or when what it was itself copied from is here. That covers both orders: b2→b1→main then b2, and b2→main then b1.
  - A direct copy from an interrupted run of *this* merge is still placed again, so T-125's redo is unchanged.
- The hashed map moved to `str.c` as `StrMap`; the linear `Map` would be quadratic over whole histories.
- SPEC: new paragraph "Work that came by another route".

**Tests**
- e2e 152, two new scenarios with the ticket's two orders. In each: nothing adopted twice (`once` on every behavior), `lap status` clean, the tagged session listed once, `verify --deep` clean. Against the previous `cmd_merge.c`, the first order fails exactly as the ticket reports (commit adopted twice, a pending edit, the session twice). The second order already passed there, since the old code followed one `from` level.
- Unit 4424: `StrMap` put, overwrite and growth, and a chain of copies followed through it to the original. The `from` walk itself lives in static merge code; the e2e covers it end to end.

**Not separately tested:** the audit's "spurious stops" variant, where the re-adopted commit overlaps b1's later work. It comes from the same double adoption, which no longer happens.

item.title: lap merge never adopts work twice when it reached this folder through another branch
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced).** b1 from main, b2 from b1. b2 merged into b1, b1 into main, then b2 merged straight into main: main adopts b2's commits, sessions and amendments a second time, and changes b1 made on top of them are undone.

```
b2: insert X after line 5 (session --meta ticket=T-9), git commit
b1: git merge b2; lap merge b2; delete X (commit); git commit
main: git merge b1; lap merge b1; git commit           → status clean
b2: edit g.txt (commit); git commit
main: git merge b2 (clean, no X); lap merge b2
```

Observed: "adopted 2 of 2 commits (L6, L7)" — L6 inserts X again (L4 is the same commit via b1); `lap status` shows `a.txt [1] line 6` pending; `session list --meta ticket=T-9` lists S1 and S2, both "b2 work session". A session is duplicated even when the branch had no commit in it. The audit also saw spurious stops where the re-adopted commit overlaps b1's later work, so b2's new work is never adopted.

**Cause.** main has no merge record of b2, so all of b2 counts as new; a duplicate is recognised only by a direct `from` on this side (`cmd_merge.c:440-446`, `639-644` cover only this run's interrupted redo; sessions `616-622` look at `b->from` only; amendments `664-666`; the chain start `406-422`).

**Fix.** Before adopting, collect every original hash already here, following `from` links transitively (an adopted copy of an adopted copy), and skip commits, sessions and amendments whose original is among them; start the chain after the last record already here by that route.

**Done when:** e2e for the orders b2→b1→main then b2→main, and b2→b1, b2→main, then b1: nothing adopted twice, status clean, sessions once, amendments once, `verify --deep` ok. Unit tests for the transitive `from` set.

item.title: A change made in several commits on both sides is already done, not a conflict (and a rerun finishes the merge)
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced).** T-158 recognises an identical change only when one branch commit equals the parent's whole net change to that region.

Flat: both sides do `5 → five → FIVE` as two commits each. git merges cleanly; `lap merge b` → "adopted 0 of 2 commits, stopped: a.txt at #… (it overlaps or touches a change the parent made)". Control: the branch doing `5 → FIVE` in one commit → "already done here". The file then stays stopped for good (later branch commits to it are never adopted).

The same breaks two promises built on it:
- **T-125, rerun of an interrupted merge.** Branch: the two-step edit plus a g.txt edit. `LAP_TEST_MERGE_FAIL_AFTER=2 lap merge b`, commit another file, `lap merge b` → "adopted 1 of 3 commits, stopped: a.txt" although its commits are in the log. SPEC says they "come out already done".
- **T-157, a nested branch merged by two routes** (b2→b1, b2→main, then b1): stops a.txt at b1's copy; b1 stays "partly merged". (Audit repro; same mechanism, not re-run by hand.)
- Also from the audit, confirmed only by reading: a chain merge interrupted between its two merge records reruns as "adopted 0, left 2, stopped", because the outer merge record has no `from` and `merge_redo_point` (`cmd_merge.c:76-89`) reads it as other work.

**Cause.** `adopt.c:103-121` compares one commit with the parent's net hunk (`ch[hit].len == c->old_lines`, same delta, same text).

**Fix.** Treat a run of branch commits whose combined effect on the region equals the parent's change as already done (compare the branch's text after each commit with the parent's text in that region, not the single commit's hunk); make the redo point skip this run's own merge records.

**Done when:** e2e: the flat two-step case, the rerun case and the nested two-route case end with everything "already done", no stop, status clean; unit tests in the adopt suite for multi-commit identical changes, including a partial match (only the first step identical → still a conflict).

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S171, git b73a8f2.

**What changed**
- `adopt_place` (adopt.c): when a commit overlaps exactly one parent change but is not that whole change, it now applies the branch's following commits in order while they are edits that stay inside that change's region. If after some commit the branch's text there equals the parent's text (with an acceptable final newline), that commit and every one before it in the run are marked already done, and the parent change becomes common ground (later parent changes are shifted by the region's growth). If the run leaves the region, or never reaches the parent's text, the old conflict path applies unchanged, so a partial match is still a conflict.
- `merge_redo_point(log, newer, run_branches)`: merge records whose branch is one of the run's chain ids no longer count as "other work since". A chain merge interrupted between its merge records now reruns as the uninterrupted one would.
- SPEC merge rule 3 and the note on interrupted merges, plus the adopt.h header, now say this.

**Tests**: unit 4440 passed (3 new adopt tests: a two-step change on both sides where a later commit carries on; only the first step identical, which still conflicts; a region that grows through an insertion then an edit. The redo point also has a new test for its own vs other merge records). e2e 154 passed, 0 failed. The two new scenarios are:
1. Flat `5 → five → FIVE` on both sides: dry-run shows 2 already done, 0 left, no stop; the merge adopts only g.txt; status is clean; branch is merged; verify --deep is clean. The same merge interrupted with `LAP_TEST_MERGE_FAIL_AFTER=2`, then another commit, then a rerun, ends with no stop and status clean.
2. Nested two-route (b2→b1, b2→main, then b1) with b2 doing a two-step change: b ends merged, status clean, and b2's commit is adopted once.

Checked against HEAD before this change: scenario 1 fails there (both the flat case and the rerun). The nested scenario already passes at HEAD, because T-172's "came by way" skip no longer re-places b2's commits when b1 is merged. So the nested case is covered by that fix, and this scenario now guards it. The chain-interrupted-between-merge-records case is covered by the unit test only, not by an e2e run.

item.title: A torn first line in a fresh open chunk is repaired, not taken for a broken chain
item.description:
**Verified (reproduced).** A crash during the first append after a seal (branch start, the 4 MB limit, a merge rolling chunks) leaves the new open chunk holding only a torn line. Every writer then refuses; only hand editing gets out.

```
lap init; commit; cp -R . ../b; cd ../b; lap branch start b --from ../main   # main.000002 is now empty
cd main; printf '{"type":"commit","id":"L9' >> .lap/log/main.000002.jsonl
lap verify     → chain ok: 3 records; note: torn trailing record ignored … the next commit repairs it
lap commit …   → error: main.000002.jsonl does not continue main.000001.jsonl: the hash chain is broken there
```

Control: the same torn line after complete records in a chunk is cut and the commit goes on ("repaired torn log tail").

**Cause.** `hist.c:835-851`: the chain check between chunks reads the open chunk's first record; `chunk_first_record` fails on a chunk with no complete record, and that failure is reported as a broken chain before the torn-tail repair runs.

**Fix.** In the open chunk, a chunk with no complete line is an empty chunk with a torn tail: skip the boundary check for it and let the writer truncate it under the lock.

**Done when:** e2e: the repro commits, the torn bytes are gone, `verify` ok; a torn line in a *sealed* chunk is still refused (T-131 stays green).

author: claude
body:
Done in lap session S172, git 73b6081.

**What changed**
- `chunk_first_record` (hist.c) has a new `torn` out-flag. It is set when the whole chunk was read and no newline was found.
- In `hist_check`'s chain check, if the **last (open)** chunk holds only a torn line, the check stops there instead of calling it a broken chain. The writer's existing torn-tail repair then cuts it under the lock ("repaired torn log tail"). Sealed chunks are unaffected: their ends-in-a-torn-line check runs before this and still refuses.

**Tests**: unit 4445 passed (new: an open chunk holding only a torn line passes the chain check; a sealed chunk holding only a torn line is still refused, named). e2e 155 passed, 0 failed. The new scenario: after a branch start, the parent's open chunk is empty; a torn `{"type":"commit","id":"L9` is appended; verify reports the torn record; the next parent commit succeeds; the torn bytes are gone; the chunk holds the new record; verify says chain ok.

Checked against the pre-change hist.c: the new scenario fails there (the commit is refused), and the T-131 sealed-chunk scenarios pass on both builds. I also ran the ticket's exact repro by hand (init, commit, branch start, torn append, commit): it repaired, and verify --deep was clean.
